# Modernization audit — 2026-09-09

Epic [#993](https://github.com/ray-manaloto/dotfiles/issues/993) — *whole-repo
modernization audit: retire hand-written code that Claude Code, codex and our
pinned tools now do natively*. Branch `feat/orchestration-modernization-audit`.

Machine-readable companion: `docs/research/kb/reports/modernization-audit-2026-09-09.toml`
(one `[[finding]]` per row, regenerated deterministically by
`.agent/kb/audit/aggregate.py` — **do not hand-edit it**). Its `schedule` field
is empty by design; the "Scheduling proposal" section below is the
human-readable proposal a later PR reconciles into it. **Since round 5:** every
citation repair travels *inside* that TOML as the finding's own `correction`
/ `correction_custom` field, sourced from `.agent/kb/audit/corrections.json`,
which `aggregate.py` and the report renderer both read. Rounds 2–4 kept the
repairs only in the renderer, so three consecutive critics correctly found the
TOML still shipping the uncorrected anchors with no marker at all
(`grep -c 'CITATION CORRECTED'` was 6 in the .md and **0** in the .toml). Round
6 adds three more corrections, bringing the total to **23 corrected rows**;
control arm, a bogus token against the same file with the same command shape → 0.
**New in round 6:** every *scheduled* row that carries a correction now renders a
⚠️ CONDITIONAL marker in the Scheduling table itself, because the fifth critic
found `mod-image-5` shipping an unqualified "add `--platform`" ask while a saved,
control-armed probe refuting it sat unread in `.agent/kb/raw/`. The marker is
mechanical over `corrections.json`, so it closes the class rather than that row.

**This is round 6, and FIVE completeness critics have now run — every one of
them is answered by name, in its own table.** Round 2 answered the first
critic's six gaps
([Method → Round 2](#round-2--completeness-critic-gaps-and-how-each-was-resolved)).
Round 3 answered the second critic's three
([Method → Round 3](#round-3--second-completeness-critic-and-how-each-item-was-resolved)).
Round 4 was a *verdict re-run* with no critic table of its own — and that was a
defect, because a **third** critic (`completeness-critic-round3.json`, 15:35
local) had in fact run seventeen minutes before round 4's report was rendered at
15:52, and round 4's own Method section opened by asserting that no critic had
run. Round 5 repairs that: the third critic's eight items are answered in
[Method → Round 4](#round-4--third-completeness-critic-and-the-verdict-re-run),
the **fourth** critic's nine
(`completeness-critic-round4.json`, 16:01) in
[Method → Round 5](#round-5--fourth-completeness-critic-and-how-each-item-was-resolved),
and the **fifth** critic's three (`completeness-critic-round5.json`, 16:49) in
[Method → Round 6](#round-6--fifth-completeness-critic-and-how-each-item-was-resolved).
Round 6 accepted all three in full — the first round in this audit where nothing
a critic said was refuted or revised downward — and two of the three were the
same defect: **an artifact this audit itself produced was on disk, unread, and
materially changed a scheduled ask.** A third, `deps:python`, exposes a worse
shape: a repair claimed as done in round 2 and carried unre-verified through
rounds 3, 4 and 5.
**Seven of the third critic's eight items were open and undisclosed in the round-4
text; six are repaired here and one is accepted-and-deferred with its measurement
published** (the `skills-2` second root — see Round 4, item 2). The report's
credibility argument is *"every critic item is answered by name, none is
dismissed"*; in round 4 that argument was false as written, and saying so is
part of repairing it.

The five highest-value retirements — chosen for surface removed and for
blast-radius reduction, not for confidence score alone:

1. **`mod-ai-3` — delete the whole `dotfiles_setup.ai` module and the
   `dotfiles-setup ai-setup` CLI subcommand.** Its two capabilities are native:
   AI-CLI presence is `mise which` / `mise ls --missing`, and post-install
   configuration is a tool-level `postinstall` hook. It is also completely
   unwired — a repo-wide `grep -rn "ai-setup"` returns 6 hits, 3 of them the
   subcommand's own registration in `main.py` and 3 in historical planning
   docs. No mise task, no hk step, no settings hook, no workflow, no suites
   contract, no test. `python/src/dotfiles_setup/ai.py:13-42`.

2. **`mod-docker-1` (with `mod-docker-2/3/4/5`) — retire `DevContainerManager`'s
   re-implementation of the devcontainer lifecycle.** `build()` pulls the ~38GB
   published base with a **classic** `docker pull`
   (`python/src/dotfiles_setup/docker.py:333-355`) — the exact call this repo's
   own `mise-tasks-only.md:15` and `verify-before-advancing.md:65,78` say wedges
   and must be a BuildKit `--output type=docker` re-export via `mise run sync`.
   `up()` passes no `--id-label`, `test()` shells a hand-composed `bash -lc`
   string, `down()` re-implements teardown, and two class constants still name a
   dead local image. A control-armed grep for live wiring
   (`dotfiles-setup docker (build|up|test|down)`) returns **0** hits while the
   same shape for `initialize-host|sync` returns three.

3. **`mod-audit-1` — delete `ToolManager.sync_versions()`, a regex tool-version
   bumper that is a provable no-op.** Re-running the module's own two regexes
   against its only target file yields **0** numeric-version matches while the
   identically-shaped `"latest"` arm yields **28** — every overlay tool in
   `home/dot_config/mise/config.toml.tmpl` is deliberately pinned to `latest`,
   so the bumper can never match anything it exists to bump. Native:
   `mise upgrade --bump`, `mise outdated --bump`, `mise lock --bump`, plus
   Renovate's native mise manager via the already-adopted
   `github>jdx/renovate-config` preset. `python/src/dotfiles_setup/audit.py:95-153`.

4. **`hk-steps-1-2` and `hk-steps-1-3` — drop two `batch` overrides that hk
   1.57.0's own builtins have superseded.** The `gitleaks` override carries a
   15-line comment describing a quirk upstream has since fixed (the builtin now
   hardcodes the single path `.`, citing the same gitleaks 8.30.1 source line
   the repo measured), and the `shellcheck` override in `hk-image.pkl:40-45`
   merely restates the builtin's own default — the project config already
   deleted the identical line at `hk.pkl:188-195`. Control arm: the same read
   over `typos.pkl`, `python_check_ast.pkl`, `gitleaks.pkl` and
   `trailing_whitespace.pkl` finds no `batch = true`, so shellcheck genuinely is
   the one builtin that ships it — which is also why the repo's `batch = true`
   on `typos` is **not** redundant. (Both rows were re-derived from scratch by
   the round-2 re-run of `hk-steps-1` and came back at the same ids, the same
   dispositions and 0/3 refuted.)

5. **`skills-1-2` (round-2 id: `skills-1-1`) — delete the vendored
   `.claude/skills/find-docs/SKILL.md` and its `.agents/skills/find-docs/`
   twin.** It is a second ctx7 skill duplicating
   `.claude/skills/context7-cli/SKILL.md`, it instructs
   `npm install -g ctx7@latest` / `npx ctx7@latest` against a mise-pinned binary
   (`mise.toml:49`), and it claims doc-lookup primacy ("Always use for…",
   "Prefer this over web search") in direct conflict with
   `.claude/rules/research-doc-sources.md`'s step-00-first chain. It has the
   largest `description` in `.claude/skills/` — **856 characters raw, 830
   whitespace-normalised**, re-measured for this report against the finder's
   stated 827; all three numbers are far under the 1,536-char skill-listing
   truncation cliff, so this is a budget-and-matcher-competition claim, not a
   truncation claim. Claude Code 2.1.261's `/skill-doctor` is the native
   measurement of what each loaded skill costs, and `skillOverrides: {"find-docs":
   "off"}` removes it from context immediately if deletion needs a review cycle.

## Method

**Units (121).** The repo was partitioned into audit units of one of eight
kinds: `module` (78 units — one per `python/src/dotfiles_setup/*.py`), `rule`
(26 units — one per `.claude/rules/*.md`), `hk` (4 units — `hk.pkl`,
`hk-common.pkl`, `hk-image.pkl` steps, split by size), `mise` (4 units —
`mise.toml` tasks, split by size), `suites` (4 units —
`python/verification/suites.toml`, split by size), `skills` (3 units —
`.claude/skills/**/SKILL.md`), `agents` (1 unit — `.claude/agents/**`), and
`scripts` (1 unit — `scripts/*.sh` + `.devcontainer/scripts/*.sh`). The
group-unit split points are recorded in `.agent/kb/audit/args-run3.json`
(`groups`). Every one of the 121 appears in the Coverage table below.

**Unit-membership completeness (round 2, CORRECTED in round 3).** The Coverage
table proves every *unit slug* was audited; it says nothing about whether each
group unit's *member list* covered everything on disk, and round 1 never
published those member lists. That is exactly where the two uncovered units hid.

⚠️ **Round 2's version of this table was itself a probe with one face for two of
the eight kinds, and the second critic was right.** The `skills` and `agents`
probes were `ls .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md | wc -l` and
`ls .claude/agents/*.md | wc -l` — *scoped to the same directory the member list
came from*, so they could not have disagreed no matter what was on disk
(`.claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md` rule 3, "bound-limited searches
are suspect by construction"). The rows below now carry the **unscoped** arm,
and it disagrees. The `ls` counts are kept in the table as the *scoped* column
so the defect is legible rather than erased.

| kind | members declared (`args-run3.json`) | scoped count | UNSCOPED arm (`git ls-files`, no root) | agree? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| module | 78 | 78 | `git ls-files 'python/src/dotfiles_setup/*.py' \| wc -l` → **78** | ✅ |
| rule | 26 | 26 | `git ls-files '.claude/rules/*.md' \| wc -l` → **26**; no second rules root exists (`git ls-files '.codex/rules/*' \| wc -l` → **0**, control arm `.claude/rules` → 26) | ✅ |
| suites | 38+38+38+38 = **152** | 152 | `grep -c '^\[\[suite\]\]' python/verification/suites.toml` → **152**; single file, no root question | ✅ |
| skills | 11+11+11 = **33** | 33 | `git ls-files '*/SKILL.md' \| wc -l` → **76** across **four** roots: `.agents/skills` 35, `.claude/skills` 33, `plugins/dotfiles-build-optimizer/skills` 7, `.codex/skills` 1. (Only the plugin root has a pre-existing exclusion the repo already states — `.claude/rules/zero-bash-logic.md` puts `plugins/**` out of scope as vendored/third-party — though `dotfiles-build-optimizer` is in fact first-party. The other two roots have no stated exclusion at all.) | ❌ → **conceded**; see Round 3 below |
| agents | 9 | 9 | `git ls-files '*/agents/*.md'` has exactly one non-`docs/` root, `.claude/agents` → **9**, so the `.md` half is complete. But the unit's real membership is not `.md`-shaped: `.codex/agents/` holds **9 `.toml`** role definitions on disk that no `*.md` probe can see — **5 tracked** (`git ls-files '.codex/agents/*.toml' \| wc -l` → 5) and **4 gitignored** (`git status --porcelain --ignored .codex/agents/` → 4 `!!` lines: `adversarial-critic`, `claude-code-expert`, `dockerfile-reviewer`, `staleness-auditor` — the Codex-Desktop-written mirrors `agents-12` describes) | ❌ → **partially conceded**; see Round 3 below |
| scripts | 11 | 11 | `git ls-files 'scripts/*.sh' '.devcontainer/scripts/*.sh' \| wc -l` → **11**; unscoped `git ls-files '*.sh' \| wc -l` finds no third `.sh` root outside `home/` chezmoi templates | ✅ |
| mise | 22+22+22+20 = 86 slots, **86 distinct** | **87** | `grep -c '^\[tasks\.' mise.toml` | ❌ → fixed in round 2, see below |
| hk | 17+17+17+14 = 65 slots, **64 distinct** (`shellcheck` deliberately audited twice: once in `hk.pkl`, once in `hk-image.pkl`) | **65** distinct step keys per the critic's extraction | see below | ❌ → fixed in round 2, see below |

**So: six of eight kinds agree under an unscoped arm; two do not, and both
disagreements are the same defect in the same direction — a second live root the
member list never saw.** Neither is repaired by re-running a finder over the
same 33/9 members; what round 3 did instead was make the second root a
*subject of a finding* (`skills-1-7`, `agents-12`), which is the only honest
close available inside a report that cannot itself widen the unit list.

The two round-2 disagreements (`mise`, `hk`) are a different failure mode — a
**character class in a splitting regex**, not a root-scope miss, and not a
judgement call:

**Survival rule.** A `retire` or `refactor` finding **survives** when it has
**>=2 lens verdicts and fewer than 2 of them refuted**. `keep` and `unknown`
findings are not voted on and are reported as raised. `unverified_contested`
is **0**, so no surviving row is surviving merely because nobody looked at it.
All 121 units have all three verdict files; **one finding**
(`rule-verify-before-advancing-5`) received only two lens verdicts —
`coverage` and `currency` returned an entry for it, `risk` did not — and it
survives on 0/2, which the rule permits. It is the only 2-verdict contested row
in the run (the other 426 of 427 have 3).

**Minority dissent is reported, not averaged away.** 107 surviving contested
rows carry exactly one refuting lens (**4** retire + **103** refactor —
re-derived for round 5; the `skills-3` re-run moved one row from the refactor
side to the retire side, so round 4's "3 retire + 104 refactor" no longer holds).
The `votes refuted/total` column shows this on every row. For the four **retire**
rows (`mise-tasks-4-4`, `mod-gcc_sha-4`, `skills-3-2`, `suites-2-4`) the
dissenting reason is reproduced verbatim immediately after the retire table,
because retire is the disposition a reader acts on first. The 103 refactor
dissents are in `.agent/kb/audit/aggregate.json` under each row's
`verdict_reasons` (they are not carried into the TOML).

checker being wrong, not the report. That is `probes-need-a-control-arm.md`
rule 7 applied to my own sweep. **Four of the nine were reported by no critic**
(`hk-steps-1-2`, `hk-steps-1-5`, `mod-ask_quality-1`, `mod-parity-3`), one of
them on a surviving `retire` row.

### The corpus moved under the audit — and it invalidated a verified correction

⚠️ **This is the report's own worked example of why an anchor into an
unversioned, re-fetched corpus decays, and it is worse than the digest
inversion because nothing flagged it.** Two earlier rounds verified that
`mod-graphify-2`'s 0.9.51 shrink-guard bullet sits at `sources/graphify/CHANGELOG.md:40`
(round 2 corrected `:37` → `:40`; the third critic independently re-confirmed
`:37` is blank and `:40` is the bullet). **Both are now wrong.** Re-probed for
round 5 against the bytes on disk right now: the file has an mtime of
**2026-09-09 15:40 local** — *after* round 3's render (15:24) and *before* round
4's (15:52) — runs to **1,996 lines**, and carries `## 0.9.56 (2026-09-07)` and
`## 0.9.57 (unreleased)` sections that did not exist when the finder ran. The
0.9.51 heading is at `:87` and its bullet at `:89`; the 0.9.53 bullet is at `:65`.

Control arm: `grep -n '^## 0\.9\.5' CHANGELOG.md` returns **9** real section
headings and a freshly-invented bogus token returns **0**, so the probe
discriminates. The quoted sentences are present verbatim at every round, so the
**claim has always stood on substance — only the pointers moved, twice.**

Scale: `find <corpus> -type f -newermt '2026-09-09 15:00'` → **171 files**
rewritten mid-audit (control arm `-newermt '2027-01-01'` → **0**). The KB corpus
has no per-file version stamp this report can read, so the honest statement is
that **no corpus anchor in this report is guaranteed to point at the bytes its
finder read**, and a corpus anchor that matters should be re-probed by content
(`grep -n '<the quoted sentence>'`) rather than followed by line number. That is
the durable lesson, and it is bigger than any single row: *line numbers into a
living corpus are a caching bug waiting to happen; the quoted sentence is the
real citation.*

Secondary consequence worth flagging for the `#997` bucket: the corpus now
documents **0.9.56 and 0.9.57** directly, which means the
`graphify-readme-0.9.56` gap fetch (recorded above as "the fetched `main` README
is OLDER than the offline baseline") is no longer the best available source for
that refresh — the corpus CHANGELOG is. Re-read it before scoping #997.

verbatim below and preserved at `.agent/kb/audit/round4-lost-verdicts.md`.
**Do not act on `mise-tasks-1-8` without re-running its probe**; the anchored
`grep -E "^${_stem}"` is load-bearing for cross-clone volume isolation.

#### The erased round-3 refutation of `mise-tasks-1-8`, verbatim

- **Claim:** [tasks.ps] is inline shell: three separate `dotfiles-setup devcontainer name ...` subprocesses, a `${_stem%-home}` suffix strip, an escaped Go-template `docker ps --format` string, and `docker volume ls --format '{{.Name}}' | grep -E "^${_stem}" || true`
- **Claimed native alternative:** docker's own server-side name filter — `docker volume ls --filter name=<stem>` — instead of piping a full listing through `grep`; and, for the rest, the repo's one-line-task-over-a-python-module pattern (`dotfiles-setup devcontainer ...`) already used by `names`/`ssh-port`
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** Live control-armed probe on this host refutes the native_alternative's implicit coverage claim: `docker volume create abc-zzqfrp9-suffix` and `docker volume create zzqfrp9-prefix`, then `docker volume ls --filter name=zzqfrp9 --format '{{.Name}}'` returned BOTH volumes — proving Docker's `name=` filter does unanchored SUBSTRING matching, not the prefix-anchored match `grep -E "^${_stem}"` performs (control arm: a bogus filter key `bogusfilterkey=` correctly errored 'invalid filter', so the probe discriminates real filters from fake ones). Swapping in `--filter name=<stem>` would therefore return a broader result set than today's script (any volume merely containing the stem substring anywhere, not just those with it as a prefix) — a real, undisclosed behavioral difference, i.e. a partial cover with no stated migration path. The finding also explicitly concedes it has no doc citation for this claim ('the docker filter flag is asserted from `docker volume ls --help` on this host and is NOT in the offline corpus — see probe'), which by this audit's own hard rule 4 should force disposition='unknown' with the settling probe, not 'refactor' at confidence 0.45. Separately, the rationale misattributes the `|| true` correctness note to `.claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md` / hk's `no_grep_q_under_pipefail` step — that step (hk.pkl:232-234) specifically targets `| *grep -q` (grep's `-q` flag causing an early-exit SIGPIPE that returns 141 WHEN THE MATCH SUCCEEDS); the actual code at mise.toml:439 uses plain `grep -E` with no `-q`, so its `|| true` is defending against the unrelated, mundane case of grep's ordinary exit-1-on-no-match under `set -e` — a different failure mode than the one that rule/step polices, so the citation does not say what is claimed.
  - Evidence: live docker probe (this session): `docker volume ls --filter name=zzqfrp9` matched both a prefix and a substring-suffix volume, control arm with an invalid filter key correctly rejected; mise.toml:439 (`grep -E "^${_stem}"`, no `-q`); hk.pkl:232-234 (`no_grep_q_under_pipefail` glob + check text, keyed specifically to `| *grep -q`)
- **Refuted by `risk`:** Live-probed the proposed native_alternative on this host: `docker volume ls --filter name=<substring>` matches the substring ANYWHERE in the volume name, not just as a prefix -- e.g. filtering on the middle fragment `amd64-home` returned 12 unrelated volumes across many different clones/branches, not just the one whose stem starts with it. The current code's `grep -E "^${_stem}"` is an ANCHORED prefix match, chosen deliberately per its own comment ('Scoped to this clone's hashed volumes') to avoid exactly the cross-clone false-positive this task exists to prevent (its whole purpose is one clone/arch's volume set). Swapping to the literal `--filter name=` form as described silently drops that anchoring invariant -- it would show OTHER clones' orphaned volumes whenever their hashed stem happens to contain this clone's stem as a substring -- and the finding names no replacement for the anchor semantics (docker's `--filter name=` has no documented anchor/regex mode). The finding's own confidence (0.45) and its 'the docker filter flag is asserted on this host and is NOT in the offline corpus -- see probe' caveat already flagged the exact gap this probe confirms; under the RISK lens that gap is enough to refute the native_alternative AS WRITTEN, even though the surrounding refactor (dedupe the 3 name-resolution subprocess calls, fix `\|\| true` swallowing docker errors) is still sound.
  - Evidence: Live probe on this host (bypass-permissions Bash, read-only docker CLI): `docker volume ls --filter name=amd64-home --format '{{.Name}}'` returned 12 rows across `dotfiles-checkout-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-codex-task-orchestration-v2-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-goal-history-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-issue-753-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-issue-763-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-pr671-*`, `dotfiles-dotfiles-rmanaloto-*`, and five separate `dotfiles-repo-rmanaloto-*` volumes -- a middle-fragment substring match, not an anchored one; control arm `docker volume ls --filter name=checkout-rmanaloto` returned exactly the one matching volume, confirming the filter discriminates by substring position, not by anchor. Current code: mise.toml:439 (`grep -E "^${_stem}"`) with its rationale at mise.toml:432-438 ('Scoped to this clone's hashed volumes'). docker CLI has no documented anchored-name filter (`docker volume ls --help` on this host lists only `-f, --filter filter` with no anchor/regex option), so there is no named 1:1 native replacement for the anchor.

#### Item 1 in full: `mise-tasks-1-11`, and why it is `unknown` rather than `retire`

`[tasks."deps:python"]` (mise.toml:196-201) turns out to be a **field-for-field
re-declaration of mise's built-in `uv` dependency provider**, and the repo already
declares that provider 188 lines above it:

| | `[tasks."deps:python"]` (mise.toml:196-201) | mise built-in `uv` provider (`deps.md:68`) | `[deps.uv]` as declared (mise.toml:5-8) |
|---|---|---|---|
| dir | `python` | — | `python` |
| sources | `["pyproject.toml", "uv.lock"]` | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | (not set) |
| outputs | `[".venv/"]` | `.venv/` | (not set) |
| run | `uv sync` | `uv sync` | `uv sync --locked` |

`[deps.uv] auto = true` means the provider runs **before every `mise run` and
every `mise x`** (`deps.md:158`, `:236-240`), and below that `uv run` itself
"locks and synced before invoking the requested command"
(`uv/docs/concepts/projects/sync.md:9-11`) — which is the form every other task
in this file uses. Liveness, control-armed: an unscoped grep for `deps:python`
across the tree returns exactly **two** hits, its own definition and a quoted
string in a test fixture (`tests/test_handoff_check.py:205`) — no `depends`, no
python caller, no workflow step, no row in `.claude/rules/mise-tasks-only.md`'s
canonical task map. Control arm, same command shape: `run dev-rebuild` → 5 hits.

**Two things a lens should test that make this more than a tidy-up.** First, the
task's `run = "uv sync"` is the **unlocked** spelling, and this repo maintains a
gate whose entire purpose is to force the locked one —
`python/src/dotfiles_setup/dependency_ownership.py:85-91` asserts
`uv_provider.get("run") == "uv sync --locked"`, error text at `:109`. That gate
reads `mise_values["deps"]["uv"]` only, so it **cannot see this task**:

forbids one layer up, invisible to the gate. Second, `[deps.uv]` carries no
`sources`/`outputs`, so if anything here is worth keeping it is those two keys
moved **onto the provider**, not a second task.

**Why it is filed `unknown`.** It is retire-shaped and cited to the line on both
sides. It is nonetheless `unknown` because it was authored by the **synthesis**
stage, not by a finder, and **no verification lens has ever voted on it**. Filing
it `retire` would have entered the run's first `contested_unverified` row and
would have sat under "Refuted" (where the renderer puts every non-surviving
contested row) despite nothing having refuted it — or, worse, been read as
confirmed. `unknown` publishes the whole claim, keeps the probe attached, and
cannot inflate the survived-retire count. The row is
[`mise-tasks-1-11`](#unknown--probes-to-run); its provenance is stamped in the
finding JSON itself (`"authored": "synthesis-round6 …"`).

#### `mod-devcontainer_names-1` — mod-devcontainer_names — refactor, conf 0.7, 1/3 refuted

- **Native-side correction:** **⚠ THE STRONGER EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW WAS ON DISK AND UNCITED THROUGH ROUNDS 1-5 (added round 6), AND IT CARRIES A CAVEAT THAT WOULD SINK A NAIVE IMPLEMENTATION.** The `alternative_evidence` above proves the passthrough by INFERENCE FROM OBSERVED USAGE (".devcontainer/devcontainer.json:103 already ships `\"options\": [\"--tag=...\", \"--platform=...\"]`"). A source-level proof of the same fact, read from the EXACT pinned install, was already saved: `.agent/kb/raw/devcontainers-cli-089-build-options-label-probe.md` (2026-09-09 11:24), reading `~/.local/share/mise/installs/npm-devcontainers-cli/0.89.0/node_modules/@devcontainers/cli/dist/spec-node/devContainersSpecCLI.js`. At **line 470** of that bundle: `let D=(N=s.build)==null?void 0:N.options;D!=null&&D.length&&l.push(...D),l.push(...c),l.push(await QI(xG(n,s),n));` — `s` is the resolved devcontainer.json config and `l` is the exact arg array handed to `docker build`/`docker buildx build`, on the single-Dockerfile path (`IW`, called from `Sp`) this repo uses. So `build.options` is a genuine raw docker-CLI-flag passthrough, not a fixed allowlist, and `--label=dotfiles.workspace=<hash>` would reach `docker build` identically (probe :5-18). **THE CAVEAT, which appears nowhere else in this report:** the CLI ALSO has a first-class `additionalLabels` → `--label` mechanism (`...e.additionalLabels.length>0?e.additionalLabels.map(f=>["--label",f]).flat():[]...` in `FQ`), but it is populated ONLY by the standalone `devcontainer build` subcommand's own `--label` flag — **every other call site, `devcontainer up` included, hardcodes `additionalLabels:[]`** (probe :20-36). Since `mise.toml [tasks.up]` drives `devcontainer up`, the native label path is UNREACHABLE from this repo's invocation and `build.options` is the only route. An implementer who reads "the CLI has a --label flag, use that instead" will wire a mechanism that silently does nothing. The live host arms in the older `docker-cli-label-filter-probe.md` remain valid and are unaffected.

### Surviving retire rows with a dissenting lens

4 of the 33 surviving retire rows carry exactly one refuting lens. The survival rule keeps them (>=2 verdicts, <2 refuted), but a `retire` is the disposition a reader acts on first, so the dissent is reproduced verbatim rather than averaged away. Treat each of these as conditional on running its own probe. (103 surviving `refactor` rows also carry one dissent — among them `mise-tasks-1-8`, which crossed the survival threshold on a round-4 verdict re-run and carries an inline warning in its own row; the `votes refuted/total` column marks them and the reasons are in `.agent/kb/audit/aggregate.json` under each row's `verdict_reasons`.)

#### `skills-3-2` — skills-3 — retire, conf 0.8, 1/3 refuted

- **Claim:** `tmux-extended-keys` skill: 135 lines carrying the tmux CSI-u recipe for Shift+Enter, plus the claim that Claude Code's `/terminal-setup` is "misdirection" / "a red herring" inside tmux.
- **Claimed native alternative:** The vendor now documents this exact procedure in the Claude Code terminal-config page, under a `## Configure tmux` heading, with a superset of the skill's config block and a corrected account of `/terminal-setup`.
- **Dissenting lens `coverage`:** Disposition is 'retire' (full elimination, at most a one-line pointer), but terminal-config.md's Configure-tmux section does NOT cover everything the skill provides: it has no tmux minimum-version gating (3.2+ for extended-keys, 3.3+ for the extkeys terminal-feature name — verified absent from terminal-config.md by grep), no verification commands (tmux show-options), and no chezmoi-template gotcha — all real, non-redundant content this repo's own tmux usage depends on (mise.toml:1367 shows a `mise run cc` task that roots Claude Code in tmux, so the feature is not hypothetical here). A 'retire' disposition requires full coverage under this lens; a stated-but-vague migration path ('at most a one-line pointer... wherever') does not rescue a disposition that discards the version-gating fact. Separately, the rationale's loudest claim — 'the doc says /terminal-setup is not misdirection' — overstates what line 42 actually says (it only states tmux config is additionally required even when the outer terminal supports it; it does not characterize the skill's framing as wrong, and is in fact consistent with it).
  - Evidence: terminal-config.md:116-127 (verified verbatim: 'allow-passthrough'/'extended-keys'/'terminal-features' block, no version-gating or verify-step content) vs .claude/skills/tmux-extended-keys/SKILL.md:67-73,86-88 (tmux show-options verify steps + 3.2/3.3 version gotcha — present in skill, absent natively); terminal-config.md:42 (verbatim quote matches finding's citation but does not say what the finding's rationale claims, i.e. does not call the skill 'wrong'); mise.toml:1367-1383 (repo's own tmux-rooted `cc` task, showing the feature is live here, not residual).

#### `suites-2-4` — suites-2 — retire, conf 0.6, 1/3 refuted

- **Claim:** ci.no-mise-data-in-cache-map — a `regex_forbid` of the literal `"mise-data"` in .github/workflows/ci.yml, described as 'mise-data must not be in buildkit-cache-dance cache-map'.
- **Claimed native alternative:** None needed — the invariant is already fully covered by the sibling suite ci.no-actions-cache-workaround. A `cache-map` is an input to the `buildkit-cache-dance` action and cannot exist in a workflow that never invokes it, so forbidding the action subsumes forbidding one of its map keys.
- **Dissenting lens `coverage`:** The claimed subsumption is not complete. ci.no-actions-cache-workaround's forbidden-token set is narrow -- literally 'actions/cache/restore', 'actions/cache/save', 'buildkit-cache-dance' (re-read verbatim at :642-649) -- and does not forbid a bare 'actions/cache@v4' invocation, nor any hand-rolled 'run:' shell step inside ci.yml (e.g. a raw `docker buildx build --cache-to type=local,dest=/tmp/mise-data ...` or an id/path literally named mise-data) that reintroduces the literal string 'mise-data' in ci.yml without using either forbidden action name. ci.no-mise-data-in-cache-map's pattern is a plain regex_forbid on the raw substring '"mise-data"' anywhere in ci.yml (:628), which DOES catch that hand-rolled case -- so the two contracts are not strictly nested, and retiring the narrower one drops real coverage the wider one still provides. The finding's own text concedes this ('if the intent is to also block a hand-rolled cache map with no action involved... flagged for the operator's call, not a unilateral delete') without proposing an actual migration -- it defers the decision rather than closing the gap, and ships confidence 0.6, the lowest in the unit. Per this lens, a partial cover with no stated migration path is refuted.
  - Evidence: python/verification/suites.toml:621-628 (ci.no-mise-data-in-cache-map, re-read verbatim: file-wide regex_forbid on the bare quoted substring, scoped only to .github/workflows/ci.yml, no dependency on any action name); python/verification/suites.toml:642-649 (ci.no-actions-cache-workaround, re-read verbatim: forbidden tokens are exactly 'actions/cache/restore', 'actions/cache/save', 'buildkit-cache-dance' -- no bare 'actions/cache' entry); control arm re-run: `grep -c 'actions/cache' .github/workflows/*.yml .github/actions/*/action.yml` -> 0 hits repo-wide today (confirming the gap is currently latent, not already exploited, which is consistent with a real-but-unexercised coverage hole rather than a false claim); .agent/kb/raw/suites-2-native-probes.md §P4 control arm re-verified (grep -c 'ci-gate' -> 5, proving the corpus is greppable and the 0-count for mise-data/buildkit-cache-dance is a real absence).
- **Probe that settles it:** `grep -n 'buildkit-cache-dance\|cache-map\|"mise-data"' .github/workflows/*.yml .github/actions/*/action.yml`

#### `mise-tasks-4-4` — mise-tasks-4 — retire, conf 0.55, 1/3 refuted

- **Claim:** `[tasks.skillopt-provenance-check]` — 'Verify SkillOpt GitHub objects and three present-day hostile replays'. It has no caller anywhere in the repo outside its own definition.
- **Claimed native alternative:** None needed — the module the task fronts is already exercised on a live path: `tests/test_skillopt_provenance.py` runs in CI's `contract-preflight` pytest step (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:186` names `skillopt_provenance` among the merge-base-resolving tests that require `fetch-depth: 0`), and its coverage is catalogued at `tests/TEST-INDEX.md:78`.
- **Dissenting lens `coverage`:** The finding's disposition rests entirely on the claim 'the module the task fronts is already exercised on a live path' via `pytest tests/ -q` in CI. I read tests/test_skillopt_provenance.py in full (174 lines, all 8 tests): every single call to `verify_live(...)` passes an explicit FAKE fetch function (`_fetch()` at line 29, or the `wrong` closure at line 111) that returns canned JSON computed from local `git show` — never the module's real default, `github_fetch` (skillopt_provenance.py:165-180, which shells `fnox gh api ...` against the live GitHub API). The one place `github_fetch` itself is invoked directly (test_api_failure_is_bounded_without_body_or_secret, line ~135) monkeypatches `subject.subprocess.run` to fail synthetically, so it never reaches the network either. `main()`'s bare invocation (mise.toml:1518-1520 / `python -m dotfiles_setup.skillopt_provenance`) calls `verify_local(repo)` then `verify_live()` with NO argument, i.e. the real `github_fetch` default — the one genuine 'present-day' check the task's description promises ('Verify SkillOpt GitHub objects... present-day'). So the CI pytest path verifies the LOCAL tamper-detection logic and the verify_live control flow against fixtures, but never the live-object-still-matches-on-GitHub-today behavior the task exists to run. The claim of full coverage via pytest is false as stated; the finding's own rationale flags this exact doubt ('the pytest path may exercise differently from a bare python -m run') but the disposition still asserts 'None needed' in native_alternative rather than reflecting that gap.
  - Evidence: tests/test_skillopt_provenance.py:29-53 (`_fetch()` fake, used at line 67 `subject.verify_live(_fetch())`), :111-121 (`wrong` closure, also fake, at :121 `subject.verify_live(wrong)`), :124-138 (`test_api_failure_is_bounded_without_body_or_secret` monkeypatches `subject.subprocess.run`); python/src/dotfiles_setup/skillopt_provenance.py:165-180 (`github_fetch` — the real, live `fnox gh api` caller) and :196 (`def verify_live(fetch: Callable[...] = github_fetch)` — real default) and :379-397 (`main()` calls bare `verify_live()` with no override, i.e. the real live fetch, when invoked as the mise task/`python -m` entrypoint).
- **Probe that settles it:** `uv run --project python pytest tests/test_skillopt_provenance.py -q  # then compare its assertions against `python -m dotfiles_setup.skillopt_provenance` (main at skillopt_provenance.py:~380-400): if the test path covers every replay the module's __main__ runs, retire the task; if it does not, wire the task into a rule/skill instead.`

#### `mod-gcc_sha-4` — mod-gcc_sha — retire, conf 0.55, 1/3 refuted

- **Claim:** A `--check` mode: `gcc_sha_main(..., check=True)` downloads the ~480 MB .deb, compares without writing, logs a drift warning and returns rc=1 so 'a caller can gate on it'.
- **Claimed native alternative:** The build's own coreutils gate already is the drift check: `echo "${GCC_LATEST_DEB_SHA256}  ${GCC_LATEST_DEB}" | sha256sum -c -` runs in the same RUN that downloads the .deb and fails the image build loudly on any mismatch — contracted so it cannot be removed. The repair path additionally reports drift structurally via `RepairResult.changed` in its JSON line, so nothing needs a separate non-writing mode.
- **Dissenting lens `coverage`:** Confirmed the wiring facts as stated: .devcontainer/Dockerfile:579 (ARG GCC_LATEST_DEB_SHA256=) and :611 (`sha256sum -c -`) exist verbatim; python/verification/suites.toml:350-359 (build.gcc-latest-deb-checksum) binds both tokens per_path_tokens; .github/workflows/gcc-sha-repair.yml:80 runs the bare `dotfiles-setup gcc-sha` (no --check); tests/test_gcc_sha.py:164 is the only check=True call site; and a repo-wide grep for `gcc-sha`/`gcc_sha` across mise.toml, hk*.pkl, .claude/settings.json, image-analysis.yml returns nothing -- control-armed against the same grep shape finding real wiring for apt-pins (mise.toml:806,826; suites.toml:1911-1928), so the negative is a real absence, not a blind probe. All of that supports 'currently uncalled', which is not in dispute. What is refuted is the COVERAGE claim: the cited 'native_alternative' (the Dockerfile's sha256sum -c gate) does not cover the behavior --check actually provides -- a cheap, standalone, non-mutating drift check (download+hash only, no image build) that returns a distinguishing exit code for a caller to gate on. The Dockerfile gate only fires as a side effect of a full image build (~30min-2.5h per feedback_ci_build_duration_baseline / this repo's own CI-duration figures), which is not an equivalent-cost substitute for a lightweight standalone check, and it cannot be invoked without building the whole image. The finding's own rationale concedes this: it offers TWO incompatible outcomes ('delete' vs 'wire it into a scheduled workflow (image-analysis.yml)') rather than a single stated migration path, and the second option is explicitly to KEEP the check-mode code and give it a caller -- which contradicts disposition=retire. A finding that cannot commit to what the native path actually replaces, for a capability (non-mutating standalone drift signal) the native path structurally cannot provide at the same cost, is a partial cover with no committed migration path -- refuted per the lens's own rule.
  - Evidence: python/src/dotfiles_setup/gcc_sha.py:228-240 (check semantics: no write, rc=1 on drift) vs .devcontainer/Dockerfile:611 (drift only detected inside a full multi-stage image build) and python/verification/suites.toml:350-359 (contract binds the build-time gate, not a standalone check); rationale's own hedge between 'retire' and 'wire it into image-analysis.yml' is the disposition's internal admission of non-equivalence.

## Refuted

26 findings failed the survival rule (>=2 of the 3 lenses refuted). The refuting lenses' reasons are reproduced verbatim, so the claim can be re-litigated on its evidence rather than on the vote count.

### `hk-steps-2-1` — hk-steps-2 — claimed **refactor** (3/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** `docker_bake_check` (hk.pkl:134-138) is named for docker-bake.hcl but never reads it, and its command duplicates `devcontainer_json_validate`'s layer 2 verbatim.
- **Claimed native alternative:** Delete the duplicated `devcontainer read-configuration` invocation (it is already covered by `devcontainer_json_validate`) and validate the bake file with a real bake-aware tool: hk 1.57 ships an HCL builtin, `Builtins.hclfmt`, whose selector already covers docker-bake.hcl.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** The finding's named 'real bake-aware tool' (hk 1.57's Builtins.hclfmt) requires the `hclfmt` binary, and this exact repo already investigated and rejected that path IN THE SAME FILE the finding cites: hk.pkl's own '--- HCL ---' comment states hclfmt is not in the mise registry and therefore 'can't satisfy ci-local-parity' (.claude/rules/ci-local-parity.md Rule 2: every hk tool must be in the repo mise config). Confirmed live: `mise registry | grep -i hcl` returns only `hcl2json` and `hcloud` — no `hclfmt` entry (control arm: hcl2json IS present, proving the registry lookup discriminates, not just empty-by-accident). The finding never checked this ~290-line-distant comment in the very config it was auditing, so its proposed native alternative is not adoptable under the repo's own tooling policy. The duplicate-devcontainer-recheck half of the finding (evidence for scripts/validate-devcontainer-json.sh layers 1-3, ensure-docker-up.sh comment naming both callers) is independently verified true, but a finding whose stated fix cannot be applied fails the coverage lens as a whole.
  - Evidence: hk.pkl:422-426 ("#154: no hclfmt step — `hclfmt` is not in the mise registry (only hcl2json/hcloud), so it can't satisfy ci-local-parity."); live probe `mise registry 2>/dev/null | grep -i hcl` -> `hcl2json ...` / `hcloud ...`, hclfmt absent (rc=1 on a direct grep -i hclfmt); .claude/rules/ci-local-parity.md Rule 2 ("verify the tool binary is listed in the repo's merged mise config").
- **Refuted by `currency`:** The proposed native alternative (hk's `Builtins.hclfmt`) wraps the `hclfmt` CLI, which this repo already investigated and rejected as unavailable: hk.pkl's own in-file comment records '#154: no hclfmt step — `hclfmt` is not in the mise registry (only hcl2json/hcloud), so it can't satisfy ci-local-parity.' A live `mise registry` grep for hcl confirms the same two entries and no hclfmt, at the current host/mise state — so the Config.Step exists in the hk 1.57.0 pkl builtin set but there is nothing this repo can pin to run its `argv = List("hclfmt", "-w", "{{files}}")` locally, which the finding's own rationale (AGENTS.md's CI-local-parity policy: 'every hk tool is in mise.toml') would then violate. The duplicate-check half of the finding (docker_bake_check re-running devcontainer read-configuration) may still be worth trimming, but not via hclfmt.
  - Evidence: hk.pkl:422-425 (`// #154: no hclfmt step — \`hclfmt\` is not in the mise registry (only\n  // hcl2json/hcloud), so it can't satisfy ci-local-parity...`); live probe `mise registry | grep -i hcl` -> only `hcl2json` and `hcloud` rows, no `hclfmt` (control arm: the same command surfaces real entries for a term known present, so the tool is not silently filtering).
- **Refuted by `risk`:** The proposed replacement (hk 1.57's Builtins.hclfmt) would silently drop the ci-local-parity invariant this repo already gates on: hk.pkl's own adjacent comment records that hclfmt was rejected before for exactly this reason ('hclfmt is not in the mise registry ... so it can't satisfy ci-local-parity'), and a live `mise registry` grep confirms hclfmt still is not installable via mise (only hcl2json/hcloud/terraform* match `hcl`). Adopting the finding's named alternative as-is would add an hk tool with no mise-pinned binary — the exact violation .claude/rules/ci-local-parity.md Rule 2 ("every hk tool is in mise.toml") exists to prevent — without naming how hclfmt gets installed. The finding's own hedge (a `docker buildx bake --print` probe) is a different, untested alternative, not the one stated as the fix.
  - Evidence: hk.pkl:421-426 (`// #154: no hclfmt step — 'hclfmt' is not in the mise registry ... so it can't satisfy ci-local-parity`); live probe `mise registry | grep -i hcl` -> only `hcl2json`/`hcloud` (2026-09-09); .claude/rules/ci-local-parity.md Rule 2 header 'every hk tool is in mise.toml'.

### `mise-tasks-2-2` — mise-tasks-2 — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** Every network- or subprocess-bound task in this unit runs unbounded: renovate-dryrun (documented ~80s, and its own comment warns a `deb` datasource pointed at Ubuntu's archive downloads the whole main,universe Packages index), verify-apt-pins (throwaway `docker run` + apt solver, ~60s), apt-repo (fetches a remote Packages index), graphify-prs (concurrent `gh pr diff` network calls), bakeoff (repeated model extraction runs), codex-lane and codex-lane-e2e (real `codex exec`, network + credits), and `doctor -- --live` (spawns each stdio MCP server). None declares a `timeout`.
- **Claimed native alternative:** mise per-task `timeout` ("Maximum execution time for this task... accepts durations such as `30s`, `5m`, or `1h`... The task fails if it does not complete within the configured duration"), plus the `mise run --timeout` CLI flag and the global `task.timeout` setting.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** Partial cover with no stated migration path, refuted on two independent grounds visible in this same repo. (1) mise.toml:207-213's own comment on [tasks.lint] records that this exact question was already probed and answered: 'mise's task timeout kills the child and fails loud, but it lacks lint.py's hk-log-tail diagnostics, so the wrapper STAYS (decision 15's retire condition was full equivalence; it is not equivalent)' -- i.e. this repo has a standing decision that native `timeout` is NOT a full-coverage substitute for a custom bounded runner, yet finding mise-tasks-2-2 proposes exactly that substitution for 7+ other tasks at 'zero maintenance cost' without addressing the precedent it contradicts. The mise doc itself supports the gap: task-configuration.md:1065-1066 says only 'The task fails if it does not complete within the configured duration' -- no mention of process-group/descendant cleanup or failure diagnostics, which is precisely what lint.py's wrapper adds (killpg on a fresh process group + hk-log-tail read on timeout, lint.py's own module docstring). (2) For codex-lane specifically, the finding's own target list, applying a hard kill-on-timeout directly conflicts with this repo's documented, deliberate design in dag_tick.py: a WEDGED long-running agent process is handled as 'classify-and-log only, never auto-respawn' in this slice ('Slice 1 deliberately ships WITHOUT automated stall recovery', dag_tick.py module docstring) precisely because forced termination of an in-flight lane produces inconsistent state for the reaper to sort out. A blanket `timeout =` on codex-lane/codex-lane-e2e would force exactly the kill this design explicitly defers, with no stated reconciliation.
  - Evidence: mise.toml:207-213 (in-repo prior-art comment establishing non-equivalence); python/src/dotfiles_setup/lint.py:18-23 (process-group kill + log-tail diagnostics the wrapper provides and native timeout does not); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/mise/docs/tasks/task-configuration.md:1060-1078 (### `timeout`, confirms only 'the task fails', no cleanup/diagnostics semantics documented); python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_tick.py:9-13,207-212 ('WEDGED... is classify-and-log only, never auto-respawn' -- the repo's chosen alternative to killing a stalled lane).
- **Refuted by `risk`:** The blanket recommendation folds in `[tasks.codex-lane]` and `[tasks.codex-lane-e2e]`, and for those two a mise-level `timeout` would silently defeat a tested, documented invariant: `run_lane_cli`'s crash-safety is built entirely on Python exception handling (`except BaseException as exc: ... re-raise`, python/src/dotfiles_setup/codex_lane.py, settling the lane in a `finally`-shaped path before the exception propagates) so that even a launcher crash or Ctrl-C still records an EXIT line and leaves the lane reapable (`test_a_launcher_crash_still_settles_the_lane`, tests/test_codex_lane.py:690-711, using a raised OSError as the crash vector). mise's task `timeout` kills the task's process from OUTSIDE — the mise docs describe only "the task fails if it does not complete" with no documented SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL grace window mise's own comment at mise.toml:207-211 records only that the child is killed, not how — and codex_lane.py installs no `signal.signal(SIGTERM, ...)` handler (grep for `signal\.` returns 0 hits in that module). Python's default SIGTERM disposition terminates the process WITHOUT raising a catchable exception (unlike SIGINT, which the interpreter turns into KeyboardInterrupt), so an external mise-timeout kill would bypass the `except BaseException`/settle-on-crash path entirely and leave the lane `in_progress` with no settled signal — exactly the "NOT_SETTLED, a no-op edge, on every tick forever, watched by nobody" failure mode that suites.toml's `workflow.codex-lane-producer` contract (python/verification/suites.toml:2181-2192) names as the thing the design prevents, with no replacement (no signal handler, no exclusion of these two tasks) named in the finding. The finding already excludes ship/land for an analogous reason (waiting on remote CI) but does not extend that carve-out to codex-lane/codex-lane-e2e, so as written it would apply an untested external-kill path to a subsystem whose only proven crash-safety mechanism is in-process.
  - Evidence: python/src/dotfiles_setup/codex_lane.py (no `signal.signal`/SIGTERM handler; `except BaseException as exc:` crash-settle path, confirmed present via workflow.codex-lane-producer's per_path_tokens 'except BaseException as exc:' at python/verification/suites.toml:2192); tests/test_codex_lane.py:690-711 (`test_a_launcher_crash_still_settles_the_lane`, crash vector is an in-process `raise OSError`, not an external signal); python/verification/suites.toml:2181-2192 (`workflow.codex-lane-producer` — "A launcher that died between writing lane.json and recording an exit leaves the lane in_progress with no settled signal: NOT_SETTLED, a no-op edge, on every tick forever, watched by nobody"); mise.toml:207-213 (the repo's own comment on the ONE existing `timeout =` user records only that mise "kills the child", not the signal/grace-period semantics); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/mise/docs/tasks/task-configuration.md:1059-1075 (`### timeout` docs: "The task fails if it does not complete within the configured duration" — no signal-handling detail given, i.e. no documented catchable-first-then-kill contract to rely on).

### `mise-tasks-2-3` — mise-tasks-2 — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** `graphify-update` rebuilds graphify-out/graph.json from the repo tree but declares neither `sources` nor `outputs`, so mise cannot tell whether the graph is up to date; and the repo's own freshness gate cannot either — `graphify_health` never compares the graph against source mtimes/content. Its only STALE path is a build-receipt mismatch, and `graphify-first.md` states this repo writes no receipt, so a graph arbitrarily behind the tree reports FRESH and every `graphify-query`/`graphify-affected` caller is silently served stale answers.
- **Claimed native alternative:** mise `sources` + `outputs`: "if this and `outputs` is defined, mise will skip executing tasks where the modification time of the oldest output file is newer than the modification time of the newest source file" and "This is also used in `mise watch` to know which files/directories to watch" — with `mise watch graphify-update` then rebuilding on change.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** Partial cover with no stated migration path, on two behaviours the custom task names that `sources`/`outputs` staleness-skip does not address. (1) mise.toml:746 documents a supported invocation this finding never accounts for: 'Pass a target: mise run graphify-update -- src/some/dir', and graphify.py:536,548 (`def update(project_root, target=".")`) confirms the rebuild scope is a runtime CLI argument, not statically knowable at task-definition time -- mise's sources/outputs mechanism (task-configuration.md:431-445) compares a FIXED declared glob's mtimes against fixed declared outputs, and cannot scope its freshness check to whatever target a given invocation passes, so the proposed declaration would either falsely skip a targeted partial rebuild or ignore the parameter entirely. (2) The finding's own evidence cites graphify_health's CORRUPT branch (graphify.py:224-242) as a named failure mode this task must be able to recover from by rebuilding, but declaring `outputs = ["graphify-out/graph.json"]` means mise will skip re-running whenever that file's mtime is newer than the sources -- exactly the state a corrupt-but-recently-built graph is in -- and the finding states no `--force`/override migration path for that case, so the change would silently defeat the one recovery action ('the ONLY sanctioned way to rebuild the graph in this repo', mise.toml:741) the corrupt-graph failure mode depends on.
  - Evidence: mise.toml:746 ('Pass a target: mise run graphify-update -- src/some/dir') and python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:536,548 (dynamic `target` argv, not a static path set); python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:224-242 (`graphify_health`'s CORRUPT branch, the failure mode a forced rebuild must recover from); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/mise/docs/tasks/task-configuration.md:431-445 (`### sources`, 'mise will skip executing tasks where the modification time of the oldest output file is newer than the modification time of the newest source file' -- a static, invocation-blind comparison with no stated force override in the finding).

Routing either through `dotfiles-setup <verb>` would import all 71 modules' transitive dependencies and any of their module-level side effects into that trust boundary's process — the identical hazard class the InstructionsLoaded precedent was hardened against, in the same codebase, and cited nowhere in this finding's rationale (which only considered the argv-provenance angle and found it unbroken). The finding's own counter-argument undersells the real risk and its confidence (0.5) does not reflect an established, on-point counter-precedent already in the repo.

### `mod-codex_agent_parity-8` — mod-codex_agent_parity — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** `.md` content requirements: a `model:` frontmatter key must be PRESENT (value deliberately unchecked), and the body must carry three repo-authored strings — `--model gpt-5.6-sol`, `model_reasoning_effort="xhigh"`, and the no-substitute prohibition — matched on whitespace-flattened text.
- **Claimed native alternative:** mdschema (pinned `aqua:jackchuka/mdschema` 0.15.2, currently UNWIRED) validates markdown declaratively: its schema exposes a `frontmatter` block with required/optional fields (`FrontmatterConfig` / `FrontmatterField`, incl. `enum` for allowed values) and a per-section `required_text` constraint — between them, `model:` presence and the three body strings are expressible without Python. agnix does NOT cover this: CC-AG-003 only validates a `model` value when one is present, never its absence.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** Live-probed mdschema 0.15.2 (the repo's pinned version) and it does NOT survive a line-wrap the way the module's own flatten() does. Built a minimal .mdschema.yml with required_text: 'Never substitute your own reasoning for a failed codex call' and a markdown fixture with that exact phrase split across a newline (identical to the module's real corpus shape and to its own test, test_an_md_marker_survives_being_reflowed in tests/test_codex_agent_parity.py, which asserts this precise marker must match after being reflowed). mdschema reported the text as NOT FOUND (rc=1); joining it onto one line made it pass (rc=0). So the native alternative is defeated by exactly the failure mode the module's docstring (lines 39-42) calls 'a second, permanent reason not to rely on' a raw scan, and that the module was rebuilt specifically to survive. The finding itself named this as the decisive open question ('if it cannot, the reflow defence the module was rebuilt around is lost') and hedged confidence to 0.5 on it; the probe answers that question negatively, so the coverage claim does not hold for the reflow-sensitive half of _md_violations — a partial cover with no stated fallback for the gap.
  - Evidence: live probe (2026-09-09) via `mise exec -- mdschema check <fixture>.md --schema <fixture>.yml`: wrapped text ("...Never substitute your own reasoning for\na failed codex call...") -> '✗ Required text ... not found in section' rc=1; same text unwrapped on one line -> '✓ No violations found' rc=0. Compare python/src/dotfiles_setup/codex_agent_parity.py:136-142 (flatten()) and tests/test_codex_agent_parity.py:326-336 (test_an_md_marker_survives_being_reflowed, the same marker string, asserting it must survive reflow) — the exact behavior mdschema fails to reproduce
- **Refuted by `risk`:** hk.pkl explicitly records mdschema adoption as DEFERRED because the schema file it would need does not exist yet — so the named replacement has zero live enforcement today, contradicting the finding's framing of it as an available swap. Worse, the module's own docstring states the whitespace-flattened marker match exists specifically because 'any multi-word content marker is defeatable by reflow' (a real, previously-measured corruption case), and the finding itself flags as UNPROBED whether mdschema's `required_text` performs that same reflow-normalization. Retiring the presence-and-literal-string checks now, before that property is confirmed, risks silently reopening the exact vulnerability class this module was rebuilt to close — this is a live invariant with no verified replacement, which is precisely what the RISK lens refutes.
  - Evidence: hk.pkl:355-363 ('#160 T12: rumdl/mdschema builtin adoption DEFERRED with probe evidence ... mdschema requires authoring a schema file that does not exist yet'); python/src/dotfiles_setup/codex_agent_parity.py:19-38 (module docstring: 'Any multi-word content marker is defeatable by reflow, which is a second, permanent reason not to rely on one' and 'matched against whitespace-flattened text so a wrap cannot hide them'); the finding's own rationale conceding 'whether `required_text` matches across a line wrap ... is unprobed'

### `mod-ghcr-1` — mod-ghcr — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** _parse_scopes() regex-scrapes the human-readable line `Token scopes: 'repo', 'read:org', ...` out of `gh auth status` stdout+stderr to learn the token's OAuth scopes.
- **Claimed native alternative:** gh exposes the authoritative machine-readable source directly: the `X-Oauth-Scopes` response header, which is exactly what gh itself reads to decide scope questions (`GetScopes`). Reachable from the CLI as `gh api -i / ` (`--include`/`-i` prints the status line and response headers).
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** The finding's own cited doc anchor is used to support a false claim: 'gh auth status has no --json (its only flags are --hostname/--show-token/--active, status.go:182-184)'. Reading the SAME function past line 184 shows a fourth flag block the finding omits: `cmdutil.AddJSONFlagsWithoutShorthand(cmd, &opts.Exporter, authStatusFields)` at status.go:187, wiring a real `--json`/`--jq` surface. That surface already exposes the exact datum the finding wants (the raw, unformatted OAuth scope string) as `authEntry.Scopes` (`json:"scopes,omitempty"`, status.go:38), populated directly from the same `X-Oauth-Scopes` header the finding's proposed `gh api -i` route would header-scrape (status.go: 'entry.Scopes = scopesHeader', ~line 415, fed by shared.GetScopes). So the simplest, most idiomatic native replacement is `gh auth status --json hosts --jq '.hosts[<host>][].scopes'` on the SAME command already in use -- no header parsing needed at all -- not the roundabout `gh api -i` + header-scrape route the finding proposes on the strength of a doc anchor that does not say what is claimed when read in full.
  - Evidence: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/gh/pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go:182-187 (flags block, including the omitted AddJSONFlagsWithoutShorthand call 3 lines after the finding's cited range); status.go:38 (`Scopes string \`json:"scopes,omitempty"\``); status.go:52-53 (`authStatusFields = []string{"hosts"}`, confirming --json hosts is a real, documented flag: see also status.go:165 `$ gh auth status --json hosts`)
- **Refuted by `currency`:** The finding's premise ('gh auth status has no --json (its only flags are --hostname/--show-token/--active, status.go:182-184)') is factually wrong at the installed/pinned gh. `gh auth status` DOES support --json on this host, and it is a simpler, more direct native route than the X-Oauth-Scopes-header path the finding proposes: no separate `gh api` round-trip, no header parsing, structured JSON with an unquoted plain-string `scopes` field per host entry. Live-verified on the actually-installed gh (2.100.0, resolved via `which -a gh` -> mise github-cli shim) in this session: `gh auth status --help` lists `--json fields`/`--jq expression` flags and an EXAMPLES block showing `gh auth status --json hosts`; `gh auth status --json hosts` returned real output including `"scopes":"admin:org, gist, notifications, ... write:packages"` for the active account. Control arm: the finding's own cited file (`gh/pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go`) in fact contains `cmd.Flags()...` plus `cmdutil.AddJSONFlagsWithoutShorthand(cmd, &opts.Exporter, authStatusFields)` at status.go:187 and `var authStatusFields = []string{"hosts"}` at status.go:52-54, registering exactly the --json flag the finding says doesn't exist -- the finding read status.go:182-184 (the non-JSON flags) but missed line 187 two lines below, in the same file it cited. The finding's proposed X-Oauth-Scopes/`gh api -i` route is itself real and separately live-verified (`gh api -i /user` returned an `X-Oauth-Scopes:` header on this host), so the refactor direction is not wrong in kind, but its stated justification for choosing that route over the CLI's own auth-status JSON output is a stale/incorrect currency claim about the current tool.
  - Evidence: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/gh/pkg/cmd/auth/status/status.go:52-54,187 (authStatusFields + AddJSONFlagsWithoutShorthand); live: `gh auth status --json hosts` and `gh auth status --help` run against the installed gh 2.100.0 in this session (2026-09-09), both showing --json is real and already returns a `scopes` field

### `mod-ghcr-5` — mod-ghcr — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** The whole check is wired as an unconditional hk pre-push step that shells out to the module and needs a logged-in gh plus five network round-trips on every push; CI jobs that push must be excluded from hooks by separate ADR-0001 machinery because this step cannot pass on a runner.
- **Claimed native alternative:** hk 1.57 has two step-level gating mechanisms this step does not use: `profiles: List<String>?` (opt-in/opt-out step selection, driven by `HK_PROFILE`/`hk.profile` git config, with a `missing-profiles` warning-suppression tag) and `step_condition: String?` (the step runs only if the condition evaluates true, e.g. `exec('...')`).
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** The `profiles`/`step_condition` citations are individually accurate (Config.pkl profiles ~662-681, step_condition ~850-858, HK_PROFILE at docs/environment_variables.md:248-257, hide_warnings 'missing-profiles' at Config.pkl ~137-147 -- all confirmed verbatim), but the finding's coverage claim for `profiles` does not hold up: hk's own doc for the `missing-profiles` warning tag describes 'steps being skipped due to missing profiles', i.e. a step carrying `profiles = List("publish")` is OFF BY DEFAULT and runs only when a developer explicitly sets `HK_PROFILE` to include it on that invocation. The finding proposes this ('profiles makes the whole network gate opt-in for the push that actually matters') as a pure improvement but never states how hk, or the developer, would automatically identify 'the push that actually matters' -- there is no described trigger (branch name, changed paths, etc.) wiring HK_PROFILE on for a real publish-relevant push. That is a genuine behavior change from the current step (which the same evidence block shows runs unconditionally on every push, hk.pkl:773-777): switching to profiles silently drops the automatic, no-memory-required prerequisite check the custom wiring currently guarantees, replacing it with a manual opt-in that depends on a developer remembering to set an env var -- exactly the kind of human-memory dependency a pre-push gate exists to remove. No migration path closes that gap, so per the coverage lens this is a partial cover.
  - Evidence: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/pkl/Config.pkl:137-147 ('missing-profiles': 'Suppresses warnings about steps being skipped due to missing profiles' -- confirms off-by-default/opt-in semantics); hk.pkl:773-777 (current step has no profiles/condition -- runs on every push unconditionally, the behavior the migration would drop)
- **Refuted by `risk`:** Confirmed against the pinned hk 1.57.0 doc itself: a step's `profiles` field is opt-IN, not opt-out -- 'The linter will only run if its profile is in HK_PROFILE' (Config.pkl:661-662), and HK_PROFILE defaults to unset/empty (docs/environment_variables.md's HK_PROFILE section shows no default-on value, and hide_warnings' own doc names 'missing-profiles: suppresses warnings about steps being skipped due to missing profiles' as the routine outcome). Adopting `profiles` for ghcr_publish_prereqs as the finding recommends ('opt-in ... rather than taxing every push') would therefore make the step SKIP by default on every ordinary local push unless a developer remembers to export HK_PROFILE=<tag> first -- silently dropping the 'every push checked' invariant currently guaranteed by the unconditional step at hk.pkl:774-777, replaced by nothing that runs automatically. This is exactly the failure shape ADR-0001 itself exists to warn about ('correctness now depends on remembering', quoted verbatim in python/src/dotfiles_setup/workflow_hooks.py:19-22) being reintroduced at the step-selection layer instead of the hook-skip layer. The `step_condition` half of the finding (self-skip when gh isn't authenticated) is comparatively low-risk since a normal dev push already has gh authenticated, but the finding bundles both mechanisms into one 'refactor' recommendation without flagging that the profiles half is opt-in-by-default.
  - Evidence: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/pkl/Config.pkl:661-662 ('The linter will only run if its profile is in HK_PROFILE') and :137-148 (missing-profiles warning tag documents skip-by-default as the expected outcome); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/docs/environment_variables.md HK_PROFILE section (no default-on value; must be exported per invocation); hk.pkl:774-777 (current unconditional step); python/src/dotfiles_setup/workflow_hooks.py:19-22 (the ADR-0001 text this would reproduce: 'correctness now depends on remembering').

### `mod-lock_shared-3` — mod-lock_shared — claimed **refactor** (2/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** A macOS-host -> amd64-devcontainer routing layer (host capability check, tri-state `--container/--no-container`, `/workspaces/<basename>` path translation, `--remote-env` plumbing) whose entire purpose is to get `mise lock` executed on linux.
- **Claimed native alternative:** The repo already runs `mise lock` on a GitHub-hosted linux-x64 runner for the OTHER two lockfiles — the `lock-refresh` composite action, which states the linux-runner requirement as its own contract — and that lane does NOT cover `.config/mise/mise.lock`: `lock-refresh-root` is handed only the root `mise.toml`. Extending the existing native linux lane (plus `gh workflow run` / `mise run gha-dispatch` to trigger it on demand) covers the same need without a local container round-trip.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** The rationale's load-bearing claim -- 'the on-demand path [is] the only route to a linux-resolved shared lock' -- is contradicted by the repo's own git history, which the finding never checked. `git log -- .config/mise/mise.lock` shows renovate[bot] committing directly to this exact file (#878 'Lock file maintenance', 2026-09-02; #822 'chore(deps): update all dependencies', 2026-09-01) with no lock_shared.py involvement -- Renovate's native `mise` manager already regenerates `.config/mise/mise.lock` for routine bumps today, and `.github/workflows/refresh.yml:235-236` documents this explicitly ('Renovate rewrites an exact pin in `.config/mise/conf.d/shared.toml` and correctly regenerates both HOST locks (mise.lock, .config/mise/mise.lock)'). So a second automated, linux-resolving route to this lockfile already exists and is observably working -- the premise motivating the refactor (no automated route exists, so extend lock-refresh) is factually false as stated, even though the underlying observation that `lock-refresh`'s composite doesn't cover shared.toml (main.py:2139, lock_refresh.py:31) is accurate on its own. Separately, the proposed mechanism itself is unverified: `lock_top_level_config_tools` runs `mise lock` with `cwd=config_path.parent`, which for `.config/mise/conf.d/shared.toml` is the `conf.d/` directory itself, not the repo root or `.config/mise/` -- untested against mise's actual config-root/lockfile-path resolution (config_root.rs:97-99, lockfile.rs:1489-1494 do point the *lockfile* at `.config/mise/mise.lock` for a conf.d file, but cwd-based project-root *discovery* from inside `conf.d/` for `--bump` resolution is a different, unverified question) -- exactly the class of 'should work' assumption this same module's own docstring shows failing twice (respec rounds 1 and 2) for the identical mise+conf.d interaction. A refactor finding whose central justification is empirically false and whose replacement mechanism is unverified does not clear the coverage bar.

### `mod-mise_config_context-1` — mod-mise_config_context — claimed **refactor** (3/3 refuted)

- **Claim:** Hand-rolled path filtering: MISE_CONFIG_GLOBS (7 fnmatch globs) plus matches(), which resolves the edited path, enforces repo containment via Path.relative_to(repo_root), and fnmatch-matches the repo-relative posix path. The hook is wired unconditionally on matcher 'Edit|Write|NotebookEdit', so a `uv run --project .../python dotfiles-setup mise-config-context` process is spawned for EVERY file write in the session and 99% of those spawns exit 0 with no output.
- **Claimed native alternative:** Claude Code's per-handler `if` field on tool-event hooks. It takes permission-rule syntax matching the tool name AND its arguments together, is evaluated on PostToolUse, and skips the handler (no process spawn) when the pattern does not match. Path anchoring is native too: a leading `/` anchors the pattern at the primary working directory, which is exactly the repo-containment property matches() implements by hand, and `Edit(path)` is the rule form that covers Write and NotebookEdit as well.
- **Refuted by `coverage`:** The finding's own cited doc anchor (permissions.md:316) does not say what the finding needs it to say. That line describes the built-in ALLOW/DENY permission engine's rule normalisation ('Claude Code checks file permissions against Edit(path) and Read(path) rules only... Use Edit(docs/**) in place of Write(docs/**), NotebookEdit(docs/**)') -- a different subsystem from the PostToolUse hook `if` filter the finding proposes to use. hooks.md's own description of `if` (hooks.md:353, :427) never states that an `if: "Edit(<glob>)"` handler fires when tool_name is literally 'Write' or 'NotebookEdit'; its only worked example (Edit(*.ts)) matches the Edit tool against itself. The finding's rationale admits this outright ('The one thing not settled on paper is whether an if: Edit(...) handler actually fires for a Write/NotebookEdit tool call... Probe it before rewiring, or the filter silently drops the wholesale-Write case this hook exists for') -- and the wholesale-Write case is not a peripheral behaviour, it is the stated reason the module is a hook at all (mise_config_context.py:8-12: 'A Write that replaces mise.toml wholesale never reads it, so the rule would be absent in exactly the case it exists for'). Independent corroboration that the native filter is inadequate here: this repo's own open ticket #935 (which the sibling finding -3 also cites and which this same audit unit inherits) records, as the reason the dispatcher project rejected the native filter as the delivery mechanism, that it 'narrows event delivery but cannot compose rules, cannot dedup, is documented best-effort, has no equivalent on the second agent, and depends on glob semantics that have already changed once.' A coverage claim resting on an unverified, self-flagged assumption about tool-name normalisation, contradicted by the project's own prior probe of the identical question, is refuted under the coverage lens's rule that 'a doc anchor that does not exist or does not say what is claimed is refuted.'
  - Evidence: python/src/dotfiles_setup/mise_config_context.py:8-12 (why a hook, not a paths:-scoped rule -- the wholesale-Write case); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/hooks.md:353,427 (`if` syntax description names only Edit(*.ts) matching the Edit tool, never states Write/NotebookEdit normalisation); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/permissions.md:316 (the Edit(path)-covers-Write/NotebookEdit canonicalisation is scoped explicitly to 'file permissions' checks, not hook `if` matching); gh issue #935 body (open, fetched live): native filter rejected as delivery mechanism -- 'cannot compose rules, cannot dedup, is documented best-effort, has no equivalent on the second agent'
- **Refuted by `currency`:** The `if` field itself is real, current, and long-standing (added well before the offline snapshot's ceiling of 2.1.257, so present at the installed 2.1.266 with no version gate blocking it) -- not refuted on pure version-availability grounds. But the finding's load-bearing native_alternative claim -- that a native `if: "Edit(...)"` handler can actually replace mise_config_context.py's wired PostToolUse dispatch -- is directly contradicted by this repo's own already-filed, OPEN ticket #935, which the finding never surfaces. #935 requires the eventual swap's commit body to record 'why the platform's native path filter was NOT used as the delivery mechanism (it narrows event delivery but cannot compose rules, cannot dedup, is documented best-effort, has no equivalent on the second agent, and depends on glob semantics that have already changed once)'. Those are exactly the properties mise_config_context.py's `_key()`/`already_seen()` (per-session-and-per-agent dedup) and `matches()` (7-glob composition) rely on, and the finding's own rationale flags the tool-name-normalization question as 'not settled on paper' -- which is the correct instinct, but the repo has already settled it in the opposite direction on record, for reasons broader than the one gap the finding names. The finding is not a false claim about the feature existing; it is a recommendation the project has already evaluated and rejected in favor of the #928/#935 rule-registry dispatcher (which finding -3 in this same unit correctly identifies).
  - Evidence: gh issue view 935 (state OPEN) body: "Record in the commit body why the platform's native path filter was not used as the delivery mechanism (it narrows event delivery but cannot compose rules, cannot dedup, is documented best-effort, has no equivalent on the second agent, and depends on glob semantics that have already changed once), and why the batch-level hook was examined and rejected (no matcher, no second-agent equivalent)."; docs/research/kb/reports/agents/2026-09-02-ticket-cut-advisor.md:152 (ticket L: "...mise reminder becomes a registry row; commit body records the native-filter justification and the PostToolBatch rejection (stories 51, 55)."); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/changelog.md:3591 ("Added conditional `if` field for hooks using permission rule syntax ... reducing process spawning overhead" -- confirms the feature is real and predates 2.1.257, so this is a design rejection already on record, not a version gap).
- **Refuted by `risk`:** The proposed native `if`-filtered sibling-handlers refactor was already evaluated and rejected by the project's own filed follow-on ticket, for reasons the finding never surfaces: it cannot compose rules, cannot dedup, is documented best-effort, and has no equivalent on a second agent.
