- **`mod-branch_guard`** — `mod-branch_guard-1` The capability is a PREDICATE ON GIT STATE, and every native pre-write control in Claude Code 2.1.266 is a static path pattern: permission rules match paths, sandbox denyWrite matches paths, and neither can say 'only while HEAD == main'. The docs themselves place branch awareness on the hook side (hooks.md:997). The exemption half is already native — is_ignored shells out to `git check-ignore` rather than re-implementing gitignore semantics — so there is no homegrown parser to retire. hk cannot substitute: it is a git-hook system that only sees a commit, which is precisely the gap the module's docstring (branch_guard.py:4-15) exists to close. `mod-branch_guard-4` `-w` is a LAUNCH-TIME OPT-IN, not an invariant: it changes where a session that chose it works, and says nothing about the session that did not — including every session started by `claude` in the main clone right after `mise run land` leaves the user on `main`, which is the documented trigger. Nothing in settings can force `--worktree` for interactive sessions (worktrees.md documents isolation for subagents and for sessions launched with the flag; there is no `isolation` setting at session scope), so the guard remains the only layer that fires whether or not the human remembered. Recommend `-w` as a habit; do not retire. `mod-branch_guard-5` The harness supplies only `cwd`, which is the wrong fact twice over — the target file often sits in a different worktree from the session cwd, and a Write can name a path whose directory does not exist yet (:112-128 exists for exactly that). The native tool for these facts IS `git rev-parse`/`git check-ignore`, and the module already calls it rather than re-implementing it; what is custom is only the batching into one invocation (#527) and the classify() table, which buys the hot path 1 subprocess instead of 3 on every Edit. `gh repo view` is a network call and is unusable in a 20s PreToolUse hook. Nothing to retire.
- **`mod-child_env`** — `mod-child_env-5` Justification, not a default: no tool in the stack offers 'hand me a copy of my environment minus mise's delta blob'. Python's subprocess has no env filter, mise's redactions are output-side, hk/uv/gh have no equivalent, and the Claude Code settings `env` block only ADDS variables. The blob is also uniquely worth removing — it is the single field carrying every other secret at once, in a compressed form no secret scanner can read (gitleaks 2 -> 0, betterleaks 1 -> 0, per .claude/rules/do-not.md #10), which is why the repo's own no_env_dump gate exists. The function is 3 lines, has six-plus live call sites, and cannot break a child because nothing but mise reads the variable and mise re-derives it.
- **`mod-classifier_tables`** — `mod-classifier_tables-1` Required justification: the gate's whole value is deriving an axis set that is a sound over-approximation across call boundaries and refusing a pin whose gated-class set is unknown. Every native linter available at these pins matches single nodes within one file; none carries a call graph, an alias fixpoint, or a fail-closed unknown state, and ruff cannot host a user rule at all. Re-implementing this in ast-grep YAML would silently downgrade it to the syntactic-substring class of check the module's own docstring (:1163-1172) records itself having been convicted of. `mod-classifier_tables-3` Required justification: the predicate's output is only useful set-differenced against REGISTRY inside the same process (`find_unlisted`:1204-1228), so even a working ast-grep rule would have to be shelled out to and re-parsed, adding a second engine and a second language to save ~40 lines of `ast` that already share `_annotation_name`/`_ENUM_BASES` with the derivation engine. The unification question below is worth settling only if a second, independent consumer of the predicate ever appears. `mod-classifier_tables-4` Required justification: the only native-to-this-repo alternative is strictly weaker along the exact axis this function exists to close. `per_path_tokens` matches text; `_binds_symbol` matches an assignment node, which is what makes `table_missing` a real check rather than one a comment can satisfy. Nothing in ruff, ast-grep, hk builtins or the verify engine at the current pins provides an anchored 'this name is bound here' assertion, so replacing it would reintroduce the documented defect.
- **`mod-codec`** — `mod-codec-1` The justification is the library's own design: because hooks are per-call arguments, every direct msgspec call would carry its own copy of the conversion table, which is the drift #675 exists to prevent — nothing native forces centralisation. And the one type that forces the issue, pathlib.Path, is unsupported in both directions on msgspec main, so upgrading the pin cannot retire this module. Retiring or thinning it would reintroduce the silent-corruption case the tests pin (a Path-annotated field decoding to str). `mod-codec-2` singledispatch covers only half the seam and breaking the halves apart would destroy the module's stated invariant. dec_hook is handed an ANNOTATION, not an instance — codec.py:314-336 — and an annotation can be a typing._GenericAlias with no __mro__ (codec.py:252-268, review F1), which singledispatch cannot dispatch on at all; it also takes the target type as a second argument (codec.py:87-94), a shape singledispatch's single-argument dispatch does not express. register() deliberately binds both directions in one call (codec.py:210-239) because a half-registration is the silent-corruption case, so adopting singledispatch for encode only would split the atomic registration into two mechanisms with two registries. The dict+MRO walk is ~20 lines and keeps both directions symmetric. `mod-codec-3` The native mechanism is already adopted — this is a five-line wrapper around msgspec.inspect.type_info whose only custom part is mapping CustomType to None and catching the two errors type_info can raise (codec.py:190-196). msgspec offers no 'is this type natively supported?' predicate of its own, so the mapping has to live somewhere; nothing to retire and nothing further to adopt. `mod-codec-5` The native reuse pattern exists and codec.py is the one module allowed to use it, but it does not pay here: every call site is low-volume and one-shot (session_ledger.py:3246,3253,3727 write/read a single ledger record; graphify.py:191 reads one build receipt), and Decoders are typed, so adopting the pattern means a type-keyed decoder cache — new state and a cache-invalidation question added to a module whose whole value is being the one obvious place. Format itself has no native equivalent: msgspec exposes json/msgpack as separate modules with no format parameter, and the enum is what keeps 'add a wire format' a reviewed decision (the yaml/toml bans at python/pyproject.toml:133-139 depend on it). Revisit only if a hot loop appears.
- **`mod-codex_agent_parity`** — `mod-codex_agent_parity-2` Required justification: this is a repo-chosen convention that the harness explicitly does not require, so by construction no native tool will ever enforce it. It is still load-bearing here because the pairing check in `_pairing_violations` keys on the STEM while both harnesses key on the `name` FIELD — without the cross-check, a renamed `name:` would silently detach a lane from its pair while the gate stayed green. `mod-codex_agent_parity-3` Required justification: codex explicitly permits the mismatch, so no codex-native validation can ever fire on it. The check exists to keep the two-surface pairing (which is stem-keyed) honest, which is a property of THIS repo's layout, not of either harness. `mod-codex_agent_parity-6` Required justification: nothing in codex, Claude Code, agnix or taplo gates 'these bytes are still the ones this repo authored', and the sentinel is the only check in the module that survives an arbitrary rewrite of the file's prose. Worth recording alongside it, though, that the hazard is narrower than the docstring states — the importer in the corpus source skips existing targets, so the realistic failure is a hand edit or a DIFFERENT writer (the Desktop app binary is not in the corpus and its version is not pinned by this repo). `mod-codex_agent_parity-7` Required justification: cross-directory, cross-format pairing between two different vendors' agent layouts is a property of this repo's dual-surface convention; neither harness knows the other's directory is supposed to mirror it, and no linter in the pinned set (agnix, taplo, claude-code-lint, cclint, agents-lint, ast-grep, zizmor, ghalint) does set-difference across two trees. The `empty` arm is a control arm baked into the gate itself and has no native equivalent at all.
- **`mod-codex_lane`** — `mod-codex_lane-3` Justification, not a default: every native signal is emitted BY the codex process, and the invariant this code exists for is the case where that process produces nothing — a launcher that dies before the spawn, a `codex` binary missing from PATH under launchd, a SIGKILL. Those leave the lane `in_progress` with no settled signal, which `codex_verdict.reap` reads as NOT_SETTLED — a no-op edge, forever, watched by nobody (codex_lane.py:502-518). A `notify` program or a hook cannot fire in any of them, and both are CONFIG-layer registrations (`~/.codex/config.toml`), so they would fire for every codex invocation on the host, not only for lanes. `--json` is worse than useless here: it would put model output on the stream the liveness gate substring-matches, which is exactly invariant 1 (a model typing `EXIT: 0` settles its own lane). The only thing native could add is a richer in-band record, and the module deliberately leaves codex's stdout to launchd. `mod-codex_lane-4` Justification: the artifacts here exist to satisfy a CONSUMER inside this repo (`codex_verdict.reap` + `dag_tick.reap_codex_lanes`) whose contract — owner+status CAS under an exclusive flock, `verdict.json` -> `verdict.processed.json` rename for idempotency, a rework counter bounded by `--max-rework` — is not a shape any external tool models. The one native-ish alternative (codex's session/task registry) is keyed by codex thread id, is TUI-oriented, and carries no field the CAS re-verifies. Two of the module's invariants (clear the previous round's settled signals; read the consumed verdict BEFORE clearing) are properties of THIS protocol and have no external owner. Nothing to retire; nothing to wrap. `mod-codex_lane-5` Re-verified today against the CURRENTLY INSTALLED plugin (1.21.0, i.e. newer than the docstring's 2026-08-06 read) rather than trusting the docstring: all three clauses still hold — mktemp'd output paths, no `--output-schema` on either codex lane, no lane record. So the `use-tool-builtins.md` justification is live, not rotted, and the custom producer stays. Two things a future audit should re-check rather than inherit: the plugin's codex-review lane now passes `--json` and `-c sandbox_mode="read-only"`, so it is drifting TOWARD machine-readable output — the day it adds `--output-schema` plus a stable run dir, clause 1 and 2 die and this becomes a wrap-the-plugin refactor. The docstring's deliberate omission of line numbers remains correct (the file is replaced wholesale on plugin update); the line numbers in this finding are audit evidence with a version stamp, not a new pin. `mod-codex_lane-6` Justification: the custom part here is only WHERE the flag is set (on the spawn, so no brief has to remember it — agent-report-persistence.md §1b), and the flag itself is already the vendor's own opt-out, which is exactly what use-tool-builtins.md asks for. The codex-side knobs do not substitute: `--ignore-user-config` would drop the whole `$CODEX_HOME/config.toml` layer (model, provider, effort) to suppress a Claude-Code plugin's env-triggered hook chain that lives outside codex config entirely, and 0.152.0's `tools.update_plan` governs codex's OWN plan tool, not planning-with-files. Do not conflate the two when refreshing this comment. `mod-codex_lane-7` Nothing to retire — the module already uses the native structured-output mechanism (`--output-schema`, which is the whole reason #580 rejected prompt-enforcement), and the live host binary confirms none of the five flags moved between 0.146.0 and 0.152.1. The only actionable part is documentary: the two version stamps say 0.146.0 while the pin is 0.152.1, so a reader cannot tell 'still true' from 'never re-checked'. Refresh both stamps to 0.152.1 citing this probe. One capability the module could newly reach if it ever drops `--ephemeral`: `codex exec resume`/`fork` (0.148.0) would let a rework round continue round 1's thread instead of re-reading the diff cold — deliberately out of scope today, since `--ephemeral` is what keeps one transcript per round off disk.
- **`mod-codex_verdict`** — `mod-codex_verdict-4` Required justification: this is exactly-once consumption of a file written by an untrusted, sometimes-aborting producer, arbitrated between concurrent DAG ticks - a concurrency contract, not a serialisation or a CLI-flag problem, and no tool in the pinned set offers one. The module has already adopted every native that does exist (it passes --output-schema/-o rather than prompt-begging for JSON, and it uses stdlib fcntl rather than a hand-rolled lockfile protocol), and the parts that remain custom are precisely the parts the provider cannot enforce: the module's own measured evidence (:26-48) is that codex can write an empty file or no file at all, so 'the provider validated it' is necessary but never sufficient. The two inverted defaults are an operational policy choice for unattended running, which no upstream default can make for us. The one genuine duplication is internal, not native: the flock-on-append-handle idiom is a third copy of the same pattern (dag_tick.try_acquire_lock and codex_lane both carry it, cited in the docstring at :437-439 and codex_lane.py:306-309) - worth hoisting into one helper, but that is in-repo dedup, not a native supersession.
- **`mod-command_audit`** — `mod-command_audit-3` Justification, not a default: none of the four supported interfaces answers this module's question. `--output-format json` and `--resume` describe ONE run and would cost a model call per session; `transcript_path` hands back the same internal JSONL this module already parses (so it relocates the parse, it does not replace it — see finding 1); the Agent SDK observes a LIVE session, not history; and `/export` renders prose for a human. There is no native 'enumerate every Bash tool call across the last N sessions of this project' surface at 2.1.266. Two mitigations follow from the citation rather than from replacing the module: (a) the parse is already defensive per line, but nothing detects a WHOLESALE schema change — a renamed key yields 0 commands and a clean-looking report, the same silent-zero shape as finding 1, so the report should assert a non-zero floor or a known-key canary and fail loudly; (b) one part of the reverse engineering is now DOCUMENTED and the docstring is stale about it — nested subagent transcripts under `<session-id>/subagents/` are described in hooks.md:2325 (`agent_transcript_path` "is the subagent's own transcript stored in a nested subagents/ folder"), which confirms project_transcripts()'s rglob rather than leaving it as measurement-only folklore. `mod-command_audit-5` Justification: shellcheck — the only candidate native linter, already pinned and already wired into hk — covers ZERO of the four shapes, measured with a control arm rather than assumed. Three of them are not lint rules at all but epistemic rules about what a PROBE's output means (a bounded find turning 'unreachable' into 'absent'; nested quoting through docker exec mangling a payload; a grep -q match returning 141), and they are this repo's own doctrine from .claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md, which no third-party tool encodes. ast-grep does not help either: these are one-line ad-hoc shell strings from a transcript, not tracked source, so nothing in the hk/ast-grep tracked-file lane can ever see them — which is exactly the gap this section exists to fill (hk.pkl's no_grep_q_under_pipefail already covers the tracked-file half). `mod-command_audit-6` Justification: the fact being recorded is the ABSENCE of a decision, and every native observability surface is keyed to a decision having been made — tool_decision fires on accept/reject, PostToolUse fires on success, PermissionDenied fires only in auto mode and explicitly "doesn't run when a PreToolUse hook blocks a call" (hooks.md:2145). A wrapper that exits 0 because its interpreter was unreachable is, from the harness's point of view, an allow; nothing at 2.1.266 emits a 'hook could not run' signal a script can count. The custom log is therefore the only possible source, and it is per-user state by design because the failure mode is precisely that the repo's toolchain is unresolvable. Worth noting the residual: fail_open_summary reads a log with no upper bound and no rotation, and a partial line is dropped rather than counted (command_audit.py:627-629), so an under-count is possible in the one direction that matters.
- **`mod-config`** — `mod-config-6` Justified, not defaulted: the value is a repo-specific pairing between a host path and the container mount that R1's sshd reads authorized_keys from, which is knowledge no tool has — mise [env] could export it for task-launched processes, but the function is called from library paths that do not run under a mise task (devcontainer.json's initializeCommand, and devcontainer_names when composing the secrets env-file path), so a mise-only declaration would be absent exactly where it is needed. Its container-vs-host discriminator already reads the devcontainer spec's own containerEnv signal instead of sniffing /.dockerenv, which is the native-first shape this repo asks for.
- **`mod-container`** — `mod-container-3` Justification, not a default: the #677 failure this guards against — two containers (amd64 + arm64) alive for one clone, where a folder-inferred lookup silently smokes the wrong architecture (mise.toml:405-409 documents that exact trap) — is precisely what `devcontainer exec`'s single-container resolution CANNOT report, because it resolves and proceeds rather than counting. @devcontainers/cli 0.89.0 ships no enumeration subcommand at all, so there is nothing native to delegate the count to. The label vocabulary is already centralized in devcontainer_names.resolve_names(), so there is no duplication to retire either. Note this check must stay even after mod-container-1's refactor, which would otherwise hand container selection to the CLI and lose the ambiguity signal. `mod-container-4` Justification: the assertion is about the RUNNING container's realized state, and every native devcontainer surface at the pinned 0.89.0 reads the workspace CONFIG instead — a container started before a devcontainer.json edit satisfies read-configuration and still mounts the wrong tree, which is the exact false-positive .claude/rules/verify-before-advancing.md exists to prevent. The only native trimming available is cosmetic (a `docker inspect --format` Go template could filter Source-side in the engine instead of json.loads), which would cost testability for nothing. After mod-container-1 lands this function's return value stops being an exec workdir and becomes purely this assertion — narrow it to a bool then, do not delete it. `mod-container-5` Justification: the gate encodes a policy — '.claude/rules/verify-before-advancing.md' § 'Validate against the latest branch code' — that binds three independent facts (a container exists for THIS workspace+arch, its source is the live host tree, and its base is not older than mise-system.toml) into one rc. No shipped tool models 'is my running dev container a valid validation environment for this branch'; each vendor surface answers at most one third of it, and only about declared config. What SHOULD change is the internals, not the gate: findings 1 and 2 route its exec through the native CLI and its outer bound through the native mise timeout, leaving this composition — which is genuinely repo-specific — as the only custom part. Secondary note (not a native-alternative finding): `git grep` finds no `[[suite]]` in python/verification/suites.toml naming `verify-container-latest` or `container.py`, so the wiring between the mise task, the CLI subcommand and this module is asserted only by tests/test_container.py, not by a contract.
- **`mod-dag_project`** — `mod-dag_project-2` The documented census cannot supply the module's product. Every field the projected comment carries as CARGO is absent from the `claude agents --json` table at agent-view.md:653-659: there is no `needs` (the verbatim question), no `suggestedReply`, no `queuedPrompt` (the third term of the NEEDS_HUMAN conjunction, without which an already-answered node would be re-escalated forever), no `tempo` (the stall axis), no `updatedAt` (which python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:404-415 establishes is authoritative over the mtime), and no `cliVersion`. `waitingFor: input needed` is a CATEGORY, not the question text, so a projection built on it would post an escalation comment with nothing in it — the failure #602 exists to end, one layer up. A hybrid (classify from `--json`, fetch the payload from `state.json`) is worse than either: it would put two disagreeing readers on one node, the exact defect class python/verification/suites.toml:1565 makes this module's most load-bearing clause. Keeping the direct read is therefore justified, not merely convenient; the real mitigation is that the layout is read through `dag_tick.node_from_state`, one shared parser, so a harness layout change breaks in one place. Re-check this finding at any Claude Code release that adds a payload field to `claude agents --json`. `mod-dag_project-3` The native signal is gated on precisely the condition this module exists to survive. hooks.md:2206 says `agent_needs_input` fires when a background session starts waiting "while agent view is open in a terminal", and agent-view.md:130 repeats the gate; hooks.md:2207 states the same for `agent_completed`. The two live escalations that motivated #602 sat blocked for three and four weeks with no agent view open — under the native mechanism they would have emitted nothing at all, and even had one fired, a terminal bell is an EDGE event with no durable record, whereas the module's product is an append-only, deduped, byte-faithful tracker comment that is still there weeks later. It is also strictly one-directional and reads nothing the hook could hand it (the `needs` payload is not in the Notification hook input either). Nothing native covers this; keeping it is the justified answer, not the default one. `mod-dag_project-4` `--edit-last` gives ONE slot per (user, issue); this module needs one slot per (node, question) on an issue shared by every unbound node. On the standing escalation issue (`DEFAULT_ESCALATION_ISSUE = 623`, python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:96) a second escalated node running `--edit-last` would OVERWRITE the first node's escalation — destroying the record that is the module's entire deliverable, and doing it silently because the write succeeds. The key must also be composite in both directions, which `--edit-last` cannot express at all: python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:151-158 records that keying on the node alone silences a node that re-escalates with a NEW question, and on the digest alone collides across nodes asking the SAME one. The marker also cannot be replaced by the label, for the reason given at python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:184-190 (the label lives on the issue, so the first node would suppress every later one). Note that the parts of this layer that ARE native are already used: `gh api --paginate` for the comment list (python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:598) rather than a hand-rolled page loop. `mod-dag_project-6` The scheduling is ALREADY the native mechanism for its tier — mise's own `[bootstrap.macos.launchd.agents]` block, not a hand-written plist or a shell cron wrapper — so there is no custom scheduler here to retire. The Claude-Code-native schedulers each fail a hard requirement of this job: `/loop` and `CronCreate` are session-scoped (scheduled-tasks.md:11), and a projector whose purpose is to notice sessions nobody is watching cannot itself depend on a session being open; cloud Routines have no access to local files (scheduled-tasks.md:23) and so cannot read `~/.claude/jobs` on this Mac at all; and a Desktop scheduled task would spend model tokens on every one of the ~288 daily fires whose overwhelmingly common outcome is `0 escalations` and, by design, zero API calls (python/src/dotfiles_setup/dag_project.py:764-771). A deterministic Python run under launchd is the correct tier. Re-open this only if a future release gives Routines local-filesystem access.
- **`mod-dag_tick`** — `mod-dag_tick-4` The native event exists and matches the semantics, but it is explicitly conditioned on agent view being OPEN IN A TERMINAL (hooks.md:2206-2207, stated twice and independently at agent-view.md:130). This watchdog's entire premise is the unattended case — a launchd tick with no terminal and no agent view — so the hook would fire exactly when the watchdog is least needed and be silent exactly when it is most needed. The same condition rules out the census's `waitingFor` field, which is present only when `status` is `waiting` and `status` itself only 'While the process is alive' (agent-view.md:656-657), i.e. never for the escalated-and-then-crashed node this classification exists to protect. No native mechanism covers a headless, out-of-band escalation census, so the custom predicate stays. `mod-dag_tick-5` Required justification: the native candidate is documented as NOT providing this. mise's exclusive lock is per-command and global (it would serialise every other mise invocation on the host, which for a 60s agent is a denial-of-service on the operator's own shell), and mise's docs explicitly state the whole-task property does not exist yet. The mise launchd surface maps only the plist keys (StartInterval, ThrottleInterval) and documents no non-overlap guarantee, and the lock must also cover the manual `mise run dag-tick -- --dry-run` path that launchd cannot see at all. 12 lines of fcntl is the minimum correct thing here. `mod-dag_tick-6` Required justification: the native census is already adopted for everything it exposes (read_census at :1047 is the row source), and the documented field table simply does not carry the three axes the classifier turns on. `tempo` gates is_terminal (a done+active node is NOT terminal — the watchdog's primary recovery case), `queuedPrompt` is what splits NEEDS_HUMAN from REPLY_QUEUED, and `needs` is the escalation payload itself; none appear in agent-view.md:653-657. There is also no native last-progress timestamp, so the WEDGED staleness proxy has to come from the file's mtime. The only native improvement available is cross-checking the census `state` against the file's `state`, which is a consistency check, not a replacement. `mod-dag_tick-7` Required justification: this half is ALREADY the native mechanism and needs no change — the scheduling, the plist generation, the launchctl load and the drift check are all mise built-ins, and the repo holds only the declaration. The one thing to leave alone deliberately: mise's launchd surface offers `kickstart` and `keep_alive`, and this agent uses neither, consistent with .claude/rules/do-not.md's 'nothing applies a LaunchAgent implicitly' invariant. Recorded so a later audit does not 'modernize' a block that is already the tool built-in.
- **`mod-dependency_ownership`** — `mod-dependency_ownership-4` Required justification: every tool in the stack is scoped to a single manifest. The invariant here is inherently cross-manifest — 'this name must be owned by pyproject.toml AND NOT by mise's tool table' — and no package manager, linter, or Renovate preset computes that intersection, because none of them knows the other manager exists. That is precisely the case use-tool-builtins.md leaves to custom code. The custom code that should survive is the intersection and the failure message; its two INPUTS should come from native sources instead (findings -1 and -3), which is where the real modernization lives.
- **`mod-devcontainer_names`** — `mod-devcontainer_names-3` Justification, not a default: the digest has six Python consumers that a mise template cannot serve — container.py:40, docker.py:27, image_lock.py:51, lock_shared.py:137, sync.py:79 and lint.py:55 all import from this module, and mise filters are only evaluable inside mise config templates. Two further blockers: mise's `config_root` is the config directory and is not documented as symlink-resolved, while `workspace_hash` deliberately hashes the PHYSICAL path (:166-172) so two logical routes to one directory are one workspace; and the digest is load-bearing for already-deployed volume names — a drifting digest renames every home and reads as an empty home, not an error. Worth recording so nobody 'modernises' the derivation into a template: the native filter agrees on algorithm and truncation, which is exactly what makes the swap look safe and be wrong. `mod-devcontainer_names-4` Justification: the port must exist BEFORE the container does. devcontainer.json substitutes `${localEnv:DEVCONTAINER_SSH_PORT}` at `up` time, and `[tasks.up]` clears the stale host key with `ssh-keygen -R "[localhost]:$PORT"` before the container is created — `docker port` cannot answer either question because there is nothing to inspect yet. The derived port is also STABLE across recreate, which is what makes the documented R1 UX (`ssh ${USER}@localhost -p $(mise run ssh-port)`, a `~/.ssh/config` Host entry, one known-hosts line) work at all; an ephemeral port moves on every rebuild and turns each recreate into a fresh host-key mismatch. The one thing the native form buys — guaranteed no collision — is already bought differently, by placing the window at 20000-29999, below the macOS ephemeral range (:113-118). `mod-devcontainer_names-5` Justification: `_.source` is documented as bash-only with the shebang ignored (index.md:489-498), so adopting it would require re-introducing a `scripts/*.sh` shim purely to call `uv run … devcontainer env` — a new file gated by `bash_logic_budget` and squarely against [[zero-bash-logic]]. It is also `[env]`-scoped rather than task-scoped, so a resolver that spawns `uv`, `platform_target` and a path resolution would run on every shell prompt (troubleshooting.md:46) rather than once per devloop task, and it silently vanishes under mise safe mode (security.md:56) — the failure shape `[tasks.up]`'s comment already warns about, where empty `${localEnv:...}` substitutions produce an unnamed container instead of an error. The current `_dc_env="$(…)"` -then-`eval` form is deliberate for exactly that reason (mise.toml:296-302: assignment propagates the resolver's failure, bare `eval` would not). `mod-devcontainer_names-6` Justification: the unit already wraps the native feature rather than replacing it — there is nothing to retire and nothing further to adopt. The CLI's native inference is exactly what is insufficient (per-folder, arch-blind), and no flag derives a per-clone+arch value, so the derivation has to live somewhere. One residual smell worth naming without acting on it here: `id_flags` is a pre-joined string used UNQUOTED (`devcontainer exec … $DEVCONTAINER_ID_FLAGS`), safe only by the whitespace-free construction the tests pin at tests/test_devcontainer_names.py:279 — a Python caller should prefer `id_labels` and never re-split the string.
- **`mod-doc_refs`** — `mod-doc_refs-1` No PINNED tool in this repo reads a backtick code span as a file citation — the module's own docstring claim (doc_refs.py:5-7) is still true at rumdl 0.2.63 and agnix 0.52.1, verified in their source/docs rather than assumed. The only tool that does (agentlinter 2.3.0, unpinned) would be a strictly worse swap here: it resolves by filesystem existence with no git-tracked model (the exact local/CI divergence finding 2 exists to catch), has no basename/suffix resolution — so this repo's dominant `ci.yml`-style bare citation (~60 of ~100 refs, doc_refs.py:14-15) would be reported broken — and offers no per-entry justified allowlist like `_ALLOWED_ABSENT`/`_ALLOWED_PREFIXES` (doc_refs.py:90-186). Adopting it means a new npm dependency that reports more false positives and fewer true ones. `mod-doc_refs-2` The native closed-world mechanism exists but only for markdown link syntax, and only if the ref set is fed as documents on stdin — it cannot see the backtick citations this repo actually writes, and the closed world it builds is over the SUPPLIED DOCUMENTS, not over the tracked-file universe that a citation like `.github/workflows/ci.yml` must resolve against. Retiring the custom check would reopen exactly the divergence it was written for. Worth revisiting only if the repo ever converts backtick citations to real markdown links (hk.pkl:361-363 records that rumdl adoption is deferred behind a 591-finding burn-down, so that is not near-term). `mod-doc_refs-4` Both citation forms this repo actually uses are structurally outside every pinned linter's scope: agnix only reads a frontmatter array in agent files (this repo's citations are prose in rules/AGENTS.md), and wikilinks are explicitly out of scope for rumdl and entirely absent from agnix. The rules-plus-skills resolution set (`[[zero-skip-policy]]` is a RULE, doc_refs.py:428-431) is repo-specific and has no native analogue at all — a skills-only native checker would report every wikilink in `.claude/rules/` as broken.
- **`mod-docker`** — `mod-docker-6` Required justification: the one native mechanism that would give us the atomic write (`doppler secrets download <path>`) encrypts its output, so it cannot feed `runArgs --env-file`; `--no-file` to stdout is the only usable native shape, and that leaves the caller owning the write. fnox's doppler provider enumerates secrets one declared name at a time and so cannot express "inject this whole config", which is what the container needs. The remaining custom surface — per-workspace+arch filename (#893), 0o600-at-creation, temp+rename, and the empty-download guard that reproduces the old `&& [ -s … ] &&` — has no native equivalent at today's pins (doppler 3.76.5, @devcontainers/cli 0.89.0). `mod-docker-8` Required justification: no tool in the stack extracts the host agent's public keys and stages them for a container's sshd. The macOS-specific half is genuinely un-substitutable — a GUI-launched or hook-spawned process does not inherit the launchd SSH_AUTH_SOCK (the same class as do-not.md #1), so the `/bin/launchctl getenv` recovery, and its hostile-output validation (single line, absolute path), exist because nothing else can produce a working agent env there. The module is already mounted in the native `initializeCommand` slot, which is the correct adoption of the devcontainer lifecycle; only the key logic is ours, per zero-bash-logic. `mod-docker-9` Required justification: R1 is a project-specific invariant (a passwordless host->container login landing as the HOST user on a per-workspace derived port); no upstream tool asserts it. The load-bearing part is the identity assertion — `lines[-1] != user` — which is what makes this a gate rather than a connectivity ping, and which nothing native offers. It also deliberately reuses `_ssh_agent_environment()` so the probe authenticates through the same agent that staged the key, closing the control-arm hole where a probe could pass on a different agent than the one under test.
- **`mod-doctor`** — `mod-doctor-4` The native warning is explicitly scoped to the no-default form. The defect this check was built for (#418) is the OPPOSITE form — `${CONTEXT7_API_KEY:-}` — where the default makes an absent variable a legal empty string, the server starts, reports connected, and serves an anonymous tier. Claude Code documents that shape as the recommended FIX for its own warning ('add a ${VAR:-default} fallback'), so adopting the native warning would retire the check for exactly the input it exists to catch. Keep it, and keep the ':-' branch of _INTERPOLATION_RE as the load-bearing part. `mod-doctor-7` Both native checks are about PATH ORDER and shim shadowing; neither compares the VERSION embedded in a PATH entry against the active pin, which is the drift this check exists for (a shell resolving hk 1.52.0 while the pin is 1.54.0 is perfectly ordered and unshadowed). Claude Code's /doctor PATH check is about its own duplicate installs. Keeping it also preserves the capture/blindness seam, which no external tool can supply because `mise doctor` invoked through mise sees a repaired PATH just as `mise run <task>` does. `mod-doctor-8` Required justification: both checks assert a REPO POLICY (a reviewed decision must live in the tracked settings file; a server's tool set must not be able to change between sessions), and no native mechanism has an opinion about either. The pin check is also load-bearing for the guard-coverage check — an unpinned spec makes the declared tool list unfalsifiable — so retiring one would quietly weaken the other. `mod-doctor-9` Required justification: every native doctor validates SHAPE (does this file parse, is this install healthy, is a hook slow). None of them can hold a project-specific REVIEWED BASELINE — that the fnox env mode is `true` with these 56 names, that .agents/skills/graphify/SKILL.md still carries 'DELIBERATE STUB', that the root AGENTS.md does not carry the vendor installer's append, that a scope declaration matches the roots the harness will actually send. Nor can they assert that a specific SessionStart hook's delegate (kb_setup.currency) is importable rather than merely written, which is precisely the gap workflow.tool-currency-wiring's text grep cannot see. The fail-open + record-the-crash contract is also unavailable natively: `claude doctor` is a separate command, not a per-session non-blocking report.
- **`mod-env_blob_scan`** — `mod-env_blob_scan-2` REQUIRED JUSTIFICATION: no scanner in this repo's toolchain decompresses. `grep -rn 'compress/zlib\|compress/gzip' <gitleaks tree> --include=*.go` returns 0 hits; control arm `grep -rn 'encoding/base64'` on the same tree with the same command shape returns 3 hits (detect/codec/base64.go:4, cmd/generate/config/rules/jwt.go:4, sentry.go:4), so the zero is a real negative, not a blind probe. Even with `--max-decode-depth` enabled, base64.go's `isPrintableASCII` guard drops the blob before any rule sees it. The module's own measurement (0 findings for both scanners on the compressed form, non-zero on the plaintext) is the matching two-arm evidence on the runtime side. This capability stays custom. `mod-env_blob_scan-5` REQUIRED JUSTIFICATION: adopting hk's `{{files}}` here would be a regression, not a modernization. The whole-tracked-tree scan is the gate's stated design (hk.pkl:300-306) and it is the only layer that re-checks files already committed — a dump that landed while the gate was absent, or via a path the pre-commit hook was skipped on, is caught on the next full run and would be invisible to a changed-files-only step. hk offers no native 'scan the whole tracked tree' primitive that also reads `git ls-files` (the sibling gitleaks builtin works around the same problem by hard-coding `.` and ignoring hk's list — see hk/pkl/builtins/gitleaks.pkl:13-17), so the enumeration stays custom. The `--paths` argument already exists for callers that want the narrow form.
- **`mod-eval_cases`** — `mod-eval_cases-2` Justification, not a default: the questions these cases ask — does a named lane CLI resolve on PATH, does a SHA-pinned dependency actually contain the module the pin promises, does the pinned CLI dispatch a subcommand, does the local graph return a non-empty answer — are deterministic host-environment assertions with no LLM in the loop. skill-creator's eval loop is an LLM-graded A/B over skill prompts and cannot express any of them, and nothing in `claude plugin` runs a user-supplied case table. Keeping the harness is also cheap: the runner is the shared `kb_setup.evals`, so only the cases are per-repo. `mod-eval_cases-3` Both native surfaces require an interactive session and a real tool call, and both report what a hook DID rather than asserting what it MUST decide — they cannot run in a ship gate and cannot carry a must-ALLOW half. The must-ALLOW half is the load-bearing one here (2 of this guard's 3 all-time denials were false positives, eval_cases.py:86-91), and no native mechanism grades false positives at all. The one genuine overlap is with `tests/test_hook_guard.py`, which already parametrizes ~35 pytest cases over the same `decide` — but that is duplication with pytest, not supersession by a native harness feature, and the eval table adds the ship-time (non-pytest) run via pr.py:352. `mod-eval_cases-4` `mise ls --missing` is structurally unable to answer this case: the interesting lane is `grok`, which is DELIBERATELY not declared in mise.toml (.claude/CLAUDE.md's 'There is no grok here' section), so mise would report nothing missing while the doctrine still names it — the exact silent-pass shape #354 cost. And the second half of the assertion is a documentation reconcile (does the doc state the degradation path?), which no tool models. The plugin doctor covers auth for INSTALLED lanes only and is already a separate live case. Keeping this case is justified; the only defensible narrowing would be to source DECLARED_LANES from the doctrine doc rather than a literal tuple, which is a maintenance change, not a native adoption. `mod-eval_cases-5` A resolver check answers 'do the declared versions install and agree'; these cases answer 'does the artifact the pin points at contain the entry point we call'. #391 is the proof the two differ — the pin resolved and installed cleanly while `mise run cc` had never once worked. `uv pip check` would have stayed green throughout. The launcher probe additionally encodes a discrimination fact no tool knows (rc=2 in both directions, so only the handler's own marker string separates 'dispatched' from 'unknown command'), which is exactly the custom knowledge a native check cannot carry. `mod-eval_cases-6` `graphify hook status` grades the WIRING (are the assistant hooks installed), which is the tier-0 question this case explicitly refuses to settle for; the case's whole point (eval_cases.py:363-367) is that `rc=0` with empty output is 'a graph that reads as healthy and knows nothing'. No graphify command expresses a non-empty-answer assertion, and the two custom parts that make the case honest — a present-but-meaningless `graph.json` as the control fixture, and a host-only precondition so the in-container run SKIPs rather than fails — are repo-specific facts no upstream tool can supply.
- **`mod-gcc_sha`** — `mod-gcc_sha-1` Justification (not a default): upstream kayari.org publishes no checksum or signature, so the sha is a locally-computed integrity pin that only a fetch-and-hash step can produce. Every native mechanism in the stack either supplies a version (Renovate datasource) or verifies a supplied sha (sha256sum -c at .devcontainer/Dockerfile:611, contracted by python/verification/suites.toml:351-359) — nothing closes the loop between the two. The module is also already the minimal shape the repo's rules ask for: subprocess curl as the blessed fetcher, an injectable seam for tests, and a strict rewrite count.
- **`mod-ghcr`** — `mod-ghcr-3` Required justification: no CLI, API or linter in the pinned toolchain answers 'does this token's granted scope set imply write:packages/workflow?'. gh's closure is narrower than what GHCR publishing needs and is unreachable from outside the Go binary; the REST API returns the granted scopes only, never their closure. The table is small, documented against the GitHub scope docs (ghcr.py:71) and control-armed in tests, so it stays — but it should be fed by the header from mod-ghcr-1 rather than by scraped display text. `mod-ghcr-7` Required justification: the value here is the COMPOSITION and its verdict shape, which no single native command produces — plus the honest negative recorded in the `note` field (the package's Actions repository allowlist is not cleanly exposed through the gh API), which is knowledge no tool encodes. Keep the orchestration and the `_run`/`_run_gh_json` seams; the pieces that should change are the ones named in findings 1, 2, 4 and 5, all of which leave this skeleton intact. Caveat for whoever acts on this: every existing test drives the module through monkeypatched seams (tests/test_ghcr.py:67, :128-129), so per .claude/rules/real-integration-evidence.md there is currently no real invocation proving the composition works end to end.
- **`mod-ghcr_cleanup`** — `mod-ghcr_cleanup-1` GitHub's own action has exactly one keep-N per package and no positive tag selector, so it cannot express three simultaneous, independent newest-3 windows inside a single package (dotfiles-devcontainer). Running it three times is impossible because there is no way to say 'only consider base-* versions' — `ignore-versions` can only subtract, and subtracting the other two families still leaves ONE global counter over the remainder plus the `:sha`/`:pr-` tags the module deliberately holds out of scope (ghcr_cleanup.py:80-82). The custom planner is therefore not a reinvention of this action; it computes something the action has no input for. `mod-ghcr_cleanup-2` This action is the closest native fit and still does not cover the unit. Three blockers, each independently disqualifying: (1) the workflow authenticates with `secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN` (.github/workflows/ghcr-cleanup.yml:65,89), a temporal token, and the README states filtering operators — which is exactly the `image-tags: 'base-*'` selector the per-family scheme depends on — do not work with temporal tokens; adopting it means provisioning and rotating a PAT or GitHub App token with packages:delete, a strictly larger credential blast radius than the current read-mostly GITHUB_TOKEN. (2) `keep-n-most-recent` is per package, so three families need three invocations, and each invocation is blind to the others: a version tagged with two families (ghcr_cleanup.py:79-92, asserted by tests/test_ghcr_cleanup.py::test_multi_tag_version_kept_while_any_family_window_open) would be deleted by the pass whose window has closed even though the other family's window is still open. (3) `cut-off` is a required input, so the action cannot express a pure count-based policy. Keeping the ~45-line pure planner is cheaper and safer than the token escalation plus a three-pass approximation that is wrong on the multi-tag case.
- **`mod-graph_bakeoff`** — `mod-graph_bakeoff-4` Required justification: no tool in the host's version set does multi-model extraction comparison with provenance. graphify neither stamps model identity into its artifacts nor keys its semantic cache on it, so the fresh-directory isolation and the manifest are load-bearing compensations for a gap in the tool, not reinventions of it; the null arm / noise floor / significance rule and the answer-key decoy scoring are experimental-design decisions no CLI provides. Two sub-parts that look reinvented but are correct as written and should NOT be 'modernized': gather_versions() shells out to `graphify --version` rather than using importlib.metadata.version('graphifyy') as graphify.py:81 does, and that is right — the harness runs the PATH binary as a subprocess, so the PATH binary's version is the honest attribution (importlib would record the in-process package, the exact two-install drift graphify-first.md warns about); and execute_matrix is sequential on purpose, so a parallel-runner 'improvement' would make the seconds column measure contention. One gap noted without proposing a native fix: `bakeoff` has zero occurrences in python/verification/suites.toml (control arm: 'graphify' -> hits at suites.toml:1833,1854), so nothing contractually binds the mise task to the module.
- **`mod-graphify`** — `mod-graphify-4` Justification, not a default. Two independent reasons the native path is refused here. (1) Project policy: this is lane 2 — our own lookups — where `.claude/rules/do-not.md` #11 and `.claude/rules/research-doc-sources.md` § "MCP: two lanes" require the tool's CLI first and treat native MCP registration as a documented last resort; a registered graphify server would buy a call the existing CLI already makes. (2) The wrappers are not a thin re-expression of the CLI: query() gates on graph health BEFORE spawning, re-reads health AFTER and compares graph_sha256 so an answer computed against a graph that changed mid-run is rejected (graphify.py:325-349), and it treats any stderr as incomplete evidence — the `.claude/rules/graphify-first.md` fall-back-to-source contract. graphify's MCP surface has no equivalent of that stability gate, so adopting it would lose the property the wrapper exists for. `mod-graphify-5` Justification, not a default. The wrapper's whole value is the one thing upstream does not expose: the nudge text is three literal json.dumps payloads at cli.py:18/28/42 with no flag, env var or file that changes the wording, so `mise run graphify-query` cannot be named without post-processing. Adopting the native installer would make it worse rather than better — a project-scoped `graphify install` emits a BARE `graphify` hook command resolved at run time (CHANGELOG.md 0.9.52, "emits a bare `graphify` hook command resolved at run time instead of pinning the absolute interpreter path"), which is precisely the bare-PATH invocation `.claude/rules/graphify-first.md` forbids here because two graphify installs exist on this machine, and `.claude/rules/do-not.md` #8 bans running graphify's installer against this repo at all. Only the strict-mode toggle is genuinely native, and scripts/graphify-hook-guard.sh:16-18 already documents that it is an env var to be set in settings.json rather than code. `mod-graphify-8` Justification, not a default. Nothing upstream answers "may I consume this graph's answers as evidence", and the verdict is load-bearing for a repo rule rather than cosmetic: `.claude/rules/graphify-first.md` requires that missing/stale/corrupt/version-drift states be declared unavailable and fall back to source, never silently rendered as an empty or complete answer, and query()/affected() enforce that by raising before any subprocess runs. The three near-miss native commands each answer a narrower question and none of them gates evidence consumption. The parts of this unit that ARE superseded are reported separately as mod-graphify-1 (the hard-coded version operand), mod-graphify-2 (the receipt branch) and mod-graphify-6 (the missing source-staleness signal); the gate itself stays.
- **`mod-graphify_skill`** — `mod-graphify_skill-4` Justification, not a default: the native installer's confinement gap is real and unconditional at project scope (install.py:640-665 runs whenever cfg['claude_md'] is true, --project or not), and no harness feature substitutes -- Claude Code installs skills from a directory or a marketplace plugin, and graphify publishes neither. What must stay repo-owned is therefore the CONFINEMENT and the CLI/task/gate surface; findings 1-3 say the resolution and copy MECHANICS inside it should be delegated to graphify's own _platform_skill_destination/_copy_skill_file rather than mirrored, which also retires the drift the module's docstring claims is impossible.
- **`mod-handoff_check`** — `mod-handoff_check-2` Justification, not a default. Three independent mismatches, each cited: (a) SHAPE — every native checker extracts markdown LINKS (`[text](url)`) or bare URLs; a handoff cites `python/src/dotfiles_setup/lint.py:42-58` as prose, which parsers/markdown.rs:133-136 cannot see at all. (b) CORPUS — agnix deliberately refuses generic markdown and names 'plans' as the excluded class (imports.rs:232-234), and `.agent/plans/session-*.md` is gitignored, so hk (a git-hook system operating on staged/tracked files) can never hand it to lychee either. (c) CAPABILITY — no link checker validates a LINE RANGE against the target file's length, which is the half that actually rots (a cited file usually survives; the line number does not). So nothing native covers it and the custom code stays. The only thing worth adopting from the native side is nothing here — leave _path_findings as is. `mod-handoff_check-3` Justification: planning-with-files owns a fixed, different file set (`task_plan.md` / `findings.md` / `progress.md` in the project root) and its catchup script reads harness session records; neither reads `.agent/plans/session-<date><letter>.md`, which is this repo's own convention fixed by .claude/rules/agent-artifact-conventions.md. Claude Code's `--resume`/`/rewind` restore a TRANSCRIPT, not a repo-relative handoff document, and cannot rank two same-day handoffs by letter suffix. There is no native selector for a project-defined filename convention, so the 17-line selector stays. It is also the cheapest half of the module to keep correct — its ordering is already regression-pinned by a test.
- **`mod-heredoc`** — `mod-heredoc-2` 'Which command consumes this redirect, and does it execute the body?' is a SEMANTIC question about argv-tail-exec wrappers, not a syntactic one, so no parser answers it — the live probe above shows the best available parser collapsing `env bash` into one command node. That is the required justification for keeping custom code under .claude/rules/use-tool-builtins.md rule 3. TWO CAVEATS worth carrying forward as defects, not as dispositions: (1) _PREFIX_WORDS (heredoc.py:63-65) omits the argv-tail-exec wrappers `env`, `timeout`, `stdbuf`, `nice`, `ionice` — measured: workflow_hooks.git_write_subcommands("env bash <<'SH'\ngit push\nSH\n") and the `timeout 30 bash <<'SH'` form both return set(), i.e. the shell-executed body IS redacted and the git write is MISSED, which is exactly the under-detect direction heredoc.py:95-99 says must never be traded for; the `bash`/`xargs -I{} bash` control arms return {'push'}, so the probe discriminates. (2) the recorded justification for the whole pair (hook_guard.py:583-604) should name ast-grep explicitly now that it is pinned, or the next reviewer cannot tell 'we checked' from 'we never looked'. `mod-heredoc-3` Named separately so it is not silently folded into mod-heredoc-1's 'no correctness gain' claim: this IS a real limit of the custom regex, and it is the reason to state precisely that adopting the native parser would not fix it — the pinned native parser reproduces the same omission on the same input. Nothing native supersedes this capability, so the custom code stays; the residual risk is bounded because the miss is in the OVER-detect direction for both consumers (unredacted text is read as commands, producing a loud false positive rather than a silent miss), which is the direction heredoc.py:95-99 explicitly prefers. If the stacked-heredoc shape ever appears in a real transcript or workflow run: block, and file it against the regex rather than against the parser choice.
- **`mod-hk_builtins_audit`** — `mod-hk_builtins_audit-2` Required justification: the fact being audited — 'this step was derived from a builtin' — exists only in the config's SOURCE TEXT. hk drops it during evaluation (Config.Step carries no builtin field) and exposes it through no CLI at the 1.57.0 pin, and the 1.58.1 gap digest reports zero new hk capabilities (.agent/kb/raw/hk-releases-since-pin.digest.md, 'None ... documentation-only release'). A text regex is therefore the only route, and this one is already anchored against the one false-positive shape the module measured. Note this is the opposite conclusion from finding -1: step NAMES are structural and should come from evaluation; builtin PROVENANCE is not, and must not. `mod-hk_builtins_audit-5` Required justification: no tool in the stack answers 'which of hk's builtins does THIS repo wire, where, and which did it decline on purpose' — hk exposes the two halves (the builtin list, the config) but never joins them, and the join is what makes the doc falsifiable. The gate's value is measured, not asserted: the hand-written predecessor claimed betterleaks ran as a second secret scanner while it was wired nowhere (hk.pkl:313-317 records the 0-vs-1 measurement against a control). Keep the unit; findings -1, -3 and -4 are the three seams inside it that should adopt native mechanisms.
- **`mod-hook_guard`** — `mod-hook_guard-4` Justification (required): the harness gives a hook the raw command string and nothing else, so any hook that must reason about command position has to parse the string itself; the three off-the-shelf parsers were probed and each fails on the exact shape this masker exists for (heredoc bodies and quoted separators). tree-sitter-bash remains the documented upgrade path if richer shell constructs ever matter — that is the only route by which this could later become a 'refactor'. Nothing at the host's pinned versions changes this. `mod-hook_guard-5` Justification (required): the self-learning loop this field serves — mine transcripts for one-off commands the guard does not yet cover, and distinguish a bypass from history — has no counterpart in Claude Code, codex-cli, or any linter in the pin set (agnix / claude-code-lint / cclint / agents-lint check configuration files, not runtime command history). The dated table is also what makes the guard auditable at all, and the module documents (hook_guard.py:562-573) why any rule whose verdict depends on live repo state would break that replay. Nothing to adopt. `mod-hook_guard-6` Justification (required): the unit's value is the REASON, and the reason is a hook-only capability at the host's version — a deny rule removes the call silently and an ask rule interrupts the human, neither of which teaches the agent which mise task to run. `updatedInput` is the one native mechanism that could subsume some redirects, but silently rewriting a command the operator asked for trades a teachable deny for an invisible substitution, and the guard's own doctrine (a redirect that misfires erodes trust) argues against it for a 17-rule table with negative lookaheads (`_GH_REPO_NOT_FOREIGN`) that permission-rule glob syntax cannot express. Keep the table; findings 1-3 are where native mechanisms should be added ALONGSIDE it.
- **`mod-hook_selfcheck`** — `mod-hook_selfcheck-4` Required justification: the #343 failure mode is a property of the COMMAND STRING relative to the session's cwd, and no shipped linter or harness command models it — the one rule that touches hook script paths normalises the defect away. Keep, and treat as a hardening item rather than a modernization one: the live settings.json anchors with `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` (.claude/settings.json PreToolUse/SessionStart/SessionEnd/InstructionsLoaded/PostToolUse commands), and the `:-.` fallback re-opens exactly #343 whenever the variable is unset, while the substring check at hook_selfcheck.py:271 passes on it. Tightening the check to reject a `:-.`-style default would be a real gain and is not available natively. `mod-hook_selfcheck-7` Required justification: every native mechanism found describes or validates what IS configured; none of them can express 'this repository requires these five events, wired to these commands, with these exact matcher tokens'. That requirement is the whole point of the unit — it is the layer that caught #343 (guard silently absent off-root) and the `Edit` ⊂ `NotebookEdit` substring hole that a containment check in tests/test_mise_config_context.py could not see (hook_selfcheck.py:114-130). Keeping it is not a default: the two adjacent capabilities it also carries ARE superseded or duplicated (findings -1 and -2), and its structural/shape half should be delegated (finding -3), leaving _SETTINGS_WIRING plus _unanchored_hooks as the irreducible core.
- **`mod-image`** — `mod-image-10` Required justification: these are project-specific MODELS and POLICIES, not generic capabilities. `classify_layer_source`'s buckets are this image's five toolchains; `estimate_pull_time_s` is a declared estimate with this project's bandwidth/zstd assumptions echoed back in the payload; `decide_analysis_target` encodes a GitHub-platform fact (`workflow_run.pull_requests[]` is empty on same-repo PR runs) that no tool exposes as a feature. Nothing in mise, hk, uv, gh, docker, renovate, graphify, the pinned linters, or the Claude Code / codex-cli gap digests offers layer-to-toolchain attribution, a pull-time model, or benchmark-delta rendering. The parts that DO have native answers are already delegating to them. `mod-image-7` Required justification: the check's whole value is that the EXPECTED set is derived independently of the mise instance being tested — asking mise for both sides would make the tier-1 tool-set diff tautological, and there is no mise interface that answers the selector question for a non-host architecture anyway (OS/ARCH are compile/process constants, not settings). Two maintenance corrections that follow from the current source: (a) all three docstring citations are STALE — the mirrored functions no longer live in `toolset/tool_request.rs`, they are `cli/version.rs:65-89`, and a mirror pointed at the wrong file drifts silently; (b) mise's `normalize_arch` returns the token UNCHANGED for an unrecognised arch while `_normalize_tool_arch` returns `None` — the outcomes agree today only because a token mise leaves unchanged can never equal `x64`/`arm64`, which is worth pinning in a test rather than left as coincidence.
- **`mod-image_lock`** — `mod-image_lock-3` Justification, not a default: the native setting cannot replace this computation for two reasons that are both documented and both measured here. (1) It names EXACT platforms — `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64` — while the image genuinely needs the variant entries mise writes beneath them (`linux-x64-musl`, `linux-x64-baseline`, `linux-arm64-musl`); the module measured that an exact-name intersection clips those (hk 6 -> 2, uv 8 -> 2, image_lock.py:150-156), and the native no-`--platform` path resolves to the same exact-name set, so adopting it would reproduce the clipping and then be refused by the coverage check. (2) mise's authoritative set always adds `Platform::current()` (lockfile.rs:2558-2560), i.e. the RESOLVING host's platform, which is exactly the macOS contamination #698/2026-08-27 pruned out of these locks. The one native piece is already adopted — the bound is read from mise's own `lockfile_platforms` declaration rather than a second private list — which is the right seam. Worth noting for a future pass: platform_target.py:255 re-parses that setting with a regex instead of asking mise (`mise settings get lockfile_platforms`), which is a smaller, separable adoption in that unit. `mod-image_lock-4` The native mechanism is already the one in use; the only custom parts are the https-scheme assertion (the bytes are piped to `sh`, so an http:// or file:// override would be a code-execution primitive — image_lock.py:207-213) and the post-condition that the install path actually exists (:253-255, the build-time self-check pattern). Neither is provided by the installer, and the version pin is not optional because mise lock formats are not cross-version compatible (:232-236), so a `mise` already on PATH cannot be substituted. `mod-image_lock-5` The native tool is already the one invoked; the custom surface is only the argv assembly (id-label resolution, the --no-container recursion terminator, and the `mise exec --` wrapper), and its shape is load-bearing rather than incidental — the docstring at :352-363 records that generalising it for lock_shared broke because `mise exec --` with MISE_IGNORED_CONFIG_PATHS cleared resolves the entire declared toolset and dies attesting host-only tools. A retire would need a native cross-architecture exec that does not exist at these pins. Note it is already factored so lock_shared reuses the prefix rather than copying it, which is the correct wrap of the native mechanism.
- **`mod-image_manifest`** — `mod-image_manifest-1` The native tool cannot answer the question the module asks. `--raw` returns the document and `--format` runs a Go template over it, but neither selects a platform, so 'which digest does this ref serve for linux/amd64, ignoring attestations' has to be computed by the caller. The module is already the thinnest possible wrapper over the most native surface available (it uses `--raw` and buildx's own `{{json .Image}}` rather than re-implementing manifest fetching), and it deliberately does NOT assert the buildx `--prefer-index` default it reads through (image_manifest.py:40-45, :99-101), which is exactly the `use-tool-builtins.md` posture of depending on the capability and not on a vendor default. `mod-image_manifest-5` Required justification: no tool in the pin set publishes an assertion of the form 'this per-architecture tag and this index entry are the same manifest'. That relation is a property of THIS repo's split-push-then-merge design (build-publish.yml:1150-1247), which no upstream product models. The module is also the only place the gate's FAIL direction can exist — the step reads a registry only CI writes to (tests/test_image_manifest.py:3-6) — so retiring the python layer would return the project to the pre-#703 state where a check that could only fail shipped green-adjacent for weeks. Findings 2, 3 and 4 are the improvements; the unit itself stays.
- **`mod-instructions_observer`** — `mod-instructions_observer-1` Required justification: the harness emits the event but persists nothing. Its own docs point at exactly this hook for this job, the OTel surface (the only machine-readable native channel) has no instructions event, and every native inspector (/context, /doctor, /skill-doctor) is interactive and single-session, so none of them can answer 'which rule never fired across N sessions'. The module already adopts the native seams it can: the documented payload field names verbatim, and $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR (instructions_observer.py:89-105) instead of cwd. `mod-instructions_observer-3` Required justification: the native matcher exists and was already evaluated and deliberately rejected in-tree — the never-fired report needs the complete baseline, so every load_reason is wanted and a matcher would only subtract records (python/src/dotfiles_setup/hook_selfcheck.py:105-108 records exactly that reasoning, with `None` matchers asserted as intentional). The matcher also cannot express the one filter that would cut work (scope: `memory_type` User/Managed), because it binds `load_reason` only. Nothing to change; this finding exists so a later audit does not re-propose the matcher. `mod-instructions_observer-4` Required justification: the only native part is the guarantee that a non-zero exit cannot hurt, which the module does not depend on anyway; the parts that matter — silent stdout/stderr and a durable record of WHY a line was dropped — have no native counterpart at these pins, and the nearest one (OTel hook_execution_complete) is count-only and needs an exporter that is not configured here. Deleting any of it would trade a real diagnostic for nothing. No change. `mod-instructions_observer-5` Required justification: the native http hook type exists and is genuinely cheaper per load, but it requires a resident local collector — a new always-on process, a port, a lifecycle, and a failure mode (connection refused = silently no records) strictly worse than the current fail-open spawn, for a measured saving of ~66-86ms per load on a hook the harness runs asynchronously. Trade is not worth it at this repo's scale; revisit only if the observer is ever measured to delay session start. The cheap win is finding -2 (`--no-sync`), not a transport change.
- **`mod-instructions_report`** — `mod-instructions_report-2` Justification required, so stated explicitly: the native surface answers a strictly narrower question. `/context` / `getContextUsage()` is a snapshot of ONE live session, reports no `load_reason` (so it cannot separate `session_start` from `path_glob_match`/`include`/`compact`, which is the whole partition this module exists for), and is reachable only from inside a running interactive session or an SDK query — not from a batch `mise run instructions-report` over historical JSONL. What the native side has and the custom side lacks is the per-file TOKEN COST; that is the one thing worth borrowing (report the `tokens` field alongside the eager list if a future ticket wires an SDK read), which is why this is not a plain 'nothing exists'. `mod-instructions_report-3` Justification required: the dead-glob question is only answerable from OBSERVED loads accumulated across sessions, and nothing in the harness persists or aggregates InstructionsLoaded events — the event is explicitly documented as fire-and-forget observability with the exit code ignored, i.e. the storage and the query are the integrator's job. `/skill-doctor` proves Anthropic ships this analysis natively for skills, which makes a rules equivalent a plausible future supersession — hence the probe, to be re-run at each Claude Code bump rather than assumed absent forever. `mod-instructions_report-4` Justification required: the harness hands out one event per load and explicitly stops there, so anything that answers 'across N sessions, which rules fired / never fired' has to be built. The custom code is also carrying two judgments no generic tool would make — malformed lines are COUNTED not dropped (:150-158), and the absence claim is coverage-gated by DISTINCT SESSIONS rather than events (:61-78, a documented false-positive this module already tripped over). The one deliberate duplication (`_RECORDS_DIRNAME`/`_ERROR_LOG_NAME` copied rather than imported from `instructions_observer`, :51-56) is justified in place by the observer's stdlib-only hot-path contract C1 and should stay; it is a different case from finding 1, where the duplicate carries actual parsing LOGIC.
- **`mod-lint`** — `mod-lint-3` Required justification: the only native piece is the pair of env vars, and the module already consumes them. The concurrency-safety property this code exists for (two clones or two windows on one host must not overwrite each other's debug log, while `long-running-command-hangs.md` rule 2 still has one predictable name to read) is a property of the CALLER choosing distinct HK_LOG_FILE values — hk cannot provide it, because hk sees exactly one path per invocation. No rotation or retention exists in hk to delegate the pruning to, and mise offers nothing here either (its task `env` is static/Tera-templated and cannot inject the runtime pid). `mod-lint-4` Required justification: this is the exact reason mise.toml:207-212 already records for retaining the wrapper under the native 700s backstop, and it re-verifies at the current pins. Without it a hang produces `timed out after 700s` and nothing about WHICH step wedged — which is the whole diagnostic content of the 7h incident in `.claude/rules/long-running-command-hangs.md`, and what rule 7 (`grep for a step with no matching completion`) depends on. The 124 convention likewise has no native producer: mise's timeout exits with its generic error code, so a caller cannot tell a hang from a red gate. `mod-lint-5` Required justification: `--all` is load-bearing, not incidental — `.claude/rules/ci-local-parity.md` and the module docstring require `mise run lint` to check exactly what CI's `hk run check --all` checks, and a `--unstaged`/`--pr` narrowing would make the local gate weaker than the CI gate while still reporting green. The new flags are a genuine opportunity, but for a DIFFERENT, additional fast task (an agent-scoped pre-flight), never as a substitute inside this gate. Nothing here is superseded.
- **`mod-lint_delta`** — `mod-lint_delta-5` REQUIRED JUSTIFICATION: no linter in this stack ships a baseline/delta mode, so the attribution question ("is this wall of diagnostics mine or the bump's?") has no native answer at the pinned versions. The unit is also already native-first where a native mechanism exists: it runs the off-pin version through `uvx <tool>@<version>` (lint_delta.py:220-239) rather than hand-installing, derives the baseline from git rather than remembering it, and keeps every seam (tool, baseline, paths, runner, lockfile) as a parameter with this repo's case as the DEFAULT — the reusable-by-parameter shape agent-artifact-conventions.md rule 6 asks for. The load-bearing part is the REFUSAL, not the report: a version compared against itself can only ever print 'no change', and printing that as a clean bill is the one-faced probe probes-need-a-control-arm.md exists to reject. Findings 1-4 are internal adoptions of native mechanisms inside this unit; none of them removes the unit. Caveat on scope, not on disposition: 0.85 rather than higher because the marketplace/plugin surface was probed only through the offline corpus and the ten gap digests, not through a live registry search — a third-party 'lint baseline' plugin could exist without appearing there.
- **`mod-listing_budget`** — `mod-listing_budget-5` Adopting the native record would REGRESS the module. Cross-check on this host: `claude plugin list --json` reports antigravity 0.23.0 and planning-with-files 3.12.0 for this repo's projectPath, while `claude plugin details` resolves 0.26.0 and 3.17.2 — which is what this session actually loaded and what plugin_root's version-max rule returns. That is the identical per-project staleness the docstring already recorded for installed_plugins.json, reproduced through a different, official surface. Control arm: the same JSON is CORRECT for mattpocock-skills 1.2.3, fable-orchestrator 1.21.0 and codex 1.0.6, so the probe discriminates rather than being uniformly wrong. `claude plugin details` agrees on the version but prints no path, so no native surface currently yields a trustworthy install path. Keep the version-max rule; re-test when the CLI exposes a path that agrees with the loaded version.
- **`mod-lock_integrity`** — `mod-lock_integrity-1` Nothing native answers the question this gate asks — 'did the committed lockfile lose platform coverage?'. mise has no lockfile-verify command, `mise doctor` does not look at lockfiles, hk has no lockfile builtin, and the damage class (same tool count, fewer platform entries; #370 measured 226 -> 226 tool blocks while 548 lines of linux conda entries vanished) is invisible to any version- or tool-level check including the repo's own test_lock_coverage.py. The gate is also deliberately artifact-shaped rather than command-shaped because mise.toml:101 sets `auto_install = true`, so any task can reach the destructive re-lock path and no command allowlist can bound it. `mod-lock_integrity-3` The exit code still cannot distinguish 'locked' from 'silently no-op', so validating the name against the config BEFORE shelling out is the only cheap discriminator, and it is what makes `mise run lock -- <name>` fail in milliseconds instead of appearing to succeed. Confidence is 0.8 rather than higher only because the read is of the 2026.9.0 corpus while the host runs 2026.9.3; the gap digest reports no releases newer than the host, so a behaviour change in those three patch releases is unlikely but not source-verified here. `mod-lock_integrity-4` The native listing would answer the question but requires mise to build and resolve the tool graph, and this repo has measured that path being fatal in exactly this context: with `auto_install = true` (mise.toml:101), a mise invocation in the lock family resolved the entire declared toolset before doing any work and died on host-only tools (python/verification/suites.toml:2255, the lock-shared round-1 failure). A pure tomllib read is also the only form that yields the literal config KEY string `mise lock` accepts (`aqua:jackchuka/mdschema`), which is precisely what the finding-3 validation must compare against; mise's short names would re-introduce the silent no-op. Custom code survives with that written justification per use-tool-builtins.md rule 6. `mod-lock_integrity-5` Adopting either native filter would put a hole in the gate, so the unglobbed shape is the correct one and should not be 'optimized'. The #370 signature is a stray `mise install`/bare `mise lock` that WRITES a lockfile and never stages it; a `glob` filters the staged set, so the step would skip precisely the unstaged damage the artifact comparison exists to catch. A `git.modified_files` condition is closer to correct but converts a always-runs gate into one whose firing depends on hk's own git-status classification — a fail-open failure mode on a gate whose entire value is catching a silent write. The only cost of the current shape is one cheap python run (four `git show` calls plus four regex passes) per hk invocation.
- **`mod-lock_refresh`** — `mod-lock_refresh-1` The native prune exists but is unreachable from this call site by construction: it fires only when `self.tool.is_empty()` (lock.rs:786-788), and this entrypoint MUST pass explicit tool names, because an unfiltered `mise lock` also locks task-scoped tools (docs/cli/lock.md:12,19) — the exact regression (#821) that lock-refresh-root exists to prevent. So at mise 2026.9.1/2026.9.3 the two native behaviours are mutually exclusive and the custom prune is the only way to have both. Keep, and treat 'a --prune flag that works with TOOL args' as the upstream feature request that would retire it. `mod-lock_refresh-2` Nothing native expresses 'lock the config's tools but not the tasks' tools'. Upstream moved the other way on purpose (#11976), so the explicit-argv filter is the only mechanism available, and deriving the names from mise.toml (rather than a second hard-coded inventory) is already the minimum-drift shape. `mod-lock_refresh-4` The native guard is strictly narrower on three axes and cannot replace this one: (a) it is intra-run — it compares against the lockfile mise itself just read, never against the git-committed baseline, so a run that already overwrote the working-tree lock is graded against its own damage, which is precisely what coverage_baseline's HEAD-first choice defends against; (b) it fires only when a stale VERSION prune would remove a platform-supporting entry, so a metadata-only refresh that drops platform entries at unchanged versions — the measured #648 shape, tool count and versions unmoved — produces no error; (c) it says nothing about conda-package family tables. Keeping the custom guard also keeps the refusal at the moment of overwrite (collect), which is the only point where a bad lock can reach the committed tree. `mod-lock_refresh-6` This is a 15-line single-source-of-truth read, not reinvented tooling: the pin has to live in the Dockerfile (the image build is what consumes it), and no native mechanism carries a Dockerfile ARG into a CI installer step. The alternative — restating the version in the workflow — is the drift this function prevents, and the fail-loud raise is what keeps a missing ARG from silently producing an unconsumable 'latest' lock.
- **`mod-lock_shared`** — `mod-lock_shared-4` Required justification: no native mise mechanism reports "this invocation locked nothing" — not the exit code (0), not `--json` (`[]` is ambiguous and additionally suppresses the message).
