The custom check stays, but it is a symptom sniff bound to upstream wording (the exact hazard .claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md rule 9 names), and it is mutually exclusive with `--json`. Two durable guards worth adding in the same breath: a comment at lock_shared.py:192 that `--json` must never be added to these argvs, and a positive assertion (mise's `✓ Lockfile written to` line, /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/mise/src/cli/lock.rs:558-563, or a pre/post content hash of `.config/mise/mise.lock`) so the gate requires evidence of work rather than only forbidding evidence of its absence. `mod-lock_shared-5` Required justification: the three behaviours this module is actually made of — (a) "a bare re-lock is destructive here" (#370), (b) "this name is declared in the SHARED fragment, not the root config", and (c) "this host cannot resolve linux assets, so refuse or route" — are all statements about THIS repo's two-config topology and this Mac's OS, and mise has no vocabulary for any of them. The one place a native mechanism could have eliminated custom code is asset resolution itself, and it has not: the aqua glibc-preference change that would be the candidate (`prefer glibc assets with musl fallback`, mise CHANGELOG.md:119 under `## [2026.8.9] - 2026-08-19`) landed BEFORE the 2026-08-27 measurement this module was built on, so it cannot be the fix. Caveat to carry forward: the offline mise changelog stops at 2026.9.0 (CHANGELOG.md:3) while the host runs 2026.9.3, so the 2026.9.1-2026.9.3 window is unread — the premise is unrefuted, not re-confirmed, at the host's exact version.
- **`mod-main`** — `mod-main-4` Required justification: nothing in mise, hk, uv, gh, Claude Code 2.1.266, codex-cli 0.152.1 or any pinned linter provides a multi-subcommand, typed, testable Python command surface — mise tasks are process wrappers that cannot own argument parsing, validation or a shared config object, and hk/uv only consume the exit code. The zero-bash-logic rule (.claude/rules/zero-bash-logic.md) actively requires this layer to exist in python/. Adopting a third-party CLI framework (click/typer) was NOT evaluated as a native alternative because it would add a runtime dependency to replace a stdlib module that already does the job once mod-main-1..3 are applied. The unit therefore stays, with the three argparse-native corrections above applied to it.
- **`mod-memory_index`** — `mod-memory_index-3` Required justification: the native mechanism and this checker answer opposite questions. Native asks 'is the index too long?' and tells Claude to shorten — which is precisely the operation that destroys index-only facts; nothing native asks 'will shortening this line lose a fact?'. The harness in fact makes the hazard WORSE by instructing a rewrite under size pressure, so the pre-trim survival check is the complement of the native warning rather than a duplicate of it. No linter in the pinned set (agnix 0.52.1, claude-code-lint 0.8.0, cclint, agents-lint 0.5.0, contextlint, ast-grep) has a rule over ~/.claude memory content, and the checker's calibration (narrow classes, prefix-tolerant shas, KB-means-knowledge-base exclusion) is repo-specific vocabulary no general tool would carry. `mod-memory_index-4` Required justification: deleting a memory has the same silent-loss shape as trimming one, and no native or third-party mechanism reads the auto-memory directory as a citation graph. The target tree lives outside the repo, which rules out every repo-scoped tool the project already pins (rumdl, markdownlint-cli2, mdschema, contextlint, graphify). The one caveat worth carrying forward is finding mod-memory_index-2: --refs inherits the same wrong-directory derivation, so a worktree invocation reports 'not a memory file' and rc=0. `mod-memory_index-5` Required justification: nothing native or pinned inspects the auto-memory directory's internal consistency, and the unparsed_lines check in particular is a coverage guard on this module's own regex — a class of self-check no external tool could provide because it is about what THIS parser could not read. Its value is unchanged by the harness's write-time budget warning, which says nothing about link resolution.
- **`mod-mise_config_context`** — `mod-mise_config_context-2` Required justification: the harness has no notion of 'inject this context at most once per session', and the two events that ARE once-per-session cannot see which file was edited. A grep of hooks.md for 'once per session\|only once\|deduplicat\|fires once' returns exactly three hits, none of them a budget mechanism -- and the one that speaks to the topic says the deduplication does not exist. So the marker-file layer is the whole of the capability, not a reinvention. Its fail-open-on-unwritable-marker posture is also the right way round and has no native equivalent to inherit. `mod-mise_config_context-4` Required justification: the vendor doc states the read-trigger limitation in as many words, so the module's premise is CONFIRMED against the native source rather than assumed -- a `paths:`-scoped rule cannot cover a blind Write, which is precisely the motivating case (the 2026-09-01 near-miss where a mise.toml decision was made without reading mise's docs). `InstructionsLoaded` is a read-side OBSERVER of the same mechanism (that is #917's use), not a write trigger. Nothing in the 2.1.258-2.1.266 gap digest or the llms-index digest adds a write-triggered instruction-loading path, and the llms-index digest reports the offline tree is current through the 2026-w34 What's New with zero new capability pages, so the negative here is armed rather than merely unfound. `mod-mise_config_context-5` Required justification: both natives were considered and neither is an improvement as the unit stands. `PostToolBatch` has NO matcher (hooks.md:2088), so adopting it trades a filtered spawn for an unconditional one on every batch -- strictly worse than finding 1's `if` filter -- and this repo already recorded that rejection once (docs/research/kb/reports/agents/2026-09-02-ticket-cut-advisor.md:152, "the `PostToolBatch` rejection"); re-deriving it here is a second, independent arrival at the same answer. `async: true` defers delivery to the next conversation turn, which for a reminder whose whole purpose is to land BEFORE the next mise-config turn is a real behavioural loss, and it would sit on top of a filter (finding 1) that already removes the spawn cost this would be buying. Revisit `async` only if the probe in finding 1 shows `if` cannot filter Write calls.
- **`mod-p2996_hash`** — `mod-p2996_hash-6` Justification, not a default: the native mechanism exists and does not reach this code. Every one of these three structs is CONSTRUCTED in-process by gather_*_inputs (p2996_hash.py:377, :435, :494) and never decoded from a serialized message, and msgspec constraints are decode-only by documented design. Porting to msgspec.Struct + Meta(pattern=...) would therefore delete the validation outright while looking like it declared it — a gate that can only pass, in the exact place the module says a bad value must raise rather than mint an unhittable cache tag (:238-241). msgspec's own escape hatch for this case is __post_init__ (structs.rst:150-170), i.e. the same hand-written check, so the port would buy nothing. The only genuinely native shape available is the one already in use: frozen dataclass + __post_init__. Worth one cleanup that is NOT a native swap — the 16-hex check at :167-176 is inlined instead of reusing a helper alongside _validate_hex_digest — but that is internal duplication, not superseded custom code. `mod-p2996_hash-7` Justification, not a default. (a) BuildKit's layer cache operates INSIDE a build: the ~80-120 min p2996 job would still have to start, pull its cache manifest and walk the graph. These hashes decide whether the GHA job runs at all — build-publish.yml probes the registry for the tag and short-circuits the whole leg (workflows/AGENTS.md:71-84). Layer cache also cannot express the property `:dev-<hash>` exists for: 'this exact content PASSED SMOKE', a marker pushed only after smoke-test, which is the entire reason a dev-probe hit is safe to skip validation on (p2996_hash.py:143-146). No BuildKit primitive carries a post-hoc validation verdict. (b) `hashFiles()` fingerprints whole files by glob and has no way to hash a SLICE of a file between sentinel comments — and section independence is the point of the design (the docstring's 'edit any Dockerfile line and the entire 2.5h pipeline rebuilds' anti-pattern), nor can it resolve a bake variable. It also runs only inside a GHA expression, while `mise run p2996-hash` must give an operator the same value locally. So the scheme stays. What findings 1-3 and 5 argue is narrower and unchanged by this: every INPUT it reads should be read through the tool that owns that input's grammar.
- **`mod-p2996_refresh`** — `mod-p2996_refresh-5` Justification (required, not a default): if finding 3 lands on option (b) — the module stays as the single writer of both files — then this fetch mechanism is the right one and should not be swapped for `gh api`. `git ls-remote` needs no token, no HTTP library, and no network in tests thanks to the `runner` seam, and it is the house pattern shared with `gcc_sha.py`. If finding 3 lands on option (a) this finding is moot because the module is deleted wholesale; it is recorded so that a future session choosing (b) does not 'modernize' the fetch into a `gh api` call and thereby introduce an auth dependency into a scheduled job.
- **`mod-parity`** — `mod-parity-2` Required justification: no harness, CLI, linter or CI feature at the host's versions observes TWO repository trees at once and asserts a declared set holds in both. The distribution mechanisms that could make the check unnecessary (plugin packaging, user-scope settings) each cover at most the plugins axis, and none can carry `.claude/rules/*.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` lines — the two axes that actually carry the doctrine. The CI-vs-local asymmetry (hard FAIL when the sibling checkout is missing) is policy no tool provides. Keep the module. `mod-parity-3` Required justification: the native mechanism exists and does NOT fit, for a stated design reason. Symlinking yields byte-identical rules, which is precisely what parity.toml:54-58 rejects — each rule is adapted per repo (knowledge-base's `local-devcontainer-first` is an ingestion-cost ladder; its `ci-local-parity` states `.github/` does not exist there), so a shared source would force one repo to carry the other's false statements. A symlink is also machine-local (`~/shared-claude-rules` is outside both clones), so it survives neither a fresh clone nor a CI checkout, while the gate's whole point is that CI can see the divergence. Keep the stem-presence check; do not convert the rules tree to symlinks. `mod-parity-4` Required justification: `InstructionsLoaded` is the STRONGER signal for the question 'is this doctrine actually in context', and it is already adopted for this repo (instructions_observer/instructions_report) — but it is per-session and per-machine. It cannot observe the sibling repo's sessions, and CI (where this gate must fail) runs no interactive session at all, so there is no hook event to read. Static whole-line presence in the committed `.claude/CLAUDE.md` remains the only cross-repo, CI-observable signal. No refactor: routing the lines axis through the observer would make the gate unable to fail in the one environment that matters.
- **`mod-path_drift`** — `mod-path_drift-1` Neither native check answers the module's question. check_path_ordering reports PRECEDENCE (is a non-mise dir ahead of mise's dirs) and never compares versions, returns early on `!env::is_activated()` and returns early again when NO mise path is found in the inherited PATH -- which is the exact shape of a badly drifted shell; check_shim_shadowing runs only when NOT activated and shims are on PATH, and the module already excludes shims by construction (path_drift.py:63-66). mise's cause-side fixes do not reach the case either: the reactivation drop of stale install dirs (#10162, v2026.5.18) only fires when hook-env decides to do a full run, gated on loaded-config / tera / watch_files mtimes (src/hook_env.rs:274-300), and the mise x/run/env child-PATH filter (#10345/#10422) repairs the CHILD, which is precisely why a probe run under `mise run` is blind. A long-lived agent process (Claude Code and its Bash tool) inherits a frozen PATH and never runs a prompt hook, so nothing native reactivates it. Control arm on the 'nothing native' claim: the same grep shape over src/cli/doctor/mod.rs returns 10 PATH hits and 60 warn/check hits, so a 0-result would have been informative -- the two PATH checks it DID find are the ones assessed above. Gap digests confirm no newer capability: mise has zero releases newer than the host's 2026.9.3 (.agent/kb/raw/mise-releases-since-pin.digest.md), hk 1.58.1 is docs-only (.agent/kb/raw/hk-releases-since-pin.digest.md), and Claude Code 2.1.258-2.1.266 shipped nothing env/PATH-related (.agent/kb/raw/claude-code-changelog-2.1.258-2.1.266.digest.md). `mod-path_drift-4` Required justification: the capability is 'know when the probe cannot see the shell it is asked about', and it exists only because mise deliberately repairs PATH for every child it spawns (src/toolset/toolset_env.rs:20-31, CHANGELOG.md:3069 #10422). No harness or tool feature hands a child its parent's pre-activation PATH, so the capture must be done by the caller and the blindness branch must exist or the check becomes a probe with one face. The only structural alternative is to stop invoking the doctor through `mise run` (call `mise doctor` or the dotfiles CLI straight from the ambient shell), which would trade the capture for losing mise-managed tool resolution for the doctor itself -- a worse trade, and it still would not supply the version comparison of finding 1.
- **`mod-plan_attest`** — `mod-plan_attest-3` Required justification: the capability is "give a human a stable, typeable command that runs a script living at a version-pinned path inside the plugin cache", and the harness exposes no primitive for it — no subcommand prints the install directory (finding 2's probe is the only candidate, and even a positive result would only replace the resolver INSIDE this wrapper, not the wrapper), and the one native path variable is scoped to plugin-provided contexts. The passthrough-not-argparse choice is also correct against `.claude/rules/ai-cli-invocation.md`: enumerating upstream's flags would rot. Keep, with finding 1 layered on the task and finding 2 possibly replacing the resolver call. `mod-plan_attest-4` Required justification: nothing is superseded because the native feature was already chosen correctly, and the two nearby natives that a modernization pass would reach for are both weaker at this host's settings — an `ask` rule is skipped by the permission mode these sessions actually run in, and `disable-model-invocation` provably never covered the script route (crossed twice on 2026-09-02). The only custom code in this capability is the PRESENCE check, and it exists because the harness ships no validator for permission-rule completeness: `claude plugin validate --json` (new at 2.1.259) validates plugin manifests, not settings.json. The check's own honest limit is already documented in its docstring — it proves the rules were not silently half-written, not that the harness still honours them.
- **`mod-platform_target`** — `mod-platform_target-1` The gate's whole value is that it is GLOB-LESS — a literal can arrive in any tracked file, including .toml, which is where the pin itself lives. Every native candidate is path- or language-scoped: hk ships no generic forbidden-pattern step, ast-grep cannot parse TOML at the pinned version, and the in-repo regex_forbid handler would require someone to predict the file list, which is exactly the failure mode (#673 AC3) the scan exists to cover. `mod-platform_target-2` A native mechanism exists and is deliberately not used, with a measured cost justification recorded in the code (emulated compilation of two compilers). The custom matrix is therefore not reinvention — it is the declaration of WHICH native runner builds WHICH arch, plus the #840 validate-only leg (same platform tuple, different runner) that an OCI index literally cannot express. Nothing in mise/hk/gh/GHA supplies a second row for one platform tuple. `mod-platform_target-3` The native half (env pin + default) is ALREADY adopted — this function only wraps it for the Python/CI callers that do not run inside a mise template. mise's arch() returns mise's own spelling (x64/arm64), not docker's triple with a microarchitecture level, and is unavailable to Python, GHA steps, or an in-container smoke; no mise/uv/gh feature returns `linux/<arch>/<level>`. `mod-platform_target-4` Required justification: the axis genuinely has four vocabularies (docker, uname, mise, LLVM) and every native source speaks exactly one of them; #698 (131 x86_64 tool resolutions in an arm64 image) and #703 (LLVM_TARGETS_TO_BUILD=X86 on arm64) are the recorded costs of treating any two as interchangeable. Centralising the maps here also keeps the shell tasks free of bash logic ([[zero-bash-logic]]) — verify-arch reads the CLI instead of re-implementing the mapping. `mod-platform_target-6` Required justification: the native settings are already adopted — the custom code is only the AGREEMENT check between three declarations mise cannot see together (what CI publishes, what the image locks, what the running container pins). No mise, hk, uv or GHA feature knows about PUBLISHED_ARCHES, and the failure mode is silent by construction (#698: a wrong-architecture binary is present, executable and counted exactly like a correct one), so there is nothing upstream to defer to.
- **`mod-pr`** — `mod-pr-2` The native flag cannot cover this capability: gh populates checks once before entering watch mode, so `--watch` returns the "no checks reported" error immediately in exactly the window this function exists for (the seconds-to-minutes after `gh pr create` while GitHub registers check runs). `--watch` is also mutually exclusive with `--json` (checks.go:81), so it cannot be used to read the machine-readable buckets `pr_checks_green` depends on. This is the documented exception to the never-hand-roll-a-poll rule, not a violation of it. `mod-pr-3` The watch/verify half is already native and follows `.claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md` (watch + independent `conclusion` cross-check). The only custom part left is resolving commit-SHA -> run-id, which gh has no native form of: `gh run watch` requires an id and falls back to an interactive prompt. The poll also has to distinguish 'no run yet' from 'no run will ever exist' (the path-filtered push trigger), which no gh flag models. `mod-pr-5` Required justification: no native mechanism expresses gate SELECTION from the branch's changed-path set. mise's `depends` graph is explicitly parallel (task-configuration.md:105) — which destroys the cheap-first ordering and the fail-fast semantics that make the first failure the task — and mise has no conditional-on-diff dependency edge at all; hk runs on git-hook events over staged files and cannot decide 'this diff touched a base-image build input, so DEFER the container gate to CI'. That path-aware policy (surface vs base-input vs apt-pin) is repo-specific judgement encoded as code, and it is what makes the ship verb a gate rather than a script. `mod-pr-6` Required justification: the wait itself is already delegated to GitHub (no client poll, no `gh run watch` on the PR), so the only custom code is the bounded retry over a documented transient 422 on the enable call, for which gh offers no flag. The single shared `enable_auto_merge` used by both `ship` and `automerge` is also what keeps the arming semantics (squash + `--match-head-commit` pinning) from drifting between the two entrypoints — a property no native mechanism provides.
- **`mod-process_env`** — `mod-process_env-2` Required justification: the module already delegates the list to the tool that owns it, which is what use-tool-builtins.md asks for; the custom code is only the fail-closed wrapper, and nothing outside git can produce this list. The measured payoff is concrete — git returns 15 names on this host while the nearest hand-maintained list in the repo (child_env.GIT_CONTEXT_NAMES, python/src/dotfiles_setup/child_env.py:36-45) carries 6, so a static list would leak 9 variables including GIT_CONFIG, GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and GIT_PREFIX. No linter, hook or task can replace a runtime query of the installed git. `mod-process_env-3` Required justification: every native unset mechanism takes a STATIC, hand-written list of names, which is precisely the failure mode the module's docstring exists to avoid — the set is derived per-host from git (15 names here, and a future git release adds more silently), and clean_env additionally removes credential-shaped names by regex, which no toml env block can express. hk's step env is typed String-only and cannot unset at all. Doing it in a shell wrapper would also violate zero-bash-logic. The native layers are already adopted where they fit (`env -u` and `mise --cd` in hk.pkl:780). `mod-process_env-5` Required justification: the two tools involved both make the stale value WIN — fnox falls back to an already-set variable as a resolution source, and gh/git-credential prefer GH_TOKEN over GITHUB_TOKEN — and neither exposes a native way to drop a name from the child environment. The custom code is a two-name deletion on a copy of os.environ, it never reads or prints a value, and it is the minimum that closes the precedence hole. Re-check if fnox ever ships an `--unset`/`--no-inherit` flag on `exec`.
- **`mod-reap`** — `mod-reap-2` The native guard does not cover this capability on the machine that has the problem. Three gaps, each measured: (1) it is Linux-only and this host is darwin — probed `test -r /proc/1/comm` -> PROC_ABSENT while `CLAUDE_PID` is SET, so the shipped wrapper function short-circuits to `command pkill "$@"` here (the wrapper body was read from the live shell; its own `[ -r "/proc/${CLAUDE_PID}/comm" ]` gate is the Linux test); (2) it protects exactly ONE pid, the Claude CLI, whereas the measured #653 incident had `--pattern 'fnox export'` matching FOUR processes, all of them the reaper's own chain (zsh wrapper -> uv -> the python entry) — a guard on the CLI pid alone would still have killed the uv/python links; (3) it only exists inside Claude Code's Bash tool shell, so it protects nothing when the operator runs `mise run reap` from a plain terminal. Nothing in mise, hk, gh, or BSD `pkill` offers ancestor exclusion. `mod-reap-3` Required justification: no tool in the pinned set expresses this policy. BSD `pkill` on macOS has no age predicate at all (probed above — procps-ng's `--older` is a GNU/Linux extension absent from the host binary), no dry run, and exit code 1 conflates 'no process matched' with failure, which is exactly the blind-probe conflation `probes-need-a-control-arm.md` rule 9 forbids and which reap.py:201 deliberately splits. A pgrep-then-pkill two-step is not equivalent either: the two invocations take two different snapshots, so the set previewed is not the set signalled — the very gap `confirm_targets` exists to close. Even after the mod-reap-1 psutil refactor this layer survives unchanged, so it is the module's real content. `mod-reap-4` The native reaping narrows the module's remaining domain but does not cover it. It applies only to processes Claude Code itself started as background shells and tracks by handle; the measured #653 pile was `mise/shims/git` and `fnox export --format json` spawned by the shell/mise plugin outside any Claude process tree, with the root cause still open upstream (knowledge-base#243). Nothing in that native path can be pointed at an arbitrary argv pattern on the host. The narrowing IS worth recording in the skill, because one recurring source of orphaned workers is now self-clearing and a session should not reach for `reap` for it — that is a doc edit, not a retirement.
- **`mod-renovate`** — `mod-renovate-4` After findings 1 and 2 the module shrinks to one thing nothing native does: turn 'this GitHub App installation is missing a permission it declares' into a non-zero exit code from a CLI. That justification is real, but it comes with two caveats the synthesis should carry. (a) The gate has no consumer: `renovate-status` is invoked only by its mise task — no hk step, no `python/verification/suites.toml` contract, and no `doctor.toml` check reference it (grep over mise.toml, hk*.pkl, .claude/settings.json, suites.toml, doctor.toml returns the mise task and two research docs only), unlike its sibling `renovate_validate`, which hk shells out to and `workflow.renovate-re2-engine-assertion` binds. So an rc=1 nobody runs is documentation, not enforcement — either wire it (a doctor check runs every session already) or drop the gate pretence. (b) Its whole rc semantic rests on the hard-coded table of finding 1 and the false-negative funnel of finding 3, so 'keep' is conditional on both being fixed; kept as-is it is a gate that under-checks in one direction and over-fires in the other.
- **`mod-renovate_dryrun`** — `mod-renovate_dryrun-3` Justification, not a default: the native rollup is strictly weaker on two axes and unreachable on a third. It has fileCount/depCount but no `updates` and no `skipped`, so it cannot distinguish 'this manager matched files and everything is current' from 'this manager matched files and every dep was skipped' — the distinction the skipped column exists for and the one that made #288 mistrust the task. It has no per-DATASOURCE view at all. And it lives in the debug log, so consuming it means scraping a ~5k-line log stream, which the module rejected on the record for `use-tool-builtins`' own reasoning (:34-39) and which would re-introduce a parser bound to log wording nobody here owns (`probes-need-a-control-arm.md` rule 9). Nothing at renovate 44.59.2 or 44.70.1 puts these tallies in the report. `mod-renovate_dryrun-4` Justification: the gate semantics ('any pending update => rc=1') are this repo's convention, deliberately aligned with `mise run sync -- --check` so the flag means one thing across the task set, and no renovate mode expresses it. The exit-code triage message is likewise about a renovate behaviour (extract succeeds, process still exits non-zero under an unsupported node) that renovate itself gives no structured signal for — the module distinguishes the two cases by testing whether the report file exists, which is the only available discriminator. A separate note, not a finding: the node-24 pin that makes this rare is already the NATIVE mechanism (`tasks.*.tools` per-task version override, mise.toml:876), not custom code. `mod-renovate_dryrun-5` Justification: the custom surface here is three tokens of JSON handed to a documented native config layer — the opposite of homegrown machinery — and the alternative (dropping the jdx preset, or adding `cloneSubmodules: false` to renovate.json) would make the file the local task reads differ from the file hosted Renovate reads, which is the property the module deliberately preserves (:26-27). The retire question was asked properly and answered NO by source, not by assumption: `cloneSubmodules(true)` still calls `syncGit()` before it looks at `cloneSubmodulesFilter`, and `syncGit()` still throws unconditionally under `platform=local`, at the newest build available on this host. The sibling node-24 pin is also still load-bearing: 44.70.1's package.json still declares `engines.node ^24.11.0`.
- **`mod-renovate_validate`** — `mod-renovate_validate-1` Required justification: at the repo's own pin (npm:renovate 44.59.2) the degradation is STILL silent — the RE2-unavailable warning is emitted outside every code path that sets the exit code, so `--strict` promotes schema warnings but not this one, and no flag or env var makes the process exit non-zero on a degraded engine (RENOVATE_X_IGNORE_RE2 only logs at debug). Nothing in hk, mise, uv, gh, renovate presets, or any pinned linter observes another tool's internal regex engine. The custom code is also already minimal and native-first: it parses no regex and keeps no blacklist of RE2-unsupported constructs; the only added logic is the inverted canary, and it is deliberately capability-shaped rather than a log-string sniff (.claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md:135). Retiring it would restore exactly the #644 failure mode: a green rc over unchecked regexes. `mod-renovate_validate-2` Required justification: two independent reasons. (a) No renovate builtin exists in hk at the pinned 1.57.0 (or in 1.58.1), control-armed above, so there is nothing native to adopt for the wiring. (b) Even if one shipped, it would call the bare binary, whose rc cannot be trusted per finding 1 — the wrapper exists precisely to order the canary FIRST, a property that suites.toml:1534 and tests/test_renovate_validate.py:113-127 bind as a safety guarantee. The wrapper adds no validation logic of its own: the flags are the tool's documented ones (`--strict`, `--no-global`, declared at config-validator.js:100 in the pinned install) and every verdict comes from the native process's exit code. `mod-renovate_validate-3` Required justification: the native check covers the same question but at the wrong time and with the wrong instrument. It only fires during a hosted Renovate run — after the config has been pushed, on branches Renovate itself processes — so it cannot gate a commit, and a broken renovate.json would silently stop dependency updates until the next scheduled run rather than failing lint. It also runs on an install that has re2, so by construction it can never surface the local-validator degradation this module was built for (#644's inversion: the LOCAL gate being weaker than the remote one). It is a complementary backstop, not a superseding mechanism; nothing in the module should be deleted in its favour. hk.pkl:463-471 additionally records that the validator is complementary to the repo-specific suites.toml contracts (ci.regex-managers-enabled, ci.renovate-extends-jdx-preset), which neither instrument covers.
- **`mod-rule_registry`** — `mod-rule_registry-7` This is the one capability with no native or third-party equivalent, and it encodes a project-specific policy no vendor could know: that eager context is the scarce resource here and an unscoped rule owes a written justification (md-size-budgets.md's 'trigger test'). Control arm on the absence: grepping the same agnix locale file for a term that IS present ('frontmatter', 'paths field') returns hits, so the zero result for an eager-rationale rule is the corpus's answer, not a broken probe. Keep — but note it is heading-anchored by operator decision (C5), so its two known blind spots are carried as a hard-coded debt list rather than by the parser. `mod-rule_registry-8` Required justification: this is ahead-of-consumers infrastructure with every consumer ticket still OPEN, not abandoned code, so 'retire' would be wrong. But it is unwired today, which means the repo's own enforcement doctrine does not yet apply to it — nothing in suites.toml asserts it stays reachable, so when #927/#928 land there is no contract preventing a wiring line from being deleted while the module and its tests stay green (the exact failure `workflow.apt-pins-enforcement` and the `per_path_tokens` doctrine exist to prevent). The concrete debt: whichever ticket first wires it must ship a `[[suite]]` binding the CALL SITE, and should land findings 3 and 6 at the same time so the third classifier and the second inject source of truth never reach production.
- **`mod-schema_vendor`** — `mod-schema_vendor-5` Justified keep, not a default: `postUpgradeTasks.commands` is gated on `allowedCommands`, which only exists in self-hosted Renovate admin config, and this repo is on the hosted app — so the native mechanism is unreachable at the current deployment. The sibling idea (a Renovate `customManager` bumping the `version`/`source` fields of `schemas/sources.toml`, in the shape of the existing hk-pkl customManager at renovate.json:85-97) is actively WRONG here: Renovate can rewrite the version string but cannot re-download the JSON or recompute `sha256`, so it would make `sources.toml` assert a version the bytes do not have — the precise failure `check_drift`'s hash arm exists to catch. `mod-schema_vendor-6` Justified keep by enumeration rather than by a 0-result grep: both tools' full command surfaces were listed and neither can print its schema, so a tagged fetch is the only way to obtain the exact bytes for a pinned version. `curl` as the fetch mechanism is this repo's existing convention (`gcc_sha._default_fetcher`), needs no auth for raw.githubusercontent, and `-f` already turns an HTTP error page into a non-zero exit; routing it through `gh api` would add an auth dependency to a job that needs none. `mod-schema_vendor-7` Justified keep: the check-jsonschema cache is per-machine under the user cache dir, so on a cold CI runner the first validation still fetches — swapping to it would move the lint gate's network dependency from 'never' to 'once per runner', which is the exact property the vendoring buys, and it would also drop byte-pinning (an mtime-keyed cache does not verify what it fetched). What no native tool provides at all is the pin-to-vendored-version binding: reading typos' pin from shared.toml, ruff's from uv.lock and mise's from a GHA action file, and asserting all three against one manifest. That mapping is repo-specific by construction.
- **`mod-script_guard`** — `mod-script_guard-1` The native rule is coarser in exactly the three dimensions that make this guard usable. (a) It cannot carry exceptions: permissions.md:66 states a broad deny cannot be narrowed by a more specific allow, so "Edit(**/*.sh)" would also block every edit to the ~20 sanctioned wrappers in bash_budget.ALLOWLIST (python/src/dotfiles_setup/bash_budget.py:66+) — including scripts/pretooluse-guard.sh, the wrapper this very hook runs from. An ask rule has the identical precedence problem and would prompt on every legitimate edit. (b) It cannot distinguish a NEW file from an edit to an existing one; the guard's contract is explicitly new-only (script_guard.py:175-184, added after a cold review found a tracked wrapper being denied with no usable escape hatch). (c) It cannot consult git-ignore state, so a scratchpad .sh would be denied too (script_guard.py:185). The commit-time siblings (hk's bash_logic_budget, hk.pkl:247) are git-hook-based and structurally cannot fire at write time, which is the whole reason this module exists (script_guard.py:7-15). Nothing at the pinned host version (Claude Code 2.1.266, incl. the 2.1.258-2.1.266 gap digest, which adds no permission-rule expressiveness) closes those three gaps. `mod-script_guard-2` No native path-glob can see a shebang, and the linters that can (shellcheck 0.11.0, ast-grep 0.45.3, hk builtins) all run at commit time through hk — the layer this module exists to precede. bash_budget's own SCOPE_PATHSPECS are *.sh globs, so the extensionless case is invisible to the commit gate too (script_guard.py:17-21, :151-158). The custom code is the minimum: it wraps the harness's own hook contract rather than reimplementing a permission engine. `mod-script_guard-5` This is the native-first pass already done: the only genuinely native facility in reach (git's ignore engine) is shelled out to, and the rest of the exemption set has no native expression — Claude Code's protected-path list is fixed and prompt-based, and permission patterns carry no ignore-awareness or single-source-of-truth link to bash_budget.ALLOWLIST. Duplicating the allowlist into settings.json allow rules would also be inert, since deny beats allow (permissions.md:66).
- **`mod-session_gate`** — `mod-session_gate-7` Justification, not a default: the engine measurably cannot express this contract. (a) It tests membership (`t not in combined`), not an exact occurrence count — and the count is the point here, since the mutation replaces one of N occurrences and a membership check would still pass on the survivors. (b) It resolves paths under the repo root only, while the whole mutation design depends on pointing the SAME gate at an isolated candidate tree (session_gate.py:278-293), which is what makes the arm real rather than a self-referential check. Retiring `prevention_check` in favour of `require_tokens` today would silently weaken both properties — precisely the `feedback_forbid_tokens_substring_fragile` failure. The constructive option is the inverse: teach `verify.require_tokens` an occurrence-count form and an optional root override, then have `prevention_check` call it; that is a change to verify.py, not to this module, so it is recorded here rather than dispositioned as a refactor of this unit. `mod-session_gate-8` The mutation-testing plugins arm a TEST SUITE against AST mutants; this module arms a mise GATE TASK against a source-token mutant in a relocated candidate tree, and asserts the gate's non-zero exit — a different subject (the gate, not the tests) and a different mutation domain (bytes of a carrier contract, not Python AST). `gh attestation` verifies Sigstore-signed provenance for artifacts and images produced under an OIDC issuer; it has nothing to say about 'this local gate rejected this local mutant at this moment', and the finalize verdict is deliberately ephemeral precisely so it cannot become a replayable artifact — the opposite of what an attestation store is for. Nothing in the Claude Code 2.1.258-2.1.266 changelog digest, the hk 1.58.1 digest (documentation-only), the mise digest (host already at newest release) or the uv 0.12.10-0.12.11 digest touches this surface. Findings 1-6 are the parts that ARE superseded; the design itself is not.
- **`mod-session_ledger`** — `mod-session_ledger-6` Justification, not a default: no harness, CLI, linter or marketplace plugin at the host's pinned versions models 'what the user asked for' and 'what the agent promised' as typed, individually-dispositionable claims with a receipt-kind gate and a fail-loud omission census. Every native surface stops at delivering messages — which is precisely why findings -1 and -2 propose adopting them as the READ boundary underneath this layer rather than replacing it. The byte-exact SourceCutoff and append-only prefix semantics also have no native counterpart: SDKSessionInfo exposes file_size and last_modified, but nothing that certifies which bytes were reviewed, and the vendor explicitly reserves the right to change the on-disk format (sessions.md:224), which makes this layer's independence from that format the thing worth keeping.
- **`mod-session_review`** — `mod-session_review-2` Required justification: the check is a cross-revision byte-prefix invariant over one tracked file, evaluated against an authority (the origin/main merge-base) that the branch under review must not be able to choose for itself. No linter, no hk builtin, and no GitHub platform feature at the host's pins expresses 'this file may only grow at its tail, measured from a baseline the branch cannot nominate'. The one piece that IS delegable — the per-snapshot document shape — is finding 1; what remains here is git plumbing plus the fail-closed baseline rule, and it stays custom. `mod-session_review-3` Required justification: the native transcript miner answers a different question (should this call be pre-approved?) and emits a settings allowlist, not a ranked candidate list; nothing native ranks by SESSION SPREAD, which is this lane's whole thesis (twenty uses in one session is a grind, three across three sessions is a workflow). `/skill-doctor` prunes existing skills and cannot propose one that does not exist. Retiring lane 1 for either would lose the finding class it exists for. Worth revisiting only if `/fewer-permission-prompts` ever gains a machine-readable dump of its mined shapes. `mod-session_review-4` Required justification: this is a project-specific semantic surfacer over a project-specific corpus (.agent/**, which is gitignored — the module docstring at :44-49 records that this is exactly why the issue's `--since <ref>` bound is unimplementable). A generic linter cannot carry this repo's own slog vocabulary or its suppressor set, both of which the module records as measured from a real first run rather than guessed (:159-163). Nothing native reads these files at all. `mod-session_review-5` Required justification: the native group binds the CLI parser only, and this module is a public library entry point — tests call session_review_main() directly with a hand-built LaneChoice (tests/test_session_review.py:563 'asking_for_both_exclusive_lanes_is_refused_not_resolved', :576, :591, :602), and the module docstring at :701-704 makes refusing-rather-than-resolving a stated contract. Deleting the check would make an impossible-via-CLI combination silently resolve for library callers. Noted as a duplication, not a defect: the correct future move is to keep the library check and NOT to add a second parser-level guess.
- **`mod-session_state`** — `mod-session_state-1` The load-bearing value is not the data collection (git and gh already do that) but the failure-mode discipline: PrState.UNVERIFIABLE for command failure, timeout, malformed JSON and detached HEAD (session_state.py:157-163, :194-215), which is exactly the false-negative class .claude/rules/probes-need-a-control-arm.md exists to prevent. A shell pipeline of the native commands returns an empty list on both 'no PR' and 'gh is broken', which is the bug this module was written to remove. Keep the module; the sub-findings below are internal adoptions of native mechanics, not replacements of the unit.
- **`mod-session_store`** — `mod-session_store-1` mise's cache is binary per task invocation: any change to any declared source is a full miss and the whole task re-runs. This unit's entire value is the opposite — a *partially changed* input where the unchanged prefix's facts are reused and only the appended suffix is decoded (CacheStats.decoded_bytes = len(suffix), session_store.py:429-433). The inputs also sit outside the workspace (Claude/Codex transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/*.jsonl, /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/agent-sdk__sessions.md:272), and the live session's own transcript grows during the run, so a task-level cache would miss on every invocation while mise's audit/outputs machinery is scoped beneath the workspace root. No native mechanism in mise, hk, uv, gh, graphify or Claude Code parses an append-only JSONL suffix; keeping the custom store is justified. `mod-session_store-4` hk's exclusivity is scoped to steps inside one hk hook run, and this store is never invoked from an hk step — it runs under `mise run session-review` / the session-review gate tasks (mise.toml:1478-1523), and two such runs (or a gate plus an ad-hoc run) are exactly the concurrency it must survive. mise has no equivalent cross-invocation task lock in the corpus, and the same flock idiom is already the repo's convention for this class of problem (dag_tick.py:1010, codex_verdict.py:441). Nothing native covers it; the stdlib call is three lines. `mod-session_store-5` The SDK's SessionStore is a *write/mirror* adapter the SDK calls while producing a transcript, for resume across hosts; it offers no parse-fact caching, no content addressing, no incremental suffix parsing, and it only exists inside a process running the Agent SDK — this repo reads finished transcripts from disk instead. So it does not supersede anything here. Recorded because the identical name is a live confusion hazard for anyone reading `from dotfiles_setup.session_store import SessionStore` and assuming SDK-protocol semantics; the fix is a one-line docstring note (or a rename such as `FactStore`), not a change of mechanism.
- **`mod-skillopt_provenance`** — `mod-skillopt_provenance-4` JUSTIFICATION (required): `gh attestation` binds an artifact to the GitHub Actions workflow that PRODUCED it. This manifest is not produced by a workflow — it is a locally authored assertion about three already-landed commits, generated by `export()` on a developer machine and committed. There is no signer workflow for sigstore to attest, so `gh attestation verify` has nothing to verify here, and adopting it would require first inverting the whole flow so CI generates the manifest. The self-hash it does implement is also honest about its own limit: a `.sha256` sidecar written by the same code that writes the manifest detects accidental drift, not an adversary with commit access — which is exactly why `verify_live()` exists alongside it. Flagging the inversion (have CI emit + attest the manifest) as a possible future direction, but at today's pins nothing native covers this, so keep. `mod-skillopt_provenance-5` JUSTIFICATION (required): the local route is cheaper but answers a strictly weaker question. `git cat-file` proves 'this content hashes to this id'; it cannot prove 'this commit is reachable from ray-manaloto/dotfiles on GitHub and landed via merged PR #728'. Only the third of the three live reads (`pulls/<n>` — merged, merge_commit_sha, base.repo.full_name, :221-230) strictly requires the network, but dropping the first two would leave the merge-commit assertion unanchored to a tree the checker has independently identified. The remote round trip is the point of the check, not incidental cost, so it stays. The efficiency half of this concern is already carried by finding -3 (batch the same reads into one `gh api graphql` call) — that is the change worth making, not moving the check offline.
- **`mod-sync`** — `mod-sync-1` Both candidate native routes were probed live and both fail. `devcontainer outdated` is scoped to Feature/Template versions declared in devcontainer.json — it has no notion of the base image digest or the local overlay container, which is the entire subject of this module. And no docker-side digest is stable across the buildkit `--output type=docker` re-export this repo must use instead of a classic pull: on a workspace the record calls converged, RepoDigests and the registry config digest BOTH disagree with the local store, which is exactly why the state record exists. Nothing native carries that witness. `mod-sync-4` The native single-call route was armed and measured empty for exactly the tag this code inspects, so adopting it today would silently report 'no platforms present' and make refresh_local_tag stop preserving the other architecture's layers — the #800 F2 regression the loop exists to prevent. Keep the N-probe loop until the probe below reports a populated array on a host that genuinely carries both platforms. `mod-sync-5` Two natives exist and neither does the job: imagetools create writes to a registry, not to the local image store (probed above), and classic `docker pull` is the measured-wedge path this repo bans for the ~38GB image. The buildkit `FROM` trick IS the native mechanism being used — the custom part is only the platform-union computation, which no docker flag expresses. `mod-sync-6` This capability already IS the native one, wrapped as thinly as it can be. `--status` takes one value out of five non-terminal statuses, so pushing the filter server-side would cost five calls instead of one call plus a one-line predicate. And the API cross-check after `gh run watch --exit-status` is mandated by .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md and feedback_gh_run_watch (watch has reported 0 prematurely), so it is a documented correction to the native tool, not a reinvention of it. `mod-sync-7` Required justification: the decision matrix is repo-specific policy — it composes three facts no single tool holds together (a registry index digest, this repo's #677 two-label container identity, and this repo's smoke/verify tiers) and encodes a fail-safe direction (offline => never take a destructive action) that no generic tool would choose for us. mise gained nothing since the pin and hk's only newer release is documentation, so there is no 2026-09 capability to adopt here. The module is already the thin-caller shape the repo's zero-bash-logic policy asks for, and suites.toml:1127 gates that shape.
- **`mod-token_audit`** — `mod-token_audit-1` The predicate is defined over an artifact no external tool knows exists: this repo's own verification manifest and its handler semantics (`per_path_tokens` -> path -> token list). A native tool would have to be taught the manifest's schema AND the cross-file resolution before it could count anything, at which point it is this module. The allowlist-with-justification + stale-entry-fails shape is likewise repo-specific policy (same shape as bash_budget.py) and has no baseline-file analogue in any pinned linter that can express 'this exception is no longer needed'. Keeping it is justified, not defaulted. `mod-token_audit-3` Retiring this to a shell one-liner would re-create exactly the defect #652 closed: the pre-flight and the gate would then ask the question through two different implementations, and the pre-flight's entire value is being BELIEVED before the contract is written — a pre-flight that says OK where the gate later says AMBIGUOUS is worse than none. The shared call site is itself contract-bound (suites.toml:2284), so a shell substitute would fail the repo's own gate. Two further behaviours a `grep -c` does not have and the callers depend on: zero and many are reported with DIFFERENT words because they are different defects, and the PASSING arm is printed because a silent success is indistinguishable from a probe that never ran. Native counting exists; native *shared-predicate* counting does not.
- **`mod-verify`** — `mod-verify-4` Required justification: what this engine asserts is cross-file WIRING — 'this hk step calls this CLI which reaches this module and this rule documents it' — and no linter in the toolchain has that shape. Every native candidate is a matcher that reports what it FINDS; this engine's dominant mode (111 of 152 suites) is asserting what must be THERE, plus a precondition that the named files still exist at all. hk's own glob semantics make it strictly worse for that: a renamed target silently removes the step. The gate is also deliberately distinct from hk (python/AGENTS.md:51-56, `.claude/rules/verify-before-advancing.md:26`), runs whole-repo in CI `contract-preflight` rather than on staged files, and its JSON/tally output is consumed as a gate result. Keep the engine; the improvements worth making are the three findings above (schema-ise the eval corpus, delete the dead handlers, move python-target token binding to a syntactic matcher), not a replacement.
- **`mod-workflow_hooks`** — `mod-workflow_hooks-4` Required justification: the check is a REPO-SPECIFIC semantic policy over a transitive graph — 'does this job reach a git binary in the runner's checkout', answered across composite-action inlining and a per-vendor behavioural verdict (peter-evans/create-pull-request writes locally; autofix-ci/action does not, despite every surface signal saying it does). No available linter accepts a user-authored rule of that shape; zizmor and ghalint are closed audit sets, and their configs subtract findings rather than add rules. The classification-gaps half additionally has no analogue anywhere — it is this repo's own allowlist-plus-staleness contract, copied deliberately from bash_budget.py. Keeping it is also what survives finding -1: if the native hk global skip is adopted, this is the part still worth having, because it is the part that answers 'which jobs write to git', not 'did someone remember an env line'. `mod-workflow_hooks-5` Required justification: this half ALREADY satisfies use-tool-builtins.md — the lexer is stdlib shlex, not a homegrown scanner, and the one thing shlex cannot model (heredoc bodies as inert data) is factored into a single module shared with hook_guard rather than duplicated. Swapping to ast-grep bash would trade a pure-python, dependency-free, in-process parse for a subprocess in a pre-commit step, and would split the heredoc semantics that hook_guard and this module currently share by construction — the sharing is what stops the two guards drifting, and drift between them is a defect class this repo has already paid for (#265). Revisit only if the shlex fallback path (unbalanced quote -> whitespace split) is ever observed producing a wrong verdict, since that is the only place the stdlib parse is knowingly approximate.
- **`rule-agent-artifact-conventions`** — `rule-agent-artifact-conventions-9` Required justification: both claims survive a re-probe with a control arm at the host version, and no native feature covers what this half of the rule does. Nothing in Claude Code reserves or writes `.agent/`, so the namespace choice is still safe; and the only native scoping lever (`paths:`) is read-triggered, so scoping this rule would remove it from exactly the sessions that are about to create an artifact. The eager cost is real but there is no mechanism to trade it against — the rule's own answer (moving archaeology to `docs/rules-evidence/`) remains the only available lever, and it has already been applied.
- **`rule-agent-report-persistence`** — `rule-agent-report-persistence-7` Required justification: no native feature writes a verbatim agent report into the repository's tracked tree, and that — not mere durability — is what this rule buys (an artifact a fresh clone, a reviewer, and a later session can all open; docs/rules-evidence and the audit trail depend on it). The native surfaces are either ephemeral and machine-local (transcripts, retention-swept) or semantically different (agent-memory = the agent's own learnings, name-keyed, not run-keyed). So the rule is not retired; findings 1-5 change HOW it is triggered and enforced, not WHETHER it exists.
- **`rule-ai-cli-invocation`** — `rule-ai-cli-invocation-8` Required justification: no native harness feature supersedes the UNIT, only individual facts inside it (findings 1-7). The harness can deny a command shape, never teach the correct one, and the correct one is set by three external release trains this repo does not control - which is precisely why the file rotted to rc=2 in finding 1. Keep the rule, but the durable fix is structural: make the content that CAN be machine-checked machine-checked (a flag-probe contract in python/verification/suites.toml or an extension of `mise run codex-agent-parity` to cover this file), and let the prose keep only the judgement half - stdin for ARG_MAX, the per-CLI `-p` collision, and 're-probe `--help`, this file included'.
- **`rule-ci-local-parity`** — `rule-ci-local-parity-6` Justified keep, not a default. These four clauses encode a POLICY CHOICE about which of several working invocations this repo standardises on — mise-pinned binary over npx, `--project` over `--directory` — and no tool feature can make that choice; mise will happily run either, and uv documents both flags as supported. Rule 5's stub is 6 lines of correct, still-true archaeology that preserves the stable numbering other docs cite, so deleting it would break references to buy back almost nothing under this file's `rule_scoped` budget (400 lines / 32,000 B; the file is 66 lines). The gap digests for all three tools were read and contain nothing that changes any of it.
- **`rule-clarify-before-acting`** — `rule-clarify-before-acting-4` Required justification: the gate enforces a CONTENT standard on the tool's input, and no native surface at 2.1.266 expresses that — the tool schema has no field for a recommendation, a citation, or a stated downside, and permission rules cannot read an option's description. The one native affordance that could have carried evidence (`preview`) is SDK-gated and emits nothing when unset, so adopting it would weaken the gate rather than replace it. PreToolUse deny remains the documented, still-current mechanism (hooks.md:1744/1836), and it fires regardless of permission mode because PreToolUse runs on every tool call, not only on prompting calls. Confidence is 0.85 rather than higher because I verified the offline corpus and the 2.1.258-2.1.266 gap digest but did not run a live 2.1.266 probe of the AskUserQuestion schema.
- **`rule-clean-git-state`** — `rule-clean-git-state-6` Required justification: (a) the rule asserts NO harness facts — it names no hook event, settings key, precedence claim or `$CC/...:line` anchor, so nothing in it can have gone stale against 2.1.266; its single cross-reference, `.claude/rules/md-size-budgets.md`, still exists and still classifies `clean-git-state` as behaviour-triggered and therefore un-scopable (md-size-budgets.md, "Scoping: the trigger test" — "clean-git-state (fires when validation is about to run)"). (b) Its trigger is a decision ("I am about to validate"), which no `paths:` glob and no native feature predicts; the enforcing layers that do exist (hk's pre-commit stash, ship's clean-tree refusal) fire only at commit/push time, leaving the ad-hoc `mise run lint` window uncovered. (c) It forbids nothing a native feature has made safe. So the rule stays eager; findings 1-5 are edits WITHIN it, not grounds to retire it.
- **`rule-do-not`** — `rule-do-not-6` Keep entry 10 as written, and do NOT adopt the native scrub here. Justification, not default: (a) the native feature solves a different problem — it reduces what a subprocess can READ, while entry 10 governs what lands in a TRACKED FILE, which no harness setting inspects; (b) the scrub only removes variables Claude Code recognises as credentials, and this repo's exposure is ~56 fnox/Doppler-provided names of arbitrary spelling (.claude/rules/secrets-out-of-the-shell-env.md), so it would leave most of them in a dump while making the dump look sanitised — the 'clean scanner means ask what it can see' failure mode; (c) enabling it directly contradicts Ray's deliberate 2026-08-02 reversal that credentials be ambient to every terminal and agent. The `__MISE_DIFF` zlib+base64 packing that makes such a dump unscannable is a mise property with no harness counterpart, so `no_env_dump` remains the only layer that sees it. `rule-do-not-7` Required justification: these four bind surfaces the harness does not model. Entry 1 is macOS GUI process env inheritance reaching a devcontainer `initializeCommand` — the harness has no launcher-env feature and the string appears nowhere in its docs. Entry 4 is a repo verification contract (`build.no-stderr-suppression`) over Dockerfile bytes. Entry 6 is a defect in the `gh` CLI's own `--exit-status`, which no harness feature can correct; the harness's `Monitor` tool is a line-streaming watcher, not a workflow-conclusion reader, so substituting it would swap a known-flaky signal for an unrelated one. Entry 7 is a Docker Desktop vs Colima runtime property (`/run/host-services/ssh-auth.sock`). All four stay as prose invariants; entries 2/3/5 are the ones that can be hardened natively (see rule-do-not-3).
- **`rule-gh-cli-watch`** — `rule-gh-cli-watch-4` Required justification for 'keep': this rule asserts no Claude Code harness fact (no hook event, settings key, precedence claim, or $CC anchor), so axis (a) has nothing to go stale against 2.1.266. Its gh-CLI facts were re-derived against the pinned gh source at the installed 2.100.0 and all hold, and the `--exit-status` cross-verify habit has no native replacement — GitHub has shipped nothing that makes a single `gh run watch` exit code trustworthy, and the harness offers no equivalent. The factual layer of the rule stays as written; only the prescriptive layer moves (findings 1-3).
- **`rule-goal-history`** — `rule-goal-history-3` Required justification: the capability is "prove a tracked markdown file was only ever appended to, relative to a baseline the branch cannot choose for itself". No harness feature, no git feature, and no pinned tool provides it — GitHub rulesets gate refs and paths, not per-file byte prefixes, and a hook can log a change (hooks.md:1294) but has no decision control at SessionEnd/InstructionsLoaded and no history-walking primitive at any event. The one native feature that shares the word "goal" solves a different problem (in-session completion condition, transcript-only). The custom validator also already satisfies this repo's own bar: it ignores caller-supplied baselines and fails closed when the baseline cannot be resolved (session_review.py:526-528), and its FAIL direction is armed by tests/test_session_review.py (rewrite-behind-an-unrelated-commit, branch-appended-entry rewrite, rewritten bootstrap, missing history). Keep it as-is.
- **`rule-local-devcontainer-first`** — `rule-local-devcontainer-first-4` Required justification: the thing this rule carries is a cost-aware judgement — which environment can exhibit THIS failure mode, and whether the cheap environment is honest about it — and no harness feature decides that. The #288 measurement (a pin that FAILED in the devcontainer and PASSED in a clean base container, because apt refuses to downgrade) is a false-negative class no linter, hook or permission rule can detect; it is the reason the rule exists and it stays entirely un-automatable. The non-license clause is likewise a bound on evidence, not a mechanism. Keep the rule, with the three amendments above (correct/condition the cost figure, stop transcribing the tier list, add the FileChanged nudge for non-apt image inputs).
- **`rule-long-running-command-hangs`** — `rule-long-running-command-hangs-8` Required justification: the wrapper in `lint.py` exists precisely because hk ships no bound of its own, and that is still true at the pinned 1.57.0 and at the only newer release. The harness's Bash timeout (finding 3) is not a substitute — it backgrounds rather than killing, so it would leave the wedged hk process group alive and print no diagnostics, and it does not exist at all in CI or a human terminal, which is where `mise run lint` also runs. Rules 5, 6 and 7 are hk-internal forensics with no counterpart in any tool: nothing native names a wedged hk step, cleans `~/.local/state/hk/`, or knows that a failed dependency never releases its dependent. Rule 2's log paths were re-verified against `lint.py` and are accurate as written.
- **`rule-md-size-budgets`** — `rule-md-size-budgets-6` Required justification: the harness deliberately does not gate instruction-file size — it degrades quietly instead, which is precisely the failure this repo pays a pre-commit gate to make loud. `claude plugin validate --json` (2.1.259) validates manifests and frontmatter parsing, not byte or line counts, so it cannot substitute. The five findings above are edits to the rule's PROSE and cited anchors; the gate, the class taxonomy and every number in the budget table survive the audit unchanged.
- **`rule-mise-tasks-only`** — `rule-mise-tasks-only-7` Keep the row and the guard rule, but the justification needs narrowing to the half that is still true. The exit-code half is untouched by any native feature: a shell pipeline still returns `tail`'s status, and the Bash tool's own valid/failure classification is derived from that masked exit code (tools-reference.md:169), so `\| tail` still converts a red gate into a result Claude reads as green. The size half — the reason anyone reaches for `\| tail` — is now the harness's job, so the row should say 'you never need to bound gate output yourself; the harness saves it and hands you the path' rather than leaving the redirect looking like the only way to see a long log. `rule-mise-tasks-only-8` Required justification: the unit's core mechanism has no native equivalent at Claude Code 2.1.266. The harness can block a command and can filter which handler sees it, but nothing native can tell the agent WHICH canonical task to run instead — that text can only reach Claude through a hook's `permissionDecisionReason` (hooks.md:1016), which is exactly what this rule's guard does. Findings 1-4 and 6 narrow the mechanism at its edges (hard bans to deny rules, `$()` framing, `if` pre-filtering, `updatedInput` rewrites, a fail-closed error path); the redirect map itself stays custom.
- **`rule-notepad-enforcement`** — `rule-notepad-enforcement-5` Required justification: (a) audit axis (a) came back CLEAN — this rule asserts no hook event, no settings key, no precedence claim and no `$CC/...` doc anchor, so it has no stale harness fact to correct. Its only external claims are that `.agent/notepad.md` is gitignored (true, .gitignore:45) and that the oh-my-claudecode notepad MCP tools are absent (control-armed 2026-09-09: `oh-my-claudecode` returns 0 hits in both .claude/settings.json and ~/.claude/settings.json while `fable-orchestrator` returns 3 in the same grep shape — the plugin is not merely disabled, it is not registered at all, so the rule's statement is if anything understated). (b) The '0 invocations across 941 transcripts' figure is INHERITED and was not re-derived in this audit — label it unverified per probes-need-a-control-arm.md rule 6 if it is ever restated. (c) The rule also forbids nothing the harness has since made safe: it forbids batching findings to session end, and no 2.1.258-2.1.266 capability persists a session's working findings automatically. The three refactors above change the CARRIER and the ENFORCEMENT of the directive, not the directive, so the file stays.
- **`rule-persistence-gate-retry`** — `rule-persistence-gate-retry-6` Required justification: nothing native retries or classifies this. mise cannot retry a task, the devcontainers CLI cannot retry `up`, and no Claude Code feature at 2.1.266 re-runs a failed Bash command or triages its stderr — the 2.1.258-2.1.266 digest's only output-related additions are `bashOutputMaxChars`/`taskOutputMaxChars` (2.1.261), which change how much output reaches Claude inline, not whether a wrapper's exit code is truthful. That last point also leaves the rule's warning at :73-75 ('the task notification cannot be trusted here') standing unrefuted at the host version. Both step-2 host probes were re-armed live and still return exactly what the rule says. Keep the mechanism; apply findings 1-5 to where it lives and what strings it cites.
- **`rule-probes-need-a-control-arm`** — `rule-probes-need-a-control-arm-5` KEEP with justification, not by default: this rule governs a JUDGMENT — whether the reader believes a result — and no harness feature at 2.1.266 can observe that decision. Findings 1-4 mechanize or update four specific SHAPES it covers (hk gate fail-arms, agent liveness, the harness's own output bound, the repo's probe/control pairs); the residue — arming an ad-hoc find/curl/grep, noticing a token spelling, re-deriving an inherited number, arming the fixture — has no native counterpart and is behaviour-triggered, so per md-size-budgets.md's trigger test it must also stay EAGER rather than being scoped or demoted to a skill. Nothing in it is forbidden-but-now-safe: every prohibition it carries (bounded searches, symptom sniffing, unarmed negatives) remains as true at 2.1.266 as when written.
- **`rule-real-integration-evidence`** — `rule-real-integration-evidence-1` Required justification: the directive is an epistemic standard about what a piece of evidence PROVES, and no harness feature at the host's versions or any repo pin (hk 1.57.0, mise 2026.9.3, pytest, ast-grep 0.45.3) can distinguish a real invocation from a fixture that returns the same bytes - that judgement is made when the claim is written, before any tool call the harness could hook. The rule also asserts nothing version-bound: no doc anchor, no settings key, no hook name, and its one named third-party ('Graphify release') is still current (.agent/kb/raw/graphify-readme-0.9.56.digest.md reports 0 new capabilities vs the 0.9.53 pin). Keep as-is; it is behaviour-triggered, so it correctly stays unscoped/eager per .claude/rules/md-size-budgets.md, and at 585 B it is far inside the rule_unscoped budget.
- **`rule-research-doc-sources`** — `rule-research-doc-sources-8` Required justification: step 00 is the rule's core and no native feature covers it — the corpus is 100 trees / 40,846 md files on local disk (measured 2026-09-09) and the harness offers no local doc index, so the cheapest harness-behaviour lookup remains a grep. Its cited layout also still holds: all five agent-harness-docs/docs/{claude-code,codex,cursor,opencode,pi} subtrees resolve. The ctx7 caveat is likewise still TRUE at the pinned 0.5.9 and should not be tidied away — live probe: `ctx7 --help` lists no `skills` command, yet `ctx7 skills --help` prints the subcommand's own usage (generate/install/search/list/remove/info/suggest). Control arms: `ctx7 library --help` prints its own usage (known-present) while `ctx7 zzqqwwxx-nope --help` falls back to the ROOT usage (known-absent), so the probe discriminates present from absent subcommands.
- **`rule-research-repo-enumeration`** — `rule-research-repo-enumeration-4` Required justification for 'keep': the enumeration is a judgement artifact — which repos a research pass genuinely relied on — that no tool can derive after the fact. The harness does not log external doc fetches per repo, mdschema validates shape not truth, and graphify indexes THIS repo's code, not consulted third parties. Measured compliance shows the habit is live and productive (85 of 88 tracked .md under docs/research/runs carry the section; control arm: 508 of 536 tracked docs/research .md contain any '##' heading, so the miss arm is real). Keep the directive; only its enforcement story (-1, -2) and its scope (-3) need changing.
- **`rule-secrets-out-of-the-shell-env`** — `rule-secrets-out-of-the-shell-env-4` Required justification: this is tool-topology and failure-mode knowledge about fnox, Doppler, the macOS keychain and mise's env encoding -- none of which the harness models, and none of which any pinned tool now solves natively. Its enforcement layer (`no_env_dump` in hk.pkl, backed by env_blob_scan.py) is a genuine capability gate rather than a symptom sniff: it exists precisely because gitleaks 8.30.1 and betterleaks 1.8.1 measurably cannot read a compressed env blob, so retiring it would return the repo to a scanner-clean-but-unscanned state. Keep as-is; the only edits this file needs are findings 1-3.
- **`rule-tool-currency-and-native-first`** — `rule-tool-currency-and-native-first-3` Required justification: the rule's core directive is a judgment, and judgment has no native implementation at any of the host's versions or the repo's pins. The version-currency MECHANICS were already retired into the shared engine (rule lines 78-91), which is precisely this rule applied to itself, so nothing custom is left to delete on that axis. What remains — 'does this custom module/manager/snapshot still need to exist?' — is answered today only by a human reading a changelog; the two closest native surfaces are `mise outdated` (version drift, already delegated) and Renovate's changelog-carrying PRs (already delegated). Keep the rule; the two refactors above widen its scope (finding -1) and give one slice of its manual hunt a measured input (finding -2).
- **`rule-use-tool-builtins`** — `rule-use-tool-builtins-4` Required justification for the keep: this is a judgment gate over an open-ended decision ("does something already do this?"), and no harness surface can decide it. A permission rule matches command strings, a hook matches tool inputs, a settings key toggles a fixed behaviour, an agent field scopes a delegate — none can tell custom code that duplicates a built-in from custom code that does not, because the answer lives in a third party's changelog, not in the tool call. `/doctor` is the only native feature that acts on this class of file and it acts on the wrong axis (context cost, not correctness). One caution follows from that: `/doctor` would propose migrating this always-loaded rule into a skill, and per .claude/rules/md-size-budgets.md § "Scoping: the trigger test" that proposal must be declined — the rule is behaviour-triggered (it fires when custom code is about to be written, which no glob and no relevance match predicts), so a skill or a `paths:` scope would make it absent exactly when it is needed. It stays eager and stays prose; findings 1-3 sharpen it rather than replace it.
- **`rule-verify-before-advancing`** — `rule-verify-before-advancing-6` Justified keep: at 2.1.266 the harness still surfaces background-task completion as a status label, not an exit code, and the field table proves a hook could not substitute for the file-based rc. The rule is the only layer covering this failure mode, and it has fired at least twice in real sessions.
- **`rule-zero-bash-logic`** — `rule-zero-bash-logic-1` Required justification: the gate's two teeth are a per-file numeric budget and a bidirectional allowlist/tracked-set reconciliation (`stale`). No native mechanism in any pinned tool expresses either — hk has no such builtin (control-armed 0 vs 75) and the harness's permission grammar is path-shaped, not count-shaped. The python enforcer is also the only form that does not itself violate the policy (bash_budget.py:28-31). Keep as-is.
- **`rule-zero-skip-policy`** — `rule-zero-skip-policy-5` Required justification: the rule's trigger is a decision, not a file read and not a tool call, so no hook event, permission rule, agent field, or settings key can fire on it — the harness has no 'about to dismiss a warning' surface at 2.1.266, and the changelog and index gap digests confirm none shipped in the version window. Its own § "Why this rule is eager" already records the measured cost of the alternative (scoped until 2026-07-15, therefore absent from exactly the sessions it governs). Keep the directive eager and unscoped; findings 1-3 trim what has since become mechanically enforced, which is the only lever available.
- **`shell-scripts`** — `shell-scripts-10` Justification, not default: this is the shape the zero-bash-logic rule explicitly sanctions — a resolve-and-exec shim with zero decision logic, whose entire body is a uv presence check and one exec, and whose nudge-rewriting core already lives in python and is unit-tested. Nothing native can replace it because a settings.json hook is a single command string and the alternative is the identical bash inlined into JSON, where it is harder to read, shellcheck-invisible, and outside the bash budget. Its one questionable line is the interpreter check, which shell-scripts-7's probe also covers. `shell-scripts-11` Required justification: this is the one script that CANNOT be python — it is the code that installs python. Every other line is a documented native mechanism being invoked (`mise install`, `uv python install`, `uv sync`, `$CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`), so there is no homegrown logic to migrate. One correction rides along from shell-scripts-7: its header claim that an absent interpreter makes the harness "fail closed, blocking EVERY Bash call" (scripts/web-setup.sh:7-10) contradicts hooks.md:833/836 — the script is still worth having (the gates genuinely need the toolchain), but the urgency framing should be fixed rather than repeated.
- **`skills-1`** — `skills-1-10` Required justification: the native review surface is an ENGINE, this skill is a CONTROLLER, and no native feature occupies the controller slot. `/code-review` at any effort level answers "what is wrong with this diff" — which is precisely the unbounded round-1 question this skill measures as non-terminating (:22-26, six inconclusive rounds on #601). Nothing bundled or in a marketplace supplies a cardinality test, a completion-over-emptiness stop condition, or the re-open clause; those are derived from a measurement of this repo's own review history and are not reconstructible from a vendor doc. Two adoption notes rather than a supersession: (1) `/code-review` is a legitimate ENGINE for the round-1 open-hunting slot the skill already sanctions at :53-54, so the round-1 template could name it instead of implying a hand-briefed agent; (2) `context: fork` + `agent:` frontmatter (skills.md:347-348) would let the skill dispatch its own bounded round in a forked subagent rather than instructing the caller to do it by hand — worth considering, but it changes the skill from advisory to executing, which is a deliberate design choice and not an audit finding. `skills-1-11` Required justification: these two are the reference implementation of the shape this audit is looking for, and there is nothing native to move them onto. Each is the top of the mandated three-layer stack (skill -> mise task -> python library, .claude/rules/agent-artifact-conventions.md rule 6), each carries only the non-derivable judgement, and both non-obvious failure modes they document are the kind a native tool would not tell you: blast-radius:35-39 (graphify prints "No unique node match" at rc 0, which is a DIFFERENT answer from "No affected nodes found" — read the message, not the exit code) and devcontainer-sync:53 (`registry: UNREACHABLE` means staleness is UNKNOWN, so a green run is not base-currency evidence). Both are exactly the control-arm discipline the repo's rules demand, encoded where it gets read. One nit, not a disposition change: blast-radius:67-73 self-flags that it was hand-written rather than authored via `/skill-creator:skill-creator` because a codex lane cannot invoke that slash command — that disclosure is correct and should stay. `skills-1-12` Required justification, one per skill. (a) bake-action-set-precedence-expertise: nothing native or pinned knows that `set:` beats `push:` in docker/bake-action — it is a third-party composite action's internal precedence, invisible to actionlint/zizmor/ghalint, and it cost three PRs (#34-#36) of green-CI-but-no-image to diagnose. A 38-line note is the right size for it and there is no cheaper carrier. The only strengthening available is a machine gate (an ast-grep or hk pattern rejecting an unconditional `*.output=type=cacheonly` in a bake-action `set:` block), which would be an ADDITION, not a replacement — the skill would still carry the why. (b) context7-cli: keep as the repo's single ctx7 wrapper (it is the survivor in skills-1-2), and update one number — the caveat says "verified on the pinned 0.5.5" while the pin is 0.5.9. I re-armed it rather than repeating the inherited claim: the deprecation is STILL true on 0.5.9, hidden from `--help` but still executing at rc 0. Change `0.5.5` to `0.5.9` and keep the "absence from --help is NOT proof they are gone" warning, which the re-probe confirms is still the correct reading. `skills-1-9` Required negative answer to the unit's explicit question, stated with its measurement rather than assumed: NO description in this unit exceeds the 1,536-char cap, so no skill in skills-1 is being silently truncated out of discoverability. Keep the descriptions as they are. The caveat worth recording is that the cap is not the only pressure — skills.md:1052 says the per-entry cap applies "regardless of budget", and the LISTING budget (1% of context, shared across all 35 skills in .claude/skills/ plus every enabled plugin's) can shorten descriptions before any individual one hits 1,536.
