This is not hypothetical — this audit runs inside a subagent, where AskUserQuestion is stripped by sub-agents.md:382's filter, so an agent obeying the literal text emits a call that cannot land and has no sanctioned way to surface a fork. The corroborating project memory (`AskUserQuestion is STRIPPED from every subagent`, feedback_orchestration_process_lessons / project_session_2026-09-01) now has a vendor-doc anchor, so the caveat can be stated with a citation rather than as folklore.
- **`rule-clarify-before-acting-3`** (refactor, conf 0.8, 1/3 refuted) — Rule 5 — 'Keep asking until sure. A second clarifying round is cheaper than rework' (.claude/rules/clarify-before-acting.md:64-66) — assumes a question stays open until the user answers it, so an unanswered ask is a blocked turn rather than a silent go-ahead.
  - **Native:** The harness now ships `askUserQuestionTimeout` (`60s` / `5m` / `10m`, user or managed settings, also on the `/config` 'Question auto-continue timeout' row). After the idle window the dialog closes on its own, submits any options already selected, and 'tells Claude you may be away from your keyboard, so Claude proceeds on its own judgment and can re-ask later'. The rule should note that an auto-continued question is NOT an answer — the agent must treat it as unresolved ambiguity and re-ask or stop, not as tacit approval — and that the timeout never applies to permission prompts or plan approval.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/clarify-before-acting.md:64-66
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:130-137 ('### Question auto-continue timeout ... set the `askUserQuestionTimeout` setting to `60s`, `5m`, or `10m` ... it submits any options you'd already selected and tells Claude you may be away from your keyboard, so Claude proceeds on its own judgment ... The timeout applies only to `AskUserQuestion`'s multiple-choice questions; permission prompts, including plan approval, never auto-resolve on idle'); .../claude-code/settings-reference.md:602 and :2759 (the `askUserQuestionTimeout` setting entry).
  - **Rationale:** Category (c): the harness can now close the question for the user and hand control back with an explicit 'proceed on your own judgment' framing — the exact outcome rule 1 exists to prevent. The rule is not superseded (nothing native decides the ambiguity), but it must name the timeout so an auto-continue is read as 'still unresolved', not as consent. Confidence held below 0.9 because the setting is opt-in and this repo has not set it — I did not read the user settings.json, so whether it is currently active here is unverified.

### `rule-clean-git-state`

**Motivating defect:** A file deleted on disk but not staged still exists in CI's checkout — the agnix/dockerfile-reviewer.md CI failure of 2026-04-05.

- **`rule-clean-git-state-1`** (refactor, conf 0.82, 0/3 refuted) — The asserted tool fact "New files must be `git add`-ed before hk runs, or hk won't check them" — the rule's justification for manually staging new files before validating.
  - **Native:** hk 1.57's own file selection: under `--all` with no stash, hk unions the git index with the untracked-file set, so untracked/new files ARE checked without staging. The `check` hook declares no `stash`, so stash resolves to None.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/clean-git-state.md:24 ("3. New files must be `git add`-ed before hk runs, or hk won't check them"); the validation command the rule points at is `mise run lint` (.claude/rules/clean-git-state.md:16), which is `hk run check --all` (python/src/dotfiles_setup/lint.py:66 `HK_COMMAND = ("hk", "run", "check", "--all")`) — the same command CI runs (.github/workflows/ci.yml:113).
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/src/hook.rs:1683-1688 (`} else if opts.all { ... let mut all_files = repo.lock().await.all_files(None)?; if !stash { all_files.extend(git_status.untracked_files.iter().cloned()); }`); stash resolution /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/src/hook.rs:637-646 + hk.pkl:748-752 (the `check` hook sets no `stash`, unlike `pre-commit` at hk.pkl:712 `stash = "git"`); default confirmed at /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/docs/environment_variables.md:319-326 (`HK_STASH_UNTRACKED` Default: `true`; only when set to false do "Untracked files ... not appear in reports or `hk check --all` results") and /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/src/env.rs:62.
  - **Rationale:** The claim is stale for the path the rule actually prescribes. It remains TRUE for the pre-commit hook path only — `defaults_to_staged_files()` returns true just for `pre-commit` (hook.rs:649-651) and that branch takes `git_status.staged_files` alone (hook.rs:1688-1691). That is the control arm: the same function yields the other answer for the other hook, so the distinction is real, not a mis-read. Refactor line 24 to scope the claim to the commit-time hook and say plainly that `mise run lint` (`hk check --all`) already sees untracked files, so a new file needs no `git add` merely to be linted.
- **`rule-clean-git-state-2`** (refactor, conf 0.75, 0/3 refuted) — The manual "Before Every Commit" checklist — run `git diff --name-only` / `git diff --cached --name-only` by hand to verify "what hk checked locally matches what CI will see".
  - **Native:** Two mechanisms already do this without a human diff: (1) hk's own pre-commit stash — `stash = "git"` makes hk remove ALL unstaged worktree changes for the duration of the run, so the steps see exactly the index content that will be committed and that CI will check out; (2) `mise run ship`'s preflight, which hard-refuses a non-clean working tree before any gate runs.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/clean-git-state.md:18-24.
  - **Evidence (native):** hk.pkl:710-712 (`["pre-commit"] { fix = true; stash = "git" }`); stash execution /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/hk/src/hook.rs:1288-1307 ("Stash ALL unstaged changes in the repository (not only files under consideration) so that unrelated worktree changes do not affect or get affected by fixers"); ship gate python/src/dotfiles_setup/pr.py:485-501 (`_working_tree_clean` -> "FAIL  ship: working tree not clean — commit (or stash) first so the gates validate exactly what ships").
  - **Rationale:** The rule predates both layers and still reads as if the human is the only mechanism. It should keep its directive but delegate the enforcement: name hk's `stash = "git"` as what guarantees commit-time local==CI content, and `mise run ship`'s clean-tree refusal as the push-time gate, then drop the two by-hand `git diff` steps to a one-line 'if you want to look, here is how'. Not a full retire: neither mechanism covers the ad-hoc `mise run lint` run that the rule's first section is about (the `check` hook does not stash), so the discipline still has a live window.
- **`rule-clean-git-state-3`** (refactor, conf 0.7, 0/3 refuted) — The per-file manual instruction "Stage ALL file deletions: `git add <deleted-file>`" and "Stage ALL file modifications you intend to commit" as separate enumerated human steps.
  - **Native:** git's own `git add -u` / `--update`: "update tracked files" — stages every tracked modification AND deletion in one command, and, unlike `-A`/`git add .`, adds nothing untracked, so it does not collide with the repo's ban on bulk-adding phantom `.agent/state/**` files.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/clean-git-state.md:11-15 and the table row .claude/rules/clean-git-state.md:30 ("File deleted on disk, not staged | File exists in CI | `git add <deleted-file>`").
  - **Evidence (native):** .agent/kb/raw/git-add-update-flag-probe.md (saved probe of the host's git 2.50.1: `-u, --[no-]update  update tracked files`; `-A, --[no-]all  add changes from all tracked and untracked files`); the bulk-add ban is .claude/rules/do-not.md #5 ("Do NOT bulk `git add .`"), which `-u` does not violate.
  - **Rationale:** The rule asks a human to enumerate deletions one by one when git ships the exact primitive — and the enumeration is the step that actually fails (a missed deletion is precisely the 2026-04-05 agnix/dockerfile-reviewer.md incident the rule cites). Replace steps 2+3 with `git add -u` plus explicit `git add <path>` for genuinely new files, and note why `-A`/`.` is still forbidden. Keep the rule; change the mechanism it prescribes.

### `rule-do-not`

**Motivating defect:** The accumulated project invariants: GUI-launched IDEs not inheriting terminal env, local base builds, raw docker lifecycle, stderr suppression, bulk `git add .` staging phantom `.agent/state/**`, `gh run watch --exit-status` reporting 0 prematurely, docker context drift, bare `graphify install` mutating `~/.claude`, and a whole session's work accumulating on `main` (three times, twice straight after `mise run land`, which leaves you on main).

- **`rule-do-not-1`** (refactor, conf 0.93, 0/3 refuted) — Entry 11's rationale asserts a harness cost fact: "A registered server taxes **every** conversation's system prompt with **every** tool's schema, forever" — used as the reason to avoid native MCP registration for our own lookups.
  - **Native:** MCP tool search: MCP tools are deferred and discovered on demand by default, so a registered server's schemas are NOT in the system prompt; only tool names are listed and the schema loads via ToolSearch. Per-server opt-out exists (`alwaysLoad`), and the deferral requires Sonnet/Haiku/Opus 4.5+ — satisfied by this host's Opus 5.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/do-not.md:79-81 ("A registered server taxes **every** conversation's system prompt with **every** tool's schema, forever"); the sibling rule already retired the same sentence at .claude/rules/research-doc-sources.md:97-100 ("the old 'every schema in every conversation, forever' cost is FALSE here ... Do not cite that sentence").
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/mcp.md:1354 ("## Scale with MCP tool search"), :1376 ("Tool search is enabled by default: MCP tools are deferred and discovered on demand"), :1393 (unset => "All MCP tools deferred and loaded on demand"), :1380 (model requirement: Sonnet/Haiku/Opus 4.5 and later), :1421 (`alwaysLoad` opt-out for the small set that must load upfront).
  - **Rationale:** The DIRECTIVE (prefer the tool's CLI / a plain HTTP API / mcp2cli over registering a server for our own problems) survives on the grounds do-not.md's own sibling gives it — a spawned process, a pin, an auth path and a doctor failure mode — but the stated REASON is a stale harness fact at 2.1.266 and is contradicted, by name, by another eager rule in the same corpus. Two eager rules asserting opposite facts about the same mechanism is exactly the drift this audit exists to catch. Rewrite entry 11's rationale to cite tool search + `alwaysLoad` and the real cost (operational surface, not context tax), or delegate the whole rationale to research-doc-sources.md § 'MCP: two lanes' which already carries the corrected version.
- **`rule-do-not-2`** (refactor, conf 0.88, 0/3 refuted) — Entry 8's parenthetical harness/tool fact: "`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is NOT containment (it redirects the skill dir only; that write is hardcoded)" — the justification for the blanket 'run every `graphify <platform> install` in a throwaway directory' habit.
  - **Native:** graphify itself now honours `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for the always-on Claude registration, not just the skill directory: at the repo's pinned graphify 0.9.53 the global branch writes `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/CLAUDE.md`, and only the no-env-var branch falls through to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. The fix shipped in 0.9.44, i.e. BEFORE the pin.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/do-not.md:34-38 (entry 8, the `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` claim at :36-38).
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/graphify/graphify/install.py:640-652 (comment: "Honor CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for the global (non-project) case, same as _platform_skill_destination does for the skill copy path (#527) -- this always-on registration path was missed by that fix (#2694)"; `elif os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR")` branch writes `config_dir / "CLAUDE.md"`); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/graphify/CHANGELOG.md:142 ("`graphify install` (Claude always-on) now writes the CLAUDE.md registration into `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` ... instead of always mutating the default `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`") and :134 ("the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR half shipped in 0.9.44"); pin confirmed at /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/graphify/pyproject.toml:7 (version = "0.9.53").
  - **Rationale:** The prohibition itself stays true — a BARE `graphify install` with no `--project` and no `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` still writes `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` (install.py:651-652) — but the stated reason 'that write is hardcoded' is false at the version this repo pins, and it is the reason the rule escalates to 'throwaway directory outside this repo'. Correct the parenthetical to: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` redirects both the skill dir and the CLAUDE.md registration since 0.9.44, so it IS containment for the profile write; the residual hazard is the codex/AGENTS.md path (which `--project` does not fix and our size gate rejects), and that is what still justifies the throwaway-dir escalation. Leaving the stale half in place means the next session either distrusts a working containment mechanism or distrusts the whole entry.
- **`rule-do-not-3`** (refactor, conf 0.72, 0/3 refuted) — Entries 2, 3 and 5 (`mise run build` / `docker buildx bake dev-load` locally; raw `docker run/exec/stop/rm/build` for devcontainer lifecycle; bulk `git add .`) are enforced only by prose in this ADR plus the PreToolUse `hook_guard`, which this repo documents as failing OPEN on its own errors.
  - **Native:** `permissions.deny` Bash pattern rules in `.claude/settings.json` — e.g. `Bash(docker buildx bake dev-load*)`, `Bash(mise run build)`, `Bash(docker run:*)`, `Bash(git add .)`. Deny rules are evaluated before allow rules, block in EVERY permission mode including `bypassPermissions`, and cannot be overridden by a PreToolUse hook returning `allow`.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/do-not.md:13-14 (entry 2), :16-18 (entry 3), :23-24 (entry 5); the fail-open property is stated in .claude/rules/mise-tasks-only.md § 'Enforcement layers' ("The hook fails OPEN on its own errors ... Hard bans that must never fail open belong in settings.json permission deny rules, not the hook"); the repo already uses deny rules for exactly this shape at .claude/settings.json:23-39 (`Bash(chezmoi apply:*)`, the plan-attest set).
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/permission-modes.md:30 ("Deny rules block in every mode, including `bypassPermissions`. Allow rules have no effect in `bypassPermissions`."); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/permissions.md:495 ("Hook decisions don't bypass permission rules ... a matching deny rule blocks the call") and :68 (scoped rule semantics, `Bash(rm *)`).
  - **Rationale:** These three entries are hard, never-bend invariants with a stable command shape — precisely the class the repo's own doctrine says belongs in `permissions.deny` rather than in a fail-open hook or in prose. The native mechanism exists, is already used in this settings file for chezmoi and plan-attest, and is strictly stronger (deny-first precedence, survives bypassPermissions, survives a broken guard script). Entry 3 needs a scoped rule, not a bare `Bash` deny, because `docker ps/logs/info` must stay allowed — write it as narrow verb patterns and keep the prose entry as the WHY. This is an adopt-the-native-mechanism refactor, not a retirement: the ADR text still has to explain the invariant.
- **`rule-do-not-4`** (refactor, conf 0.62, 1/3 refuted) — Entry 8's prescribed habit for containing a third-party installer's writes: 'Run any `graphify <platform> install` in a **throwaway directory outside this repo**, never here' — a remembered human/agent procedure with no machine layer.
  - **Native:** Sandbox filesystem isolation: `sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite` (e.g. `["~/.claude"]`) is enforced at the OS level for every sandboxed Bash command AND its child processes — which is the only layer that can stop graphify, since it is a Python subprocess writing files itself and Read/Edit deny rules explicitly do not reach those.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/do-not.md:40-43.
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/sandboxing.md:190 ("You can also deny write or read access using `sandbox.filesystem.denyWrite` and `sandbox.filesystem.denyRead`") and :172 ("These paths are enforced at the OS level, so all commands running inside the sandbox, including their child processes, respect them"); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/permissions.md:319 ("Read and Edit deny rules ... don't apply to arbitrary subprocesses that read or write files indirectly, like a Python or Node script that opens files itself. For OS-level enforcement that blocks all processes from accessing a path, enable the sandbox").
  - **Rationale:** The rule's own escalation ('throwaway directory') exists because no layer below it could catch a subprocess write to `~/.claude`. The harness now has exactly that layer, and the docs name this failure mode verbatim. Adopting it converts entry 8 from a remembered habit into a machine-enforced boundary that also covers every OTHER tool that writes outside the repo. It is a refactor rather than a retirement for two reasons: the sandbox only binds sandboxed Bash commands (a session run without `sandbox.enabled`, or a command that falls back to unsandboxed, is uncovered), and the codex/AGENTS.md half of entry 8 is a size-gate problem the sandbox does not address.
- **`rule-do-not-5`** (refactor, conf 0.55, 0/3 refuted) — Entry 9's branch-first enforcement stack — the custom PreToolUse `branch_guard` denying `Edit`/`Write`/`NotebookEdit` on a repo file while on the default branch, plus the manual recovery recipe (`git branch <new> && git reset --hard origin/main`).
  - **Native:** Git worktrees are now first-class in the harness: `claude --worktree <name>` starts the session in `.claude/worktrees/<name>/` on a NEW branch `worktree-<name>`, and mid-session Claude can create one itself with the `EnterWorktree` tool. A session started that way structurally cannot write to the default branch's checkout, so 'branch BEFORE the first edit' becomes the session's starting state rather than a deny that fires after the fact.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/do-not.md:45-66 (entry 9; the guard at :58-62, the recovery at :47-49).
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/worktrees.md:21 ("Pass `--worktree` or `-w` with a name to create an isolated worktree and start Claude in it ... on a new branch named `worktree-<name>`"), :41 ("You can also ask Claude to 'work in a worktree' during a session, and it creates one with the `EnterWorktree` tool"), :12 (desktop app gives every new session its own worktree automatically).
  - **Rationale:** Native worktrees cover the ENTRY path that entry 9 says keeps failing — the two recorded relapses both happened straight after `mise run land`, which leaves the session on `main`; a `--worktree` launch would have made that state unreachable. They do not cover the whole rule: a session legitimately launched in the main checkout still needs `branch_guard`, and the branch name the harness picks (`worktree-<name>`) is not the repo's `feat/...` convention, so `ship` would need to tolerate or rename it. So: adopt `--worktree` as the documented default launch for implementation work and keep the guard as the backstop — do not retire the guard. One caveat the ADR must carry if it adopts this: hook `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` does NOT follow the worktree (worktrees.md:46-49), and every guard in this repo is invoked as `bash "${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}/scripts/..."` (.claude/settings.json:56-58) — the #343 fail-open-off-root defect class.

### `rule-gh-cli-watch`

**Motivating defect:** `cmd | grep -q PAT` under `set -o pipefail` returns 141 when the match SUCCEEDS — a check that can only fail. That broke the #289 base build and is now the `no_grep_q_under_pipefail` hk step.

- **`rule-gh-cli-watch-1`** (refactor, conf 0.88, 0/3 refuted) — The rule's 'Canonical patterns' section prescribes the three commands an agent should run to wait on CI: `gh pr checks 123 --watch --interval 30`, `gh pr checks 123 --watch --fail-fast`, `gh run watch 1234567890 --exit-status`, and `gh pr checks --watch`.
  - **Native:** In-repo canonical mise tasks, machine-enforced: the live PreToolUse guard DENIES both `gh run watch` and `gh pr checks ... --watch` and redirects to `mise run ship` (watches PR checks to bucket-verified green) / `mise run land -- <PR#>` (watches main CI via --json buckets), leaving only the one-shot `gh pr checks <n> --json` and `gh run view <id> --json conclusion` reads allowed. The guard's own deny message cites THIS rule as its authority, but the rule never names the mise verbs.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:31, .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:34, .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:41, .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:49
  - **Evidence (native):** python/src/dotfiles_setup/hook_guard.py:404-412 (Rule "gh run watch", deny message names `mise run land -- <PR#>` and cites .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md); python/src/dotfiles_setup/hook_guard.py:413-421 (Rule "gh pr checks --watch", deny message names `mise run ship`); .claude/rules/mise-tasks-only.md table rows `gh run watch <id>` -> `mise run land -- <PR#>` and `gh pr checks ... --watch` -> ship/land already watch
  - **Rationale:** Every command the eager rule holds up as the canonical thing to do is denied for agents by a guard that cites this rule as its justification. An agent that reads only this rule writes a command the harness rejects, and the deny cancels the whole compound command. The rule should lead with `mise run ship` / `mise run land` for agents, keep `gh ... --watch` explicitly scoped to a human's long-running terminal, and name the allowed one-shot JSON reads. Nothing upstream changed here; the repo's own mechanism moved out from under the rule.
- **`rule-gh-cli-watch-3`** (refactor, conf 0.62, 1/3 refuted) — The rule's headline ban on hand-rolled `while ! gh ... ; do sleep 30; done` poll loops, and its anti-pattern block, stated unconditionally for 'all scripts, hooks, skills, agents, and ad-hoc Bash invocations in this repo'.
  - **Native:** Partially covered natively, but NOT by a block: Claude Code never auto-backgrounds a command that starts with `sleep` (it stops it at the timeout instead), so a detached sleep-poll degrades rather than being refused — control-armed live on this host, `sleep 1; echo rc=$?` returned rc=0, so a leading `sleep` is executed, not denied. The genuine native substitute for the wait-on-a-condition shape is the `Monitor` tool (see finding 2). The pipefail half of the ban (`cmd | grep -q PAT` returning 141) has no native cover and stays repo-enforced by hk.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:3-5, .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:52-59, .claude/rules/gh-cli-watch.md:64-68
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:179-181 ('Claude Code never auto-backgrounds three kinds of command. It stops them at the timeout instead: * A command that starts with `sleep`.'); tools-reference.md:315 (Monitor polls a PR or CI job); hk.pkl:232 (`no_grep_q_under_pipefail` step, still present)
  - **Rationale:** The unconditional ban now contradicts a sibling eager rule: .claude/rules/long-running-command-hangs.md:36-43 PRESCRIBES an in-turn `while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do grep -q RC "$LOG" && break; sleep 15; done` poll for Mac-side container ops, because backgrounding gets those reaped. Two eager rules, opposite instructions, no carve-out in either. The harness has not made the sleep-poll safe (probe above: it runs, it is merely never auto-backgrounded), so the fix is not to relax the ban but to scope it — 'never poll a GHA run/PR when gh has a --watch flag or a mise verb; for a local condition-wait use Monitor, or the bounded in-turn poll that long-running-command-hangs.md defines' — and cross-link the two rules.

### `rule-goal-history`

**Motivating defect:** Goal history being rewritten/squashed, and two writers mutating one repository after a Desktop task restarted while a fallback subagent still owned it.

- **`rule-goal-history-2`** (refactor, conf 0.6, 1/3 refuted) — The append trigger is a manual habit: "After an accepted goal change, orchestration-topology change, major milestone, landing, or handoff, append one iteration to `docs/agents/goal-history.md` before advancing." Nothing fires at the moment of advancing; the validator only runs when a human invokes `mise run session-review`.
  - **Native:** A `Stop` hook, the only per-turn event with decision control — it can refuse to end the turn and feed a reason back to Claude. For a judgment-shaped trigger ("did this turn accept a goal change, topology change, landing or handoff?") the native `type: "prompt"` hook form evaluates the condition on a model and returns `ok:false` + `reason`, which is fed back so Claude keeps working; `impossible: true` is the documented escape so the turn can still end.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/goal-history.md:3-5 (the directive); mise.toml:1478,1493 ([tasks.session-review] -> `dotfiles-setup session-review`, operator-invoked); .claude/skills/session-review/SKILL.md:10-14 (invocation is a manual command list); .claude/settings.json hooks block contains PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded and NO Stop entry, so no per-turn gate exists.
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/hooks.md:2458 (### Stop — "Runs when the main Claude Code agent has finished responding"); hooks.md:2530 (#### Stop decision control — "`Stop` and `SubagentStop` hooks can control whether Claude continues"); hooks-guide.md:841-850 (## Prompt-based hooks — `type: "prompt"`, model-evaluated, `ok:false` on Stop feeds the reason back unless `impossible:true`); hooks.md:1025 (SessionEnd has "No decision control", so the repo's existing SessionEnd hook could not carry this).
  - **Rationale:** The rule's enforcement story is strong for CONTENT (the byte-level validator, finding 3) and empty for TIMING: `before advancing` is carried by prose alone, and the session's own hook config proves no per-turn gate is wired. `Stop` is the documented event for exactly this — it is the only per-turn hook that can block, and its prompt-based form handles the judgment trigger that no deterministic matcher can express (the same machinery the harness itself uses for `/goal`, per goal.md:120 "`/goal` is a wrapper around a session-scoped prompt-based Stop hook"). Confidence is held at 0.6 rather than higher because a naive Stop hook fires on every turn and most turns are not goal changes, so the adoption is a prompt-based hook with a narrow condition (and an `impossible` escape), not a blanket blocker — a design decision, not a mechanical swap.
- **`rule-goal-history-4`** (refactor, conf 0.5, 0/3 refuted) — The rule's unqualified use of "goal" — "an accepted goal change", "Prior goal digest", "Current goal digest", "the current goal text", and the artifact name `docs/agents/goal-history.md` — written before the harness shipped a command of the same name and with different semantics.
  - **Native:** The native `/goal` command: a session-scoped completion condition (one per session) evaluated after every turn by the small fast model, with `/goal` (status), `/goal clear`, an `◎ /goal active` indicator, restoration across `--continue`/`--resume`, and achieved/failed entries written to the transcript.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/goal-history.md:3, :7-12 (field labels `Prior goal digest` / `Current goal digest`, "A digest identifies exact goal text"), :24-27 ("distinguish an accepted decision from verified delivery").
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/goal.md:9 ("The `/goal` command sets a completion condition..."), goal.md:38 ("One goal can be active per session"), goal.md:68-86 (status output), goal.md:88-98 (`/goal clear`), goal.md:100-104 (restore on resume), goal.md:120-124 (evaluator verdicts recorded in the transcript).
  - **Rationale:** Not a superseded mechanism — the two things do not overlap in function (finding 3 establishes that) — but a live ambiguity introduced by the harness after this rule was written. An agent that reads "append one iteration ... after an accepted goal change" with `/goal` in context can plausibly read the rule as being about session goal state, or conversely can run `/goal` and believe the durable record was updated. The cheap fix is one disambiguating clause in the rule ("goal here means the repo's tracked objective, not the session-scoped `/goal` completion condition"), which costs a few bytes against the rule_unscoped budget and removes the collision. Held at 0.5 because this is a clarity finding, not a defect: nothing currently mis-fires, and the rule's own text is internally consistent.

### `rule-graphify-first`

**Motivating defect:** Broad source search when a fresh graph could answer, plus the two graphify installs drifting: nothing records WHICH graphify built the graph bytes, and an earlier rebuild-stamp check could only ever record what `graphify-update` always resolves, so it could never fail.

- **`rule-graphify-first-1`** (refactor, conf 0.95, 0/3 refuted) — The rule's headline dated fact: "**The two installs are aligned as of 2026-08-31 — both 0.9.53.**" (.claude/rules/graphify-first.md:16-17), with the whole "Nothing records WHICH graphify built the graph" section resting on the two installs currently agreeing.
  - **Native:** No native harness feature — this is a stale FACT, not a superseded mechanism. The user-global pin has moved to 0.9.56 while the repo pin stayed at 0.9.53, so the alignment the rule records has ended and the divergence the rule warns about is live today.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/graphify-first.md:16-23; the repo pin it names is python/pyproject.toml:9 `"graphifyy[all]==0.9.53"` and python/pyproject.toml:57 `override-dependencies = ["graphifyy[all]==0.9.53"]`.
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/.config/mise/config.toml:290 `"pipx:graphifyy" = { version = "0.9.56", extras = ["all"], minimum_release_age = "0s" }`. Live probe (control-armed): `command -v graphify` -> `/Users/rmanaloto/.local/share/mise/installs/pipx-graphifyy/0.9.56/bin/graphify` (positive arm `command -v mise` -> resolves; negative arm `command -v qzzxwv7` -> ABSENT), so bare-PATH graphify is 0.9.56 vs the repo's 0.9.53. Upstream latest is also 0.9.56 per .agent/kb/raw/graphify-readme-0.9.56.digest.md (0 new capabilities).
  - **Rationale:** The rule explicitly says to treat the alignment as "a fact with a date on it, not an invariant" — and it has now expired. Rewrite lines 16-23 to state the CURRENT state (PATH 0.9.56 vs repo 0.9.53, diverged) or bump python/pyproject.toml to 0.9.56 to restore alignment. Leaving it as-is is worse than silence: a reader who trusts the sentence concludes a bare `graphify update .` would at least have built the graph with the same version, which is now false. Note the bump is blocked by finding 5's hardcoded literal.
- **`rule-graphify-first-3`** (refactor, conf 0.9, 0/3 refuted) — The rule presents its opening directive — "Before broad source search, run `mise run graphify-health`" — as a manual habit, and says the guarantee is "procedural, not enforced". It never mentions that a PreToolUse hook layer now injects that orientation automatically on every search and read.
  - **Native:** The native `PreToolUse` hook event with `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` — already wired in this repo on the `Bash|Grep` and `Read|Glob` matchers to `scripts/graphify-hook-guard.sh`, which execs graphify's own native `hook-guard` subcommand and rewrites its nudge copy to this repo's mise tasks. Its escalation path is also native and config-only: strict mode via the `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT`/`_TTL` env vars set in settings.json's `env` block, no code change.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/graphify-first.md:3-9 and :36-43 (no reference anywhere in the file to a hook, to scripts/graphify-hook-guard.sh, or to strict mode).
  - **Evidence (native):** .claude/settings.json:64-68 (`"matcher": "Bash|Grep"` -> `graphify-hook-guard.sh search`) and :74-78 (`"matcher": "Read|Glob"` -> `graphify-hook-guard.sh read`); scripts/graphify-hook-guard.sh:1-30 (thin fail-open wrapper; line 16 documents `GRAPHIFY_HOOK_STRICT/_TTL` as an env var, not a code change); python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:564-575 `rewrite_hook_nudge`. Harness doc: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/hooks.md:972 "The `additionalContext` field passes a string from your hook into Claude's context window... inserts it into the conversation at the point where the hook fired." Observed live this session: every Bash call returned `PreToolUse:Bash hook additional context: MANDATORY: graphify-out/graph.json exists. You MUST run mise run graphify-query...`.
  - **Rationale:** The rule is stale about its own enforcement topology: what it describes as an unaided habit is already carried, per-tool-call, by a native hook the repo wires — and a reader following the file alone would not know the layer exists, nor that strict mode is one settings key away. This is the load-bearing half of the rule that IS now mechanized; the un-mechanized half is finding 2's bare-binary ban. Add a short "Enforcement layers" paragraph naming the hook and strict mode, so the eager bytes describe the real system.
- **`rule-graphify-first-2`** (refactor, conf 0.85, 1/3 refuted) — The ban on the bare binary is carried by prose alone: "**Always the mise tasks, never a bare `graphify` on `PATH`.**" and "Never run a global Graphify binary or installer as a substitute for the project tasks" — self-described as "**procedural, not enforced**" and enforced "by convention, not by verification".
  - **Native:** A native `permissions.deny` rule — `"Bash(graphify *)"` plus the bare `"Bash(graphify)"` — which blocks deterministically in EVERY permission mode, including bypassPermissions, and needs no custom code. The repo already uses exactly this idiom for the same class of ban (`Bash(chezmoi apply:*)`).
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/graphify-first.md:10-12, :36-43. Control-armed: `grep -rn graphify python/src/dotfiles_setup/hook_guard.py` returns 0 hits (the PreToolUse guard that denies `gh pr merge`, `--no-verify`, etc. has no graphify rule), and .claude/settings.json's `permissions.deny` (line 23ff) lists chezmoi/plan-attest entries but nothing for graphify.
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/permission-modes.md:30 "Deny rules block in every mode, including `bypassPermissions`."; permissions.md:148-151 (wildcard form, `*` after the program/subcommand); permissions.md:235 "A deny or ask rule matches past any leading assignment, so `Bash(rm *)` in deny still matches `FOO=bar rm -rf tmp/`"; permissions.md:239-241 confirms environment runners (`mise exec`, `npx`, `uv`-style wrappers) are NOT stripped, so the sanctioned routes `mise run graphify-*` and `uv run --project python dotfiles-setup graphify *` do not match the rule and keep working. Repo precedent: .claude/settings.json:23-25.
  - **Rationale:** The rule states its own weakness ("procedural, not enforced") but a native, zero-code, mode-proof enforcement layer exists and is already in use elsewhere in this same settings file. Finding 1 makes the gap consequential rather than theoretical: with PATH graphify now at 0.9.56 and the repo at 0.9.53, one bare `graphify update .` silently produces graph bytes from a different builder, and by the rule's own account nothing records it. Add the deny pair to .claude/settings.json and have the rule cite it instead of asserting convention.
- **`rule-graphify-first-4`** (refactor, conf 0.85, 0/3 refuted) — The rule correctly records that the self-authored builder-version stamp was REMOVED ("An earlier version of this rule claimed a rebuild stamp closed that gap; it did not... It was removed rather than kept as a check that always reports 'fine'"), but the mise task the rule points readers at still advertises the stamp as present.
  - **Native:** No native feature is involved — this is stale wiring copy that must follow the code. The native surface that DOES exist and is correctly used is `mise run graphify-update`'s task description, which is what `mise tasks`/`mise run --help` shows the operator; it currently advertises a capability the implementation does not have.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/graphify-first.md:29-34 (stamp removed) and python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:145-177 `_receipt_problem` docstring ("An earlier version of this fix tried to restore (2) with a self-authored stamp written by ``update()``... Removed rather than kept as decoration") plus graphify.py:536-549 `update()`, whose body is a single `_run(["graphify", "update", target])` that writes no stamp. Contradicted by mise.toml:738 `description = "Rebuild the project knowledge graph and stamp the graphify version that built it"` and mise.toml:744-745 "...and records the builder version so graphify_health can catch a graph built by the wrong binary."
  - **Evidence (native):** python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:536-549 (`update()` returns `_run(["graphify", "update", target], cwd=project_root)` — no stamp write anywhere in the module; `grep -n stamp python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py` matches only the docstrings explaining the removal, never a write).
  - **Rationale:** A rule and the task it sanctions assert opposite things about the same mechanism, and the mise description is the surface an operator reads first (`mise tasks`). By this repo's own tool-currency-and-native-first rule 5, retiring a mechanism means syncing every doc that describes it in the same change; that sync missed mise.toml. Fix the description and comment to say the stamp was deliberately removed and why, so the rule stops being contradicted by its own call site.
- **`rule-graphify-first-5`** (refactor, conf 0.8, 1/3 refuted) — The `version drift` state the rule instructs you to act on ("`missing`, `stale`, `corrupt`, version drift... say the graph is unavailable and fall back to source") is decided by a hardcoded string literal duplicated out of pyproject.toml.
  - **Native:** Derive the expected version from the distribution's own declared requirement with stdlib `importlib.metadata` — the module already imports from it at graphify.py:20 (`from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version`). `importlib.metadata.requires("dotfiles-setup")` returns the pin verbatim, making pyproject.toml the single source of truth.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/graphify-first.md:7-9 and :19-21 ("`mise run graphify-query`/`graphify-update` resolve **this repo's pinned version** (`python/pyproject.toml`), which is what `graphify_health`'s `version drift` check compares against"); the check is python/src/dotfiles_setup/graphify.py:235-236 `if runtime != "0.9.53": return HealthResult(GraphifyStatus.VERSION_DRIFT, runtime, "expected 0.9.53")` — a literal, not a read of the pin.
  - **Evidence (native):** Live probe (this repo's own venv): `uv run --project python python -c "from importlib.metadata import requires; print([r for r in requires('dotfiles-setup') if 'graphify' in r])"` -> `['graphifyy[all]==0.9.53']`, matching python/pyproject.toml:9 exactly. Existing native usage in the same file: graphify.py:81-83 `_runtime_version()` already calls `version("graphifyy")`.
  - **Rationale:** The literal makes finding 1's remediation actively unsafe: bumping python/pyproject.toml to 0.9.56 to re-align with the user-global pin would leave graphify.py comparing against `"0.9.53"`, so `graphify_health` would report VERSION_DRIFT on the CORRECT version and the rule would then instruct every session to declare the graph unavailable and fall back to source. Reading the pin from package metadata removes the duplicate and is stdlib, already imported. No native harness feature is at stake here, but the fix is a native-library one rather than more custom code.

### `rule-local-devcontainer-first`

**Motivating defect:** Pushing to 'see if CI catches it' when a CI base rebuild costs ~2.5h and the local probe is under a minute — and #288, where the same apt pin failed in the devcontainer and passed in a clean base container, because the devcontainer already had a newer package.

- **`rule-local-devcontainer-first-2`** (refactor, conf 0.72, 1/3 refuted) — The hand-maintained "Existing local tiers — use them, don't reinvent" table (.claude/rules/local-devcontainer-first.md:34-42), a five-row transcription of mise task names + costs kept in sync by hand.
  - **Native:** mise's own task registry as the source of truth instead of a transcribed table: `mise tasks ls --json` (and the `description` field each task already carries) enumerates every local tier with its description, so the rule can point at the registry rather than restate a subset that silently drifts.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/local-devcontainer-first.md:36-42 lists exactly verify-apt-pins, verify-container-latest, verify-local, renovate-dryrun, apt-repo. All five resolve (mise.toml:806, 941, 1048, 844, 679 — control arm: `[tasks.lint]` at mise.toml:207 found by the same grep shape). But two local tiers that answer precisely the rule's step-2 question are ABSENT from the table: `mise run verify-image` (mise.toml:375-397 — a throwaway `docker run --rm --pull=never` spot-check of cookbook paths/toolchains inside `:dev`, i.e. the exact 'ephemeral probe container' pattern the rule prescribes at :52-54) and `mise run smoke` (mise.toml:399 — tier 1-3 checks in the running devcontainer, the mechanism behind the table's own verify-container-latest row).
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/mise/docs/cli/tasks/ls.md:2 (`mise tasks ls`), :18 (`-J --json` — Output in JSON format), :28 (sort/display by `description`); the descriptions that would be surfaced already exist, e.g. mise.toml:807 and mise.toml:376.
  - **Rationale:** The table's content is correct but incomplete, and incompleteness is the failure mode that matters here: a reader told 'use them, don't reinvent' who does not see `verify-image` will hand-roll exactly the `docker run --rm` the table was meant to prevent. Keep the two rows whose COST and CAVEAT are judgement (verify-apt-pins ~60s vs a base rebuild; verify-local ~20min), and replace the enumeration with a pointer to `mise tasks ls` plus the task descriptions, which cannot drift out of date.
- **`rule-local-devcontainer-first-3`** (refactor, conf 0.63, 0/3 refuted) — The four-step gate at .claude/rules/local-devcontainer-first.md:19-29 is a manual habit for every image build input EXCEPT apt pins: name the failure mode, pick the container, run both arms, then push. Only the apt-pin tier has an automated trigger; for `.devcontainer/Dockerfile`, `docker-bake.hcl`, `mise-runtime.toml` and `mise-system.toml` there is no edit-time or push-time layer at all — ship deliberately SKIPS container validation for base-image inputs and defers to CI.
  - **Native:** The `FileChanged` hook event (new since this rule was written), which fires on a filesystem watcher regardless of what wrote the file — an Edit/Write, a Bash command, or a process outside Claude Code — combined with the `watchPaths` output field (returnable from SessionStart/CwdChanged) to arm absolute paths like `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` and `docker-bake.hcl` that a working-directory-literal matcher cannot name.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/local-devcontainer-first.md:19-29 (the prose gate); python/src/dotfiles_setup/pr.py:363-366 — `if changes_apt_pin_inputs(paths): gates.append(Gate("verify-apt-pins", ...))` followed by `if touches_surface(paths) and not changes_base_image_inputs(paths):`, i.e. base-image inputs get NO local container gate; .claude/settings.json wires only PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, SessionEnd, InstructionsLoaded — no file-change-triggered hook exists in this repo.
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/hooks.md:60 ("`FileChanged` | When a watched file changes on disk. The `matcher` field specifies which filenames to watch"); :2787-2793 (fires "no matter what changed the file"; matcher segments are registered as literal filenames in the working directory); :2828 (`watchPaths` for files you cannot name up front, seeded from SessionStart/CwdChanged); :1153 (`watchPaths` — "Array of absolute paths to watch for FileChanged events"); :1544 ("Unlike PreToolUse, Claude Code runs FileChanged hooks after the change, and they have no decision control, so they can't block the write"); :876 and :1025 (FileChanged: no decision control, stderr shown to user only). Control arm on the corpus: a known-absent token in the same file returns 0.
  - **Rationale:** Native covers PART of the gate, and precisely the part the repo lacks. `FileChanged` is an at-the-moment-of-edit trigger that no glob-scoped rule or ship-time gate provides, and by the corpus it cannot block (no decision control), which makes it the right shape for this rule: a nudge naming the cheapest probe for the file just touched ('you edited .devcontainer/Dockerfile — the cheapest arm is `mise run verify-image` / `mise run verify-apt-pins`'), not a new deny. The blocking half stays where it already is (ship's gate matrix, pr.py:363). Do NOT extend the PreToolUse guard to deny pushes for this: the rule itself concedes at :61-66 that base-image inputs cannot be validated locally, so a deny would redirect to nothing — the outage shape mise-tasks-only.md warns about.

### `rule-long-running-command-hangs`

**Motivating defect:** Session 2026-06-29: `hk run pre-commit --all` hung at 0% CPU for ~7 hours (hk has no native timeout), and because it was launched as `hk ... 2>&1 | tail -40` the pipeline reported exit 0 when it was finally killed. Two traps in one incident.

- **`rule-long-running-command-hangs-1`** (refactor, conf 0.88, 1/3 refuted) — Rule 2 prescribes a hand-rolled in-turn polling loop as THE way to watch a long local command: `deadline=$((SECONDS+540)); while [ $SECONDS -lt $deadline ]; do grep -q RC "$LOG" && break; sleep 15; done`. The rule never mentions the Monitor tool.
  - **Native:** The built-in Monitor tool: runs a command in the background and feeds each output line back to Claude mid-conversation, explicitly for "Tail a log file and flag errors as they appear", "Poll a PR or CI job and report when its status changes" and "Track output from any long-running script you point it at", with "You keep working in the same session and Claude interjects when an event arrives." It also inherits the Bash permission rules, so this repo's existing Bash allow/deny surface still applies. Secondarily, the Bash tool's own `run_in_background` re-invokes the session when the command exits, so no loop is needed to notice completion.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/long-running-command-hangs.md:37-43 ("What works is **in-turn polling** — background the command, then keep the turn engaged reading its log" + the bash while/sleep loop); .claude/rules/long-running-command-hangs.md:54-59 (the log path the loop is told to poll)
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:39 (Monitor in the tool table); :310-324 (Monitor tool section, the four bullets above, "Claude interjects when an event arrives", and "it uses the same permission rules as Bash"); :173-175 (`run_in_background: true`, `/tasks`). The host's own Bash tool contract at 2.1.266 states "Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition", and the docs corroborate the mechanism: /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:179-181 — "Claude Code never auto-backgrounds three kinds of command. It stops them at the timeout instead: * A command that starts with `sleep`."
  - **Rationale:** The rule's prescribed mechanism is now both superseded and partly hostile: Monitor does exactly what the loop does (background + line-by-line callback + no turn-blocking), and a foreground `sleep`-driven wait is the one shape the harness refuses to auto-background. Rule 2 should keep its EXCEPTION (Mac-side container ops must not go idle) but name Monitor as the mechanism, demoting the bash loop to a non-Claude-Code fallback (a human terminal, CI).

MUST be run with a hard time bound", justified by a `hk` invocation that "hung at 0% CPU ... for ~7 hours" because nothing bounded it. The rule presents the out-of-process wrapper in `lint.py` as the only thing standing between an agent and an unbounded wait.
  - **Native:** Every Bash tool call already runs under a harness-enforced timeout the model cannot exceed — `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (2 min out of the box when Claude passes none) and `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 min ceiling) — and on expiry Claude Code moves the command to the background rather than blocking the turn. An unbounded blind foreground wait is therefore unreachable through the Bash tool at 2.1.266.
  - **Evidence (custom):** .claude/rules/long-running-command-hangs.md:3-14 (headline + the 7-hour incident); :22-29 (rule 1, the wrapper as the bound)
  - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:153-158 ("Each command runs under a timeout, and Claude manages it"; `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`; `BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS`); :177 ("When a command reaches its timeout without finishing, Claude Code moves it to the background instead of stopping it"); /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/env-vars.md:185,187

But the rule currently reads as if nothing bounds an agent's command, which is false at this host version and leads agents to over-engineer bounds the harness already supplies. Rule 1 should state the harness bound, then say precisely what it does not do (no process-group kill, no diagnostics, no coverage outside a Bash tool call) as the justification for keeping `lint.py`.

  - **Native:** The lifetime rule is now documented and CONDITIONAL, and the documented condition contradicts the blanket form: a background command started by a FOREGROUND SUBAGENT ends at that subagent's final response, while "Commands started by the main conversation or by a background subagent keep running." A third case is headless `-p`, where background tasks end shortly after the run's final result.

In non-interactive mode with the `-p` flag, background tasks end shortly after the run's final result."; :177 (a timed-out command moved to the background inherits "the same lifetime rules")
  - **Rationale:** As written the rule attributes the reaping to 'the turn going idle', which is not the documented predicate — the predicate is WHO started the command. A main-conversation `mise run ship` in the background is documented to survive; a subagent-launched one is not. Rewriting the exception in the harness's own terms makes it actionable (launch long Mac-side work from the main conversation, never from a foreground subagent) instead of a blanket prohibition. Confidence is short of 0.9 because the rule records a real observed reaping whose launch context it does not state, so the observation may be the foreground-subagent case rather than a doc contradiction.
- **`rule-long-running-command-hangs-6`** (refactor, conf 0.7, 1/3 refuted) — Rule 3's blanket prohibition on `cmd 2>&1 | tail -N`, whose stated motivation is capture ('to capture'), and whose replacement is a manual redirect-to-file.
  - **Native:** Claude Code already streams every Bash command's output to a working file and hands Claude the file path plus a preview once a valid result passes ~30,000 characters, with `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` raising the read-back window to a hard ceiling of 150,000; 2.1.261 added the `bashOutputMaxChars` and `taskOutputMaxChars` settings raising inline command/background-task output up to 128K characters, and 2.1.265 added a 1 GB cap on tool results saved to disk with the preview noting truncation.   - **Evidence (native):** /Users/rmanaloto/dev/github/ray-manaloto/knowledge-base/sources/agent-harness-docs/docs/claude-code/tools-reference.md:160-171 ("Claude Code streams a command's output to a working file as the command runs"; the valid/failure inline table; `BASH_MAX_OUTPUT_LENGTH` 30,000 default, 150,000 ceiling); .agent/kb/raw/claude-code-changelog-2.1.258-2.1.266.digest.md — `bashOutputMaxChars`/`taskOutputMaxChars` (2.1.261) and the 1 GB tool-result cap (2.1.265)
